News.title: Paris Jackson says she and her brothers are still waiting on family trust money 17 years after their father’s death
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Paris Jackson is asking her late father Michael Jackson’s estate to transfer $600 million to a family trust, claiming she and her two brothers have gone without the money for more than 17 years.

In a court filing dated October 29, Paris said that the late singer’s estate has brought in billions of dollars since his death in 2009. However, the Michael Jackson Family Trust — which was set up to provide benefits to Paris, 28, and brothers Prince, 29, and Bigi, 24, after their father’s death — has remained empty.

The trust was supposed to distribute income for the siblings starting when they turned 21. According to the filing, the terms said the three siblings were supposed to receive money held for them when they turned 30, as well as 35 and 40, according to the filing reviewed by The Independent.

Paris alleges in the new court documents, which were filed in Los Angeles County Superior Court, that executor John Branca and his late co-executor John McClain instead paid her and her siblings smaller amounts.

“What is clear is that, as more and more cash became available, the Michael Jackson Children’s Trust remained wholly unfunded,” the petition for preliminary distribution said. “More than seventeen years after his passing, Michael Jackson’s family trust remains unfunded.”

open image in gallery Paris Jackson is asking Michael Jackson's estate to transfer $600 million into the family's trust ( Getty )

open image in gallery Michael Jackson died in 2009 ( Getty )

Paris is now asking a Los Angeles judge to order the estate to partially distribute assets to the trust.

Her attorneys argue that business deals and property sales have generated a large amount of money for the King of Pop’s estate, including the sale of Neverland Ranch for $22 million in 2020. The petition notes that the executors previously valued the estate at between $2 and $3 billion.

The Michael Jackson Estate told The Independent in a statement that it cannot fund the trusts fully until several legal issues are resolved, but added that more than $200 million has already been distributed to Paris and other beneficiaries.

“Michael Jackson’s will is clear. None of his children receive a distribution until they are in their 30s,” the statement said. “The Estate looks forward to the time when all issues are resolved so that their trusts can be fully funded as Michael wanted.”

In response, a spokesperson for Paris Jackson said in a statement: “The Estate is once again deflecting from its own incompetence. Paris called for the trust to be partially funded, something Mr. Branca had the ability and obligation to do long ago. After years of delay, Paris had no choice but to step in herself.”

open image in gallery Prince Jackson, Paris Jackson and Bigi Jackson are the beneficiaries of Michael Jackson's trust ( Getty )

The dispute is the latest development in Paris’ battle against her father’s estate over how his money has been managed.

Since last July, she has argued that executors Branca and McClain were mishandling Jackson’s money after she reportedly noticed irregular payments. She went on to accuse the attorneys of “skimming money” from her father’s estate. In April, she accused the executors of her father’s estate of using his money to publicly insult her.

Most recently, Paris asked courts to cut payments that Branca is allegedly awarding himself.

“Enough of the smoke and mirrors — Paris is asking to reduce the management fee. Executor Branca has repeatedly failed to meet deadlines ordered by the judge that are in place to provide Paris and her siblings visibility about how the Estate is being run,” a representative for Paris Jackson told The Independent.

Branca and McClain have denied all allegations against them.

News.title: Alec Baldwin declares US midterms beginning of end for America’s ‘nightmare’
News.content:
Alec Baldwin has hailed Tuesday's midterms as the "beginning of the end" of a "nightmare" he says America has been living in.

Voters have begun to cast their ballots and decide which party controls Congress in a contest that is being widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump's second term/

In an Instagram video on Monday, the 68-year-old actor said he hoped his followers would be voting and described the midterms as "the beginning of the end of [a] nightmare."

"We go and make our first step in the direction we think this country should go in, which is to really be more sane," he added.

News.title: Richard Osman sends foul-mouthed message to ‘pathetic’ critics of Celebrity Traitors winners
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Richard Osman didn’t pull any punches when it came to those criticising the Celebrity Traitors winners’ choice of charity, with the TV presenter branding the commentators “pathetic idiots” who should “f*** off”.

The 2026 series of Celebrity Traitors came to an end on Friday, with Faithful contestants Romesh Ranganathan and Sebastian Croft winning and splitting the £83,000 prize pot between their respective charities: the Refugee Council and Choose Love.

While many applauded their choice of charities, which both work with refugees, parts of the right-wing media criticised the decision – claiming that it was proof that the BBC are biased.

Addressing the backlash on the latest episode of their podcast The Rest is Entertainment, Osman and Marina Hyde singled out “sections of the broadcast media and a couple of Tory MPs” who thought the prize pot “shouldn’t be coming from the licence fee”.

open image in gallery Romesh Ranganathan and actor Sebastian Croft won the 2026 series of ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ ( BBC/Studio Lambert )

“It turns out a lot of those people are idiots or it’s possible that they’re very clever and they have an agenda,” Osman said. “It’s definitely one or the other because they ain’t right.”

Talking about baseless claims that the BBC fixed the competition so that two refugee charities would receive the prize money, Osman said: “You know what? I’m done with it. It’s genuinely so pathetic. Fifteen million people watched that. Let’s say a thousand people are being twats about it. That’s like being in a Championship football game where 15,000 people are watching, 14,999 people are cheering and there’s just one idiot who’s not happy.”

He continued sarcastically: “I’m really sorry that two people who wanted to give money to refugees won this show. But that’s the world that you are living in. Different people think different things to you.

“Stop wetting your pants about everything. Stop saying, ‘Well it all comes out of licence fee money.’ You cannot be that stupid. You cannot be that stupid to not know thatTraitors makes a fortune for the BBC.

“The fact that you have to get column inches and clickbait out of just co-opting this thing. Stop co-opting other people’s work. Stop co-opting the fact that other people have done extraordinary things and made something and made a series of correct decisions about what people want and done it brilliantly.”

“I mean f*** off, you know? Really, f*** off. It’s pathetic,” he added.

open image in gallery Richard Osman on 'The Rest is Entertainment' ( The Rest is Entertainment )

It marks a change for the broadcaster and TV producer, who is known for being somewhat less vocal with his opinions on his podcast, The Rest is Entertainment, than his co-host Marina Hyde.

Responding to Osman’s comments, Hyde said: “I am so pleased to find you off your fence this Monday morning.”

The Independent has contacted the BBC for comment.

On Friday night, Ranganathan and Croft were declared the winners of the 2026 series, having banished Maya Jama and King Kenny (who were Traitors) and Leigh-Anne Pinnock and James Blunt (who were Faithful).

Despite not winning the show, Jama matched the prize pot with a donation to her chosen charity, Action for Children.

Croft’s charity Choose Love said it was “absolutely thrilled” and “deeply grateful” to receive his share of the prize money and that it would “quite literally change and save lives”.

The final attracted a record audience for the show, with 11.2 million people tuning in to watch the pair win.

News.title: Pilot in Learjet crash that killed 9 in Florida was a husband, father and a devout Christian
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The pilot of a business jet that crashed in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, was a longtime aviator, husband and father from the Philadelphia suburbs, according to a colleague who organized an online fundraiser for his family and social media posts from people who knew him.

Jeff Gregory, 55, was one of two crew members in the cockpit of the Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 as it encountered bad weather and slammed into the ground Sunday afternoon in Greenacres, about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.

As the plane plunged, a man’s voice could be heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer in the background of the copilot’s final radio transmissions to air traffic control. Friends are convinced it was Gregory, a devout Christian.

A federal investigator said Monday that parts of the jet likely started to break off before it struck the ground. Gregory’s co-pilot, 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, told air traffic controllers that ice was accumulating on the plane and that severe turbulence had thrown it up and down by more than 700 feet (210 meters).

“We’re going to die!” she said with a scream before the jet slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball.

Thomas Noetzel, the director of operations at the company that operated the flight, Upper Jets, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory’s wife and children.

Gregory was a close, personal friend and “knowing him has made me a better person," Noetzel wrote on the fundraising website GoFundMe.

“Jeff was a devoted, conscientious, and deeply faithful man who had a genuine passion for flying and a strong love for the Lord​,” Noetzel’s father, Walter, posted on Facebook. “His journey on earth may have ended, but I like to think he is now flying among the angels, soaring peacefully in the presence of our Lord.”

Gregory held airline transport pilot and flight instructor certificates, according to Federal Aviation Administration records. He lived in Gilbertsville, about 35 miles (56 kilometers) northwest of Philadelphia, and had previously worked for a charter company based in Allentown, Pennsylvania.

“We are deeply saddened to learn that Captain Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives,” said April Honnen, the director of charter sales for East Coast Jets, Inc., where he worked in 2016 and 2017. “Our prayers go out to Jeff’s family, his fellow crew member, the passengers and everyone affected by this heart breaking tragedy.”

The Learjet hit the ground with enough force to create a crater before bursting into flames. The impact scattered plane fragments over a large area.

Images of the moment just before the aircraft made impact appear to show the horizontal stabilizer missing from the tail of the plane.

All nine people aboard the plane that was flying from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas died. The victims included technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two young children, relatives said.

About 600 nearby residents remain displaced, but only one injury was reported on the ground.

Tom Chapman, a National Transportation Safety Board member, said Monday that weather would be a key focus of the investigation. A preliminary report describing what happened will be released in about a month, but it will likely take more than a year to determine the cause of the crash.

News.title: King Charles brands UK slave trade ‘monstrous’ - but stops short of offering apology
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The King has said the slave trade “fills my heart with horror” – but stopped short of offering an apology – in a speech to Commonwealth leaders as the UK faces mounting demands to pay reparations for its role in the slave trade.

King Charles told a summit in the Caribbean: “The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth.

“As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.”

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Earlier this week prime minister Andy Burnham signalled that he was “open” to a formal apology for Britain’s role in the transatlantic slave trade and approved £40m in aid funding for the Caribbean amid calls for the UK to pay reparations.

But former Archbishop of Canterbury Justin Welby has warned that forcing millions of ordinary Britons to fund huge sums in slavery reparations would be a “moral evil”.

Writing for The Independent, he argued it would be a “vast fine on the entire British people for a crime they did not commit”.

“The vast majority of Britons have no connection to slavers’ profits – and nor did their ancestors,” he wrote.

“What about those sailors of the Royal Navy who died liberating the slaves, or the UK parliamentarians who spent their lives campaigning for the abolition of slavery and its trade? Should their descendants be treated differently?”

He added: “To do even the right thing in the wrong way makes for more evil. It is right to act differently, wrong to act foolishly.

“Investment in new technologies and solving current existential dangers in partnership will build more wealth than a futile and unjust payment of fake ‘reparations’ ever could.”

As the King delivered his keynote speech to presidents and prime ministers on Tuesday, he described his “growing commitment” to finding ways to work in “modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future”.

He said: “And yet history also teaches us that evil need not have the last word; that character and courage can combine to overcome the most monstrous injustice, as they did with the determination to end international trade in enslaved people, in which the Royal Navy played such a leading role.

“The more I have furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking, the more committed I have become to finding ways for us to work in modern partnership to address the wrongs of the past with action for the future.

“Through improving access to education, investing in jobs and opportunities, encouraging intra-Commonwealth trade, and inspiring vital climate resilience measures across the world, I have always felt that there is so much that can be done to help lift up those who struggle against hardship and disadvantage.”

At the perimeter of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) area was a small protest, where activists held placards that read “You say you regret so apologise”, and “Apologise for the greatest crime against humanity and let’s have reparatory justice”.

The funding announced by Mr Burnham will be given over three years to speed up critical infrastructure investment, including green energy schemes in the Caribbean, according to Downing Street.

The prime minister is expected to begin discussions with Caribbean leaders about the prospect of offering a formal apology for the UK’s role in selling enslaved people for profit. But he has ruled out offering direct financial reparations.

open image in gallery ( PA )

King Charles said in his speech: “History can be hard to compass, viewed as it is through the prism of time, which can be both clarifying and distorting, and yet its consequences resonate with contemporary force.

“Our history inspires us, can appal us, yet it can always teach us. We cannot change the actions of those who came before us. We can, however, learn from the past.”

Britain’s royal family has a long association with the transportation and selling of enslaved people for profit.

Elizabeth I backed the lucrative dealings of John Hawkins, one of Britain’s first slave traders, and Charles II encouraged the expansion of the enterprise.

The Duke of Clarence, George III’s son, later to become William IV, opposed the campaigns of slavery abolitionists.

The King also said: “All around us, trust between nations is under critical strain, as international norms and systems are tested to their limits.

“Brutal conflict stalks our world, destroying lives and casting long shadows across the globe. Technology is transforming our societies and our economies at dizzying speed, with little certainty about where it might lead us.”

The King also addressed the “catastrophic reality” of climate change, saying: “Each of these is a challenge of the highest order. Together, they comprise the crisis of our time.”

News.title: European supermarket fridges got hacked. Again. Here's what to know
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Mysterious cyberattacks on European supermarket fridges have sent officials around the continent scrambling to figure out the cold, hard facts.

Supermarkets in a number of European countries reported this week that their fridges and freezers warmed up after they were remotely taken over, resulting in tons of spoiled food at a total cost of millions of dollars (euros).

One Swedish supermarket said its fridges and freezers had been hacked and set to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit).

It's a repeat of an earlier incident that struck refrigeration systems in hundreds of supermarkets and independent stores across France, Belgium and the Netherlands.

Here's a closer look:

What happened and who was affected

Supermarkets in at least half a dozen European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, Italy and Estonia, reported problems on Monday.

It wasn't just big chains.

The owner of a butcher shop in Athens told private Greek Skai TV Tuesday that someone hacked into the temperature control of a refrigeration unit, raising the temperature to 150 degrees Celsius (302 Fahrenheit).

George Boubas said his employees who start their shift at 4 a.m. at the shop in the Kifisia suburb first noticed the problem. It took a technician two hours to wrest back control of the unit’s temperature settings, although the meat products weren’t affected, he said.

Boubas said the technician told him that an area supermarket and a fast-food restaurant experienced the same issue.

He said they resorted to switching off the Wi-Fi connection to the refrigeration units to restrict outside access.

Experts said the cyberattacks were a reminder of the risks that come as more things get connected to the internet.

“This attack is a wake-up call. We have filled our homes and shops with devices that are really small computers, yet we still treat them like ordinary appliances," said Katerina Mitrokotsa, a cybersecurity professor at the University of St. Gallen, in Switzerland.

“A fridge doesn’t look like a security risk, and that’s exactly why attackers like it.”

Fridges are connected to save money and cut waste

The cyberattack mirrors one that happened weeks earlier that affected mainly French and Dutch retailers.

French cybersecurity investigators blamed problems with outdated remote control modules made by Danish company Danfoss as well as U.S.-based Copeland. Danfoss said most affected systems were older products that no longer received software or security updates, while Copeland identified a vulnerability in discontinued controllers.

“Supermarkets connect their fridges so they can monitor temperatures around the clock across hundreds of stores, get alerts before food spoils, cut energy costs and let technicians fix faults remotely," Mitrokotsa said.

"This saves money and reduces food waste, but every connected fridge is also an entry point that needs to be secured like any other IT system.”

Experts said many businesses are rushing to embrace trendy new technology while neglecting the vast network of connections that they rely on for their daily operations, from payment and ordering systems to warehouses, refrigeration and other building controls.

“Organizations are pouring budget into AI and digital transformation while the systems that keep food cold, water clean, and lights on often run on hardware that has not been funded since installation," said Nicole Carignan, senior vice president of security and AI strategy at cybersecurity company Darktrace.

“Nobody broke into these refrigeration systems with a zero-day," she said, using a term for a flaw that has gone undetected by the system’s creators and security reviews. "They got in through internet-facing controllers, end-of-life firmware, and default passwords. That is technical debt coming due.”

British cybersecurity officials on Tuesday shed little light on the latest attack, while pointing to what they called “legacy technology.”

“The cyberattack on French supermarkets was a result of exploitation of known vulnerabilities,” U.K. cyber minister Liz Lloyd said in a speech. “It’s a clear demonstration that poor cyber hygiene, like weak passwords, continues to put organizations at risk.”

Richard Horne, the head of the U.K.’s National Cyber Security Center, told reporters the French fridges were "connected directly to the internet with default passwords.”

A team from the center issued warnings and worked through Monday night contacting organizations that had “vulnerable technology exposed,” he said.

No evidence so far that AI was involved

Advanced artificial intelligence systems from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI have come under fire recently after a string of revelations that they hacked into organizations while evading human control.

Experts, however, said Tuesday that they didn't think these attacks were powered by AI.

“There is no evidence AI was used, and the techniques did not require it,” said Carignan.

“I think the key element of that is that this wasn’t an AI attack” said Paul Chichester, director of operations at the U.K. cyber center. “This is using vulnerabilities that absolutely have been out there for a long period of time. And that’s where we really need to sort of focus on.”

Who’s behind it and what's the motive

Investigations have so far failed to discover who might have carried out the cyberattacks and why.

France’s national cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, said it has been investigating refrigeration-system breaches since mid-October and coordinating protective measures with “all sectors that could be affected.”

In a statement to The Associated Press, the agency said it knew of compromised remote refrigeration controllers in Danfoss’s AK-SM and AK-SC ranges, as well as Copeland and Dixell xweb systems.

ANSSI said it was mobilized to assist “potential victims in France” and pointed to a security alert first published Oct. 12, which has been updated regularly.

Italian cybersecurity and intelligence officials were scheduled to meet Tuesday morning to discuss the incident, according to Italian news agency ANSA.

Officials at the European Union's executive Commission were also holding similar meetings.

European Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier declined on Tuesday to comment on who might have carried out the hacks, saying that's up to the bloc's 27 national authorities to figure out.

Regnier told reporters the incidents “are not isolated” and that Europeans "have to be collectively resilient and prepared for such cyber incidents.”

___

Hadjicostis reported from Nicosia, Cyprus. AP writers Lorne Cook in Brussels, Lefteris Pitarakis in Athens and Thomas Adamson in Paris contributed to this report.

News.title: Gabonese TikTokers fight back against toxic skin lightening products
News.content:
There is a buzz among the pupils at Nzeng-Ayong 2 primary school in Libreville, the capital of Gabon. At least among those who use TikTok. Black Choco is here: social media personality, entrepreneur, and a bona fide celebrity. With the fervour of a revivalist preacher, she takes over the lesson. Today’s topic is kwandza, the Gabonese term for skin-lightening.

“Is kwandza good? No! It’s like pouring boiling water on your skin. And we don’t do that, do we?”

Why do people want to become white, she asks the pupils – boys and girls between eight and 12 – before answering the question herself.

“To please other people! Aren’t you proud of your skin? Our skin is our identity!”

She asks a handful of pupils to stand up. “Look at them! Aren’t they beautiful with their dark skin? Let them hear it!”

“Gloire, you are beautiful,” the whole class chants.

News.title: Newcastle fans turn on Jaissle as defeat triggers relegation concerns
News.content:
Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

News.title: US dairy worker dies from bird flu as outbreak rages in cattle
News.content:
“People at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. Transmission of avian influenza between humans is extremely rare and has never been documented in the United States. Public health officials are continuing to monitor individuals who had close contact with the patient for symptoms,” the health district said in a statement.

Experts say the US bird flu outbreak is not only costing the dairy industry millions of dollars but also raises the risk that the virus could mutate to spread more easily between mammals. They are also concerned that authorities are doing little to check the spread.

Marc Johnson, a virologist at the University of Missouri, told the Telegraph last week that the outbreak in dairy cattle was “completely preventable”.

“Cattle infections last only a few weeks before the animals recover. If infected herds were simply isolated until the outbreak fizzled out, it would stop.

“But cattle keep being moved around, spreading it into new states,” said Dr Johnson, referring to the way the US dairy industry operates, in which cows are routinely transported across state lines, whether to join new herds, for breeding, or to replace animals at large milk-producing operations.

A bird flu outbreak has also been raging on a mink farm in Utah for the last couple of months, according to news outlet ProPublica.

Jonathan Ball, professor of molecular virology at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, said allowing a virus to rage unchecked raises the risk of it mutating.

“Viruses like influenza are constantly exploring new hosts, and more often than not, it burns out. It’s not quite got the right combination of genetic changes to allow it to efficiently infect, efficiently replicate, and then efficiently transmit to the new host. But the longer these steps - adaptive changes, so genetic changes - are happening in these sporadic outbreaks, the more likelihood you’ve got of it mutating. It’s a bit like a one-armed bandit machine - if you keep pulling that handle, eventually you’re going to get three cherries,” he said.

News.title: First ever trial of long-acting injection against malaria to launch in Africa
News.content:
Dr Cristina Donini, executive vice-president of research and development at MMV, said the compound would be “complementary” to existing tools, rather than replacing them.

“The vaccine is doing a fantastic job in infants but if you could add onto that another tool that can cover a broader population with a longer regimen then we would be in a very good position to eliminate the disease,” she said.

Children in malaria-endemic regions are already given prophylactic drugs during the malaria season and studies have shown that these combined with the vaccine are highly effective. However, resistance has developed to these drugs and they have to be given monthly.

The malaria season in Africa varies by region but usually peaks after periods of rainfall. If the season lasts longer than three to four months it’s likely that people would need two injections. However, Dr Donini and her colleagues are working on a second generation LAI which they hope would provide year-long coverage.

Full costs have not yet been worked out but Dr Donini said affordability was an important factor in assessing the LAI’s suitability.

“It’s too early to say whether it will be cheaper than an injection - hopefully, yes. The beauty of it is that if you simplify it and decrease the number of injections needed you decrease the cost,” she said.

LAIs are gaining traction in the fight against infectious diseases - Lenacapavir, now being rolled out after being approved in 2025, provides almost 100% protection against infection from HIV and many believe it could help end the HIV pandemic. There are also LAI candidates in development for the prevention of tuberculosis, treatment and prevention of which usually relies on daily pills being taken over many months.

Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK, welcomed the launch of the trial.

“Thanks to sustained investment in malaria science including here in the UK, we are now on the brink of a number of breakthroughs which could turn the tide on the fight against the disease. And the long-acting injectable, specifically, could be a valuable addition to this toolbox as it has the potential to provide sustained protection from a single shot, avoiding the need for repeat doses.

“This phase of the trial also builds on earlier research conducted in the UK, highlighting the importance of the UK’s ongoing role as a malaria science superpower and the value of continued investment in malaria R&D. We look forward to the trial progressing further and eagerly await the results.”

News.title: Tears flow for Antonelli after becoming youngest champion in F1 history
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

Sports.title: West Ham-bound Scott Parker learned grit from 3am lorry runs with dad & being bullied at school over McDonald’s ad
Sports.content:
Next

SCOTT PARKER is set to take the reigns at West Ham following Nuno Espirito Santo’s sacking.

The former Fulham and Bournemouth boss is a free agent after leaving Burnley in April.



As a player, Parker, 46, played 129 times for the Hammers and is remembered as a modern day cult hero among the fanbase.

Many of those supporters can relate to the ex-England international’s work ethic that was borne out of his working class roots.



Former Chelsea, Spurs and England star Parker was raised on a council estate in London by a delivery driver dad and special needs teacher mum.

He found early fame aged 13, when he appeared in an advert for McDonald’s before finding his feet at Charlton Athletic.



Away from the pitch, Parker met his wife Carly Arter when he was 16, and married her when he was 20.

SunSport takes a look at Parker’s formative years that have made him grounded, disciplined – and the man that could lead the Irons back to the Premier League.

Family ties

Parker was born in Lambeth in 1980 and grew up on the Lettsom Estate in Camberwell, South East London.

His father, Michael, worked as a Heinz delivery driver and would take his son on lorry runs at 3am, including trips along the Kent coast.



Recalling that time in his life, Parker told SunSport: “As a kid every day I was on at my dad to take me out on the lorries.

“Twice a week he’d take me out of school — probably not the right thing to do — but we’d get up at 3am and pick up the lorry.

“Thursdays were the best because he’d have coast runs — Ramsgate, Margate — then he’d take me to the amusements after.



“For a young kid, those days were fantastic. Great memories.”

Early stardom

In the ’90s, Parker found himself flitting between helping his dad out on his lorry to attending Haberdashers’ Aske’s Hatcham College in New Cross and navigating a promising footballer career.

He was part of Charlton’s youth set-up when national fame at the age of 13 came calling.

Parker appeared in a McDonald’s advert doing keepie-uppies in a commericial that landed ahead of the 1994 World Cup.

He played a character called Jimmy who snubs an invite to the fast-food chain and instead keeps juggling his football.



Speaking about how that came about, Parker told the Daily Echo: “I was a 13-year-old little boy for the USA World Cup in 1994.

“McDonald’s, or an  company, rang up Charlton to ask if they had a young boy to do some kick-ups. Charlton put me forward.

“I went to audition in Pineapple Studios in Covent Garden.



“At the back of a queue full of young boys that had been to acting school, mums were doing all their hair and that, and I was a scruffy boy at the back of the queue with my ball in my hand.

“I take it those boys weren’t football – they were more actors. I just went in, did some kick-ups and got the role.

“I was known as the McDonald’s boy for large parts, that was definitely me.”

But, it had its drawbacks…

Unfortunately for Parker, he was bullied by his peers at school for his star role.

“It was mixed (reaction) to be honest with you. It was horrendous and it was also very good.



“It was horrendous because I was at an age where I went to an all-boys school in the middle of New Cross in South East London, do you know what I mean?

“In the advert I was the kid called Jimmy. As you can imagine, there were elements which were tough because you get the mick taken out of you every day and it turned into that, really.

“But then on the flip side, it was a brilliant experience. There was a bit of a balance really, but all part and parcel of growing up.”



Family life

Parker was 16, and on the cusp of the Charlton first team, when he met his wife, Carly Arter.

They dated for four years, before marrying when they were just 20 years old.

While she has been photographed at matches sporadically, and featured in paparazzi pictures on holiday, Carly has opted to stay out of the public glare.

Speaking about family life, Parker said back in 2021: “I have four sons and when I am going to get older, I want to create memories for them that we can reminisce a little bit and they can enjoy what I do.

“I am fortunate enough, as stressful as it is at times, and as much as I’m wary of that for these young boys – that I don’t want to put them into the situation that they are forced into sometimes, because what their dad does at work.



“There is also an element where they are fortunate enough, that they can also enjoy what I do. So that’s nice.”

Carly’s younger brother, Harry Arter was just six when she started dating Parker.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Parker would later become a close mentor and role model for Arter, as he became a professional footballer himself.



The pair would later work together at Fulham, where Parker was coach and Arter was player.

Sports.title: How Jude Bellingham became football’s latest It boy from Calvin Klein ads to glamorous girlfriend and luxury mansions
Sports.content:
Next

JUDE BELLINGHAM may just well be football’s latest ‘it boy’.

The internet went into meltdown after the England star dropped his Calvin Klein campaign on Monday.



But one photoshoot does not hand over the keys to the it boy kingdom, where David Beckham still sits on the throne beside Victoria.

At just 23, Bellingham has football, fashion deals, and a famous girlfriend.



But there is a long way to go before he masters the reinvention of masculinity and style like Posh and Becks.

The carefully selected bunch of lads have to tick the boxes of a young man who has captured the attention of the masses with charisma, style, sex appeal – and undeniable cultural presence.

In the Calvins video, Bellingham muttered “icons are forever” as he throws his shirt into the camera lens.

Quite the claim – although judging by the comments, nobody was listening to the dialogue.

SunSport presents the unofficial guide to Bellingham’s it boy status…

MEET THE BELLINGHAMS

From the Kardashians to the Beckhams, to tellies showing Succession and Dynasty, every star needs an ensemble to back them up.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

On Saturday, dad Mark scored SEVEN goals for England Over-50s in Saturday’s 13-1 win over Republic of Ireland Veterans.

Younger brother Jobe also put on a stunning show for Borussia Dortmund in their 2-2 clash against Bayern Munich.



And mum Denise is never too far away, given her moves from Birmingham to Dortmund, then Madrid.

But for all the designer campaigns, the tight-knit family picture keeps enough of the boy-next-door appeal intact.

Model girlfriend Ashlyn Castro adds another dose of glamour.



She’s been spotted in the family box but appearances on each other’s social media are rare enough to get people talking – without satisfying the nosy ones.

FASHION FIRST

Bellingham’s latest Calvin Klein campaign had some fans briefly forgetting their own relationship status.

One Instagram user commented under his post: “I’m married, I’m married, I’m married.”

Another said: “Lots of boyfriends became single today.”



Someone else joked: “Jude bro my girlfriend is on this app.”

Bellingham stripped off in 2024 as he announced himself as the new face of SKIMS, and the couture suitors keep coming…



That year, he also signed a stunning deal to become a Louis Vuitton ambassador, and when he does put some clothes on, it’s a signature Adidas line, complete with a monogram of his initials.

The star is only the second footballer ever to get his own Adidas Originals collection, after the magical Lionel Messi.

HEY JUDE

Of course, none of this works quite as well if you cannot play – but fortunately, Bellingham has the day job covered.

Standing in front of a crowd of thousands, Bellingham swaggers up before holding his arms out to take it all in.

The England fans will belt out Hey Jude down at the 20-something lad from Brum, having watched him save the Three Lions again – before their inevitable tournament defeat.



But is that enough to call it an undeniable cultural presence?



Having lifted both the Spanish and German titles, Bellingham won the Champions League – beating his former side at Wembley in 2024.

But heavy expectations and trademark celebrations can also bring out a spikier side.

At the 2026 World Cup, Bellingham gave Argentina sub Valentin Barco a slap round the back of the head for his ballsy antics.

BRUM TO THE BERNABEU

Bellingham’s No22 shirt was retired when he left Birmingham City – some laughed but the Blues knew what they were losing.



And three years later, Real Madrid came knocking and few can bring more glitz and glamour than the residents of the Bernabeu.

He has also evaded the Premier League.

Fans in England are deprived of the week-in-week-out action, so when Bellingham does feature, it creates an occasion for both parties to rise to.

And supporters can even go without remembering the winner he scored against their club last Saturday as an added bonus.



THE INNER CIRCLE

And what would an it boy be without his inner circle of high-profile mates.



Bellingham and Erling Haaland had a budding bromance from their shared Dortmund stint and survived transfer windows as best pals.

Then, Morgan Rogers grew up just five miles down the road and they played together long before the Three Lions badge came calling.

And there’s certainly no shortage of X factor in Real’s star-studded squad.



HOME SWEET HOME

Away from the pitch, Bellingham can lay claim to two stunning pads in both Spain and England.

Bellingham’s reported £5.5million Spanish six-bed mansion sits in the exclusive La Finca neighbourhood.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It features a gym, cinema and outdoor pool, gourmet kitchen and views overlooking the nearby La Finca Golf Club.

Back in the West Midlands, a reported £7m estate takes things further, showing off another five bedrooms, indoor and outdoor swimming pools, a spa, a trophy room and even a barbershop.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta shares heartfelt moment with former Arsenal team-mate as Gunners prepare for Slavia Prague clash
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA was reunited with a former team-mate and forgotten Arsenal man at London Colney on Tuesday.

Arteta, 44, took the Gunners for an important session ahead of Wednesday night’s trip to Slavia Prague in the Champions League.



And while walking out onto the training pitch, the Spaniard was seen embracing Yaya Sanogo.

There was a handshake, a hug and a quick chat between the pair, who shared the dressing room between 2013 and 2016.



Sanogo was decked out in a black and white scarf, grey trousers and a smart black jacket.

The Frenchman, 33, has not played professionally since leaving Brazilian club Amazonas last year.

He was snapped up by Arsenal in 2013 after Arsene Wenger saw him bag seven goals in a week for Auxerre.

Despite standing 6ft 3ins and playing up front, Sanogo only scored once in 20 games for the Gunners.

He also managed one in 11 matches on loan at Crystal Palace, and made nine goalless appearances in a permanent spell at Huddersfield.

Arsenal fans lapped up a clip of Sanogo and Arteta doing the rounds on social media.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

One wrote: “That ex-colleague who left years ago drops by and gets more hugs than everyone who stayed.”

Another put: “The man, the myth, the legend.”

A third added: “Once a Gooner always a Gooner.”



And a fourth commented: “What a guy. Loved him.”

Sports.title: Arsenal make tweak to training ground to remind Mikel Arteta’s squad every day that they’re Premier League champions
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL players are being reminded that they are champions every time they walk into the training ground.

The Gunners have installed a replica of the Premier League trophy on the wall at the entrance to their St Albans training ground.



The new addition has replaced a silhouette of the trophy that previously acted as a motivational tool for Mikel Arteta’s team.

Arteta had installed the silhouette to remind players what they were competing for, but after ending their 22-year wait for the league title, it has now been replaced.



The actual Premier League trophy is currently held at the Emirates Stadium, where fans can see it up close on a stadium tour.

Last season, after Arsenal sealed their league title and celebrated at the training ground, clips of Jurrien Timber and Bukayo Saka asking for the silhouette to be “lit up” circulated on social media.



Instead of using a light, the club have added a replica trophy over a silhouette of the Arsenal badge.

Next to the trophy are the words: “Together we make history.”

Arteta’s side is now looking to make more history by becoming the first Arsenal team to win consecutive Premier League titles.

No Arsenal squad has achieved the feat, despite memorable teams including the 2003/04 Invincibles and the 1997/98 and 2001/02 double winning squads.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Gunners are currently three points clear at the top of the Premier League after earning a huge three points at Anfield on Sunday.

Their 1-0 victory over Liverpool was the first time they have beaten the Reds away from home in the league for over 14 years.

Arteta will have his full focus on the Champions League for now.

Arsenal face Slavia Praha in the league phase of the competition tonight [WED] and are looking to go one step further in Europe too.



The Gunners suffered penalty shootout heartbreak in last year’s final, falling at the final hurdle to Paris Saint-Germain.

Sports.title: Barcola: People are starting to understand me better - but I'm not Mo Salah
Sports.content:
Big money signings can take time to get going at their new club. There are plenty at Liverpool who can testify to that.

As Sky Sports settles into a room at Liverpool's AXA training facility, a large window shows some of their big-money stars walking off one of the pitches after a recovery session. It's a sheer amount of attacking wealth.

Two of them are Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who arrived in deals that could reach a combined £241m. But the jury is still out on both of them. Isak has only just started delivering his highly-anticipated goal numbers, while many believe Wirtz is yet to get going on Merseyside.

This year, Bradley Barcola - who goes from the pitch to sitting in front of the Sky Sports cameras in the training facility - is the latest marquee signing, this time for £123m. But a slow start to life at Anfield brought about familiar concerns about recent buys.

After making the move, Barcola failed to get a goal or an assist in his first 10 games for club and country this season. But then came some encouraging signs.

A hat-trick in Liverpool's thumping Champions League over LASK was backed up by back-to-back assists in wins over the tricky Brighton and Brentford.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool's Bradley Barcola got his goal tally under way after scoring three goals against LASK in the Champions League

While Barcola fired a blank against Arsenal in the last match, his first half running caused the Premier League champions a lot of concerns. Isak and Wirtz didn't quite start this quickly, so is Barcola starting to deliver on that hefty cheque?

"No, I don't think I'm at my best yet," Barcola tells Sky Sports. "You still haven't seen the best version of me.

"On top of that, we're working with my team-mates so that they can make the most of my strengths.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better. And I think things are improving all the time.

"People are beginning to understand my style of play much better. I think it's going much better."

After Isak arrived as the British record transfer last year, with Wirtz also entering Liverpool as the golden boy of German football, Barcola has arrived at Liverpool under different, arguably more microscopic circumstances.

Image: Barcola is Liverpool's second-most expensive signing after Alexander Isak (left)

Barcola is the marquee attacking signing in the wake of Mohamed Salah's departure this summer. Salah graced Anfield with his world-class ability and delivered titles. Barcola arrived as a back-to-back European champion with Paris Saint-Germain.

When signings like these are made, there is expectation, which leads to pressure. But Barcola insists he is not feeling anything of the sort - neither the huge price tag, nor Salah's shadow on the club.

"First of all, I wasn't the one who decided the transfer fee," he says. "So that's not been my problem.

"And regarding Mo Salah, he's a legend here. A huge one. He's done big things here and for that I have an enormous respect for him. But it's not pressure for me at all.

Image: Barcola arrived as the marquee attacking signing after Mohamed Salah's departure

"I'm not Mohamed Salah, so I'm going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don't feel any pressure about that."

Those final words feel pertinent. Barcola has already achieved huge success in his career - delivering the piece de la resistance European trophy at PSG not once, but twice in successive years. But did he make his mark on that PSG success story compared to others?

Barcola was often used as the 'back-up guy' in Luis Enrique's set-up. The French winger was a regular in domestic football, which helped delivered league titles - but when it came to the big Champions League ties against the best of the best, he often had to settle for the bench.

Image: Barcola left PSG after winning back-to-back Champions Leagues with them

Given his competition was Ousmane Dembele, Kvicha Kvarasthkelia and Desire Doue ahead of Fabian Ruiz, Vitinha and Joao Neves, there's no shame in that. But it explained why he rejected a new contract at the club, pushed for a new challenge and eventually moved on.

"For me, it was the right time to leave PSG," he recalls. "I spent so many great years there and I won an enormous amount of trophies. But it was time.

"It was quite difficult because, over there, it was a real family. We'd built something very special together. On top of that, it was very difficult to leave and say goodbye to my team-mates. But ultimately, that's just how football is.

"When a club like Liverpool comes calling, it's a great thing. I didn't have any doubts and I just knew I had to come here. I'm happy to be here, and I hope things go well for PSG."

Barcola basically won it all at PSG last season - but at Liverpool there may need to be a bit more patience. Andoni Iraola has clearly improved the Reds off the back of Arne Slot's flawed final year, but defeats to Man City and Arsenal at Anfield have shown how far they are from the elite.

The weekend's 1-0 loss to Arsenal saw Liverpool fail to register a shot on target at home for the first time since Premier League data records began. They sit second-bottom in the Premier League this season for big chances created. If Arsenal are the level required, Liverpool have work to do.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Liverpool and Arsenal.

So do expectations need to be tempered now? "No, I don't think it has changed the goals for the season," Barcola says. "I think we should have done better in a game like this. We had the chances to score, even to win the match.

"I think we need to work on being able to control the game more and play more football. Often, when we're in a game like this, we resort to long balls. But in my opinion, we should try to keep the ball on the ground more, because we have players with the quality to do that.

"We were really disappointed after the game but we know what we have to do better at. We're not going to give up. We know that other teams will drop points. So it's down to us to remain consistent until the end of the season."

In that case, Barcola and his team-mates need to get back on that training pitch. There's work to be done.

Sports.title: Westwood has 'no regrets' about turning down Ryder Cup captaincy
Sports.content:
Lee Westwood has "no regrets" about turning down the chance to captain Team Europe at the 2023 Ryder Cup to join LIV Golf, as the former world No 1 revealed he is yet to sign with LIV 2.0.

During a wide-ranging interview on The Chipping Forecast podcast, the 53-year-old said he was currently "unemployed" and added LIV 2.0 had not presented him with "anything agreeable" for the league's proposed relaunch in 2027.

Westwood has represented Team Europe at the Ryder Cup on 11 occasions, having tied Sir Nick Faldo for the most appearances at the biennial tournament during his last outing at Whistling Straits in 2021.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Westwood last played at the Ryder Cup during Europe's defeat in 2021 at Whistling Straits

Having worked as a vice-captain under Thomas Bjørn at the 2018 Ryder Cup in France, the Englishman was one of the DP World Tour's leading candidates to be appointed captain for the tournament in Rome in 2023.

"Whistling Straights had happened and then quite shortly after that I had a conversation with [DP World Tour chief executive] Guy Kinnings, where he talked about the Ryder Cup captaincy and the captain in Italy," Westwood, who joined LIV Golf in 2022, said.

"It was put to me whether I'd like to be Ryder Cup captain, and I had started discussions with LIV. I think I asked: 'If I did go to LIV, could I still be Ryder Cup captain?'

"They didn't say no, but it was made clear that there would be very little chance of it, and I made the decision to go to LIV.

"You make calls in life, don't you?" Westwood added. "You make a choice, and I have no regrets over the choice I made."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Westwood equalled Sir Nick Faldo's record to have the joint-highest appearances for Europe at the Ryder Cup (11)

The DP World Tour dictates a player cannot be a European Ryder Cup captain or vice-captain if they decline membership to the tour or fail to fulfil their minimum event obligations.

Henrik Stenson was later named captain for 2023 before he also joined LIV Golf, with the baton ultimately being handed to Luke Donald.

Westwood, who jointly holds the record for the most appearances for Europe at a Ryder Cup, was asked whether he would consider being captain in the future.

"I don't know, I get asked that question a lot," Westwood said. "I've always just wanted to play, I love playing golf.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Multiple LIV Golfers, including Jon Rahm, Ian Poulter and Sergio Garcia, have already announced their exits from LIV Golf

"When I was vice captain, everybody has a little say in the team room, and I said to the guys: 'You better enjoy it as much as you can because when it's gone, you really miss it, and I'll tell you one thing worse than playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup is watching other people playing practice rounds in a Ryder Cup.'

"I loved being a Ryder Cup player and getting in that environment. I don't know whether I'd have been a good Ryder Cup captain, because of what I said in France. I don't know whether I would have liked watching."

Delving further, Westwood said: "I'm not good at really pushing control.

"That's one of the reasons I started playing golf, I played a lot of football and rugby and cricket before taking up golf. The reason I enjoy playing golf is because the buck stops with me.

"I didn't want to have to rely on other people and that probably goes back to a little bit of the reason why the Ryder Cup captaincy wasn't really that higher priority.

"When push came to shove, it wasn't the be-all and end-all for me. I'm not sure I wanted it enough."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player LIV Golf are hoping to relaunch in 2027 but questions remain who will play on the tour

'I haven't made a decision on anything'

LIV Golfers have a deadline of November 16 to reapply for their DP World Tour memberships, and Westwood says he is deliberating whether to do so.

Should he reapply, he would face a 10-tournament suspension for his decision to resign his DP World Tour membership.

"I haven't signed up to anything anywhere, I haven't made a decision on anything yet," Westwood said.

"I am yet to have everything put in front of me and I have not really had any dialogue with the DP World Tour.

"I know if I sign up, I've then got to serve a 10-tournament suspension. I've looked at the schedule, and I feel like the first event I could play in on the DP World Tour will be the Turkish Airlines Open, which is the first week in May, so I haven't looked any further.

"There's nothing that's been presented to me that was agreeable for LIV 2.0. There are still a lot of things that would need fine-tuning; deadlines have come and gone, and I've heard nothing on whether I have to sign or not.

"I haven't signed [for] 2.0. So, I literally am unemployed."

Sports.title: King's former horse Point Of Law wins Melbourne Cup
Sports.content:
Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington.

Seen as a St Leger hope after finishing fourth in the Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot and winning Newmarket's Bahrain Trophy for former trainers John and Thady Gosden, he was bought privately to continue his career in Australia, winning the Geelong Cup on his first outing for new connections.

With stablemate Royal Supremacy setting a strong pace for the big-race favourite to aim at, the son of Frankel showed a deadly turn of foot to run down the eventual fifth as Maher trained not only the first three home but also the fifth and sixth in the 'race that stops the nation'.

Maher told Australia's Channel Nine: "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but it's got to execute. I certainly didn't know Royal Supremacy was going to lead by that far but there's nothing better than a true staying test.

"Point Of Law has just thrived and I can't thank all the team and the owners enough. What a ride they've been on. It's been a whirlwind really, but I'm very proud of all the team."

Maher, who had previously won the Flemington feature alongside David Eustace with Gold Trip in 2022, also saddled Zahrann to finish the best part of four lengths behind his stablemate in second, with his Juja Kibo claiming the final spot on the podium.

The trainer, who fielded seven runners in total, added: "To get three horses in the first three spots, I'm very proud. It's been a whirlwind really."

Point Of Law was ridden by Ethan Brown who was enjoying his finest hour in the saddle at the venue his career was almost ended in a near-fatal fall in 2023.

Persuaded back to riding by Maher, his precision ride on the 6-1 favourite was the perfect way to repay the trainer, with the jockey saying: "Please don't wake me up. It's an amazing feeling.

"It's been well documented how Ciaron talked me out of horse training at one stage when I was about 22 years old, but he's done nothing but support me and back me.

"I've messed up plenty of times on his horses and he's had nothing but faith. He's believed in me and shown that by putting me on. I'm quite speechless.

"I thought Point Of Law had the best turn of foot in the race by far. He was shuffled back a bit further than I would've liked and I was trying to get him settled, and I looked up and saw Royal Supremacy about 20 in front and thought, 'Oh God'.

"I had to stay cool, stay patient, cut the bend and once he got that clear run in, his turn of foot was enormous. He's going to be a superstar horse, he's something special."

The raiding European party was dominated by Joseph O'Brien's five-strong team, but there was to be no third win in the race for the Irishman with Sons And Lovers achieving the best position, temporarily halting the Maher procession in fourth.

Derby third James J Braddock was next best of the O'Brien contingent in seventh, with George Boughey's Ebor runner-up Hopewell Rock, heavily backed by none other than JP McManus prior to the race, only ninth.

Sports.title: England's Mitchell ruled out of Nations Championship
Sports.content:
England have been dealt a blow with Alex Mitchell ruled out of the entire Nations Championship after sustaining a hamstring injury during Northampton’s 28-14 victory over Gloucester on Saturday.

The British and Irish Lions scrum-half underwent a scan on Monday, with the results confirming he will miss all four of this month's Tests.

It is the fourth hamstring injury Mitchell has sustained in 2026, dealing another setback to the scrum-half, who had been expected to play a key role in England's matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, as well as the Nations Championship finals weekend from November 27-29.

Jack van Poortvliet is now likely to start in the No 9 jersey for England's clash against the Wallabies on Sunday at the Allianz Stadium, with either Ben Spencer or Harry Randall providing cover from the bench.

Mitchell's Northampton team-mate Fin Smith is facing a race against time to be fit for Sunday's match, as he battles his second calf problem of the year.

Head coach Steve Borthwick will give Smith until Wednesday to prove he can play, with George Ford and Marcus Smith on standby to step in at fly-half.

Archie McParland, another Northampton half-back who is struggling with a calf issue, could return against Japan or New Zealand, but Sam Underhill (biceps), Kepueli Tuipulotu (knee) and Benhard Janse van Rensburg (concussion) will miss the whole of the second phase of the Nations Championship.

Sports.title: Lawson admits 'no assurance' of retaining Racing Bulls seat
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson has admitted he has been given "no assurance" about retaining his seat at Racing Bulls for 2027.

Lawson is the highest-placed midfield driver in the F1 Drivers' Championship, with only the Mercedes, McLaren, Ferrari and Red Bull drivers ahead of him in the standings.

The 24-year-old has scored more than twice as many points as team-mate and rookie Arvid Lindblad and underlined his strong campaign by finishing seventh in Mexico after starting from the pit lane.

Racing Bulls are the only F1 team that has not yet officially confirmed either of its 2027 drivers and it is understood Lawson's seat is under threat from Red Bull junior and Formula 2 title protagonist Nikola Tsolov.

"I'm trying my best. Every weekend I'm trying to maximise," Lawson timidly told Sky Sports F1.

"In Mexico I gave it everything. There's definitely no assurance at the moment [for next year]. It's a tough sport. Right now, I don't know what else to say, really."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP - the clash would eventually lead to both drivers receiving a grid penalty

Bulgarian driver Tsolov is highly rated by Red Bull as he's competing for the Formula 2 title in his rookie campaign, having been runner-up in Formula 3 last year.

The 19-year-old made his F1 practice debut in Mexico and was only one tenth behind Lindblad, which impressed Racing Bulls chief executive Peter Bayer.

"Honestly, [Tsolov's] performance on Friday was superb. It was his first time in the car, and he integrated into the team absolutely perfectly," Bayer told Austrian outlet ORF.

"Regarding the driver decision, he put in a fantastic performance. That decision rests with [team principal] Alan [Permane], and he will make it, or rather, announce it when he feels the time is right."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson reveals he apologised to Red Bull's Max Verstappen following their collision during practice at the Mexico City GP

Asked whether Lawson has done everything he can to prove himself, Bayer said: "That's the general consensus in the paddock.

"At the same time, our role, as the leading developer of talent in Formula 1, is to continuously bring new drivers through. We've brought 22 drivers into Formula 1, including the likes of Sebastian Vettel, Max Verstappen and others.

"That's why I say that, at the end of the day, the decision lies with Alan. And he will make the right choice for the team. We chatted about that briefly on Saturday."

Formula 1 2027 field Team Driver Driver Mercedes Kimi Antonelli George Russell Ferrari Lewis Hamilton Charles Leclerc McLaren Lando Norris Oscar Piastri Red Bull Max Verstappen Isack Hadjar Racing Bulls ???? ???? Alpine Pierre Gasly Franco Colapinto Haas ???? Rafael Camara Audi Nico Hulkenberg Gabriel Bortoleto Williams Carlos Sainz Alex Albon Aston Martin Fernando Alonso Lance Stroll Cadillac Sergio Perez Valtteri Bottas* *reported to be in doubt

What else is left to play out in the F1 driver market for 2027?

Despite signing a multi-year contract which began at the start of this year, Valtteri Bottas' future at Cadillac is up in the air.

Cadillac are keen for Formula 2 driver Colton Herta to qualify for a super licence, which would make him eligible to become a full-time Formula 1 driver.

The team have ran Herta in five practice sessions this season to try to gain super licence points, and the American is now just one point away from earning the licence.

What is a super licence in F1? A super licence is a licence you need to drive in Formula 1.



Points are collected by racing and performing well in other motorsport categories such as Formula 2, Formula 3 and IndyCar.



You need 40 points to qualify for a super licence which means you can drive full-time in F1

Cadillac are set to run Herta again in first practice this Friday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, where, if he drives 100km, he will pick up another super licence point.

"It is important (for Cadillac to have an American driver). It's an American team, it races under an American flag," said Cadillac team principal Marcin Budkowski.

"I think you've seen in Austin that we're building a strong American identity as well. It's great to have an American driver, it increases the hype.

"But it's also a question of timing. The right driver, when the team is ready for it, and so we're assessing this."

Image: Colton Herta is a threat to Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac seat for 2027 (Memmler/picture-alliance/dpa/AP Images)

Last month, Haas announced Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara will replace Esteban Ocon next year but did not confirm Oliver Bearman's seat.

Both Bearman and Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu have expressed confidence in recent weeks that a deal will be done to extend the 21-year-old's current contract, which expires at the end of the 2026 season.

"There are a few things in the background that we're working on, but it's been very clear that continuing with Haas will be my target, and we're just finalising a few things on that front," said Bearman.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman goes head-to-head with Jenson Button in the Ultimate Lap Challenge, but who will take the win? Powered by AWS

Asked about the delay, Bearman insisted that a deal would have been finalised by this point if it was up to him.

"It's not really in my hands, I can tell you that. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago," he added.

"But there are a few bigger-picture things that we're working on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman is reduced to tears after driving Ayrton Senna's 1985 Lotus 97T, the car Senna drove to his first-ever Formula 1 victory

Komatsu furiously dismissed reports claiming that contract extension talks with Bearman are being held up by the British driver demanding a £5m annual salary.

"I have no idea where that comes from," he said.

"I've experienced this sometimes this season as well. People say there's no smoke without fire but really some people will invent a story.

"What happened in Miami? Apparently, I had an argument with (Bearman's team-mate) Esteban Ocon. There's just absolutely zero truth in it and even those people claiming that they had some insider information etc, absolute total nonsense.

"This one again I don't know who smoked up this six-million euros number. The first time I saw it on Instagram, or Stu [Morrison, Haas press officer] forwarded it to me, and I was just like, 'oh another great… somebody has come up and stirred up whatever'.

"I have no comments to make because it's just not even close to the truth. Why do we engage in such an absolute nonsense? What's the point of it?"
