Sports.title: Why Leclerc didn’t give up Mexico GP lead after cutting Turn 5
Sports.content:
Ferrari Formula 1 driver Charles Leclerc has delved into his controversial Mexico Grand Prix drive, more specifically the way he snatched – and retained – the lead from Lewis Hamilton.

Leclerc challenged his polesitting team-mate for the lead at the start, with Hamilton holding him off over the first sequence of corners. The Monegasque then launched an attack around the outside of Turn 4, but while he was ahead at the apex, both cars went deep and ended up fully off the track.

Hamilton trundled back on track, losing a position to Max Verstappen, while Leclerc cut Turn 5 and stayed out in front. Having gained a lasting advantage from exceeding track limits, he was expected to let the sister car back through, but that would have entailed giving up a position to the Red Bull too.

In the end, Leclerc remained ahead of his rivals, copping a five-second penalty for the infringement.

“Lewis and I both tried to brake very late, we both didn't make the corner, I obviously cut the track,” the Monegasque recounted.

“Eventually then after Turn 5 there was Max in between, which made the situation more confusing. And speaking with the team, I didn't really have a clear feedback, and I think it was just confusing enough to keep the position, and I was expecting some kind of penalty. Then we paid the penalty.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Clive Mason / Getty Images

“We spoke briefly with the team to try and understand [what to do]. I asked ‘What should I do now?’ It's always very tricky – obviously in that situation you have to do something, but is it second, is it third? At the end I kept going. Obviously it's going to be a bit of a talking point, for sure, next briefing.”

The decision drew the ire of Hamilton, who repeatedly complained to race engineer Carlo Santi on the radio. “The problem is he's got clean air, and doesn't have to manage like the rest of us. He should just give the place back,” he said of Leclerc, before doubling down: “The stewards are basically handing Charles this win.”

Regardless of Leclerc’s controversial move to retain the lead, the intra-team incident came amid occasional friction between the Ferrari drivers this year.

Consequently asked about the rules of engagement at Ferrari, the 29-year-old played the situation down: “I mean, we are fighting for the win, so of course there's going to be very little margin left from him and from me. [In] the end, we both did a mistake going into Turn 4, it's not like we had contact or whatsoever. We both went straight and that gave the opportunity for Max to overtake.

“I don't think it should be that much of a talking point. Of course it was close, Turn 1 to 3 was very close, but I was expecting it, [in a] fight for the lead. For [Turn] 5 we both made a mistake, I paid with a penalty, then you can argue whether it's enough or not. And Lewis then paid out of [Turn] 5 with Max.”

Pressed on whether he and Hamilton needed more rules going forward, Leclerc pondered: “We will talk about it obviously. I don't know if he was very unhappy with what I did because I felt like it was very much on the limit also what he did. I think he was maybe more angry with the whole situation, how the situation was dealt in [Turns] 4-5 with the penalty, etc. So this is something we'll talk about for sure.”

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Photo by: Yuri Cortez / AFP via Getty Images

From then on, Leclerc worked at pulling away from Verstappen in an attempt to mitigate the impact of his penalty. He brought the gap up to 5.243s at the end of lap 24, but by the time he pitted – with the Red Bull following him into the pits – the Dutchman had cut his deficit by a few tenths.

In the end, this made no difference to the outcome. Leclerc’s pitstop was 6.3s longer than Verstappen’s, with 1.3s unaccounted for by the penalty, so the four-time world champion comfortably took the lead.

Leclerc’s race went from bad to worse at the second start, following the red flag for Valtteri Bottas’ crash, with a hefty lock-up that damaged the SF-26’s tyres – especially the front-left.

“I think we had quite a good pace, but unfortunately on the second restart everything went a bit more difficult,” he lamented.

“There was quite a lot of marbles on the right side of the track, and when I went on the brake, even though I didn't put a massive amount of brake pressure, I locked up straight away and I went to the cord of the tyres. So the last stint was very tricky.”

Leclerc consequently ended up fourth under the chequered flag – still scoring a sixth consecutive top-four finish.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Verstappen puzzled by engine braking: ‘It just decides by itself what to do’ | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen said he couldn’t explain the engine braking problems he reported on his radio during the latter stages of the Mexican Grand Prix.

“It happens randomly,” said Verstappen, who won the race despite. “The engine just decides by itself what to do, to be honest. So, I don’t know.

“Maybe I need to have a conversation with the engine before going into the race. Maybe it has to behave better.”

He suspected the problem was linked to the demanding conditions at the track. “We don’t know, sometimes it just happens. It’s not very consistent.

“I think, honestly, everything is running so hot here, and also for the turbocharger and everything, it’s tough to make everything spot on.”

Sports.title: “Silly” power unit rules prevent passing, says Hamilton: “The engine can go faster” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s power unit rules made it harder for drivers to race at the Mexican Grand Prix, according to Lewis Hamilton.

The Ferrari driver spent the final laps of the race trying to attack race leader Max Verstappen . He said he was unable to do so because of the limits on energy deployment. This causes the effect known as “clipping”, where the amount of power being delivered drops.

“You can’t overtake here,” said Hamilton in the post-race press conference with Verstappen and Andrea Kimi Antonelli. “I think it’s something the FIA need to [address]. It’s just quite bad, I’m sure these guys would agree.

“We have this clip at the end of the straight where you can’t go past a certain speed, so everyone just follows. It’s the silliest thing when you are behind and you have a little bit more power in the slipstream. You should be able to go past that to have a chance to overtake.

“The engine can go faster, it’s just they have these silly clips. It’s the worst engine profile setting that I think they’ve probably ever had in this sport and it doesn’t provide great racing. So today you probably didn’t see much overtaking, unfortunately, because of that.”

Other drivers warned before the race that the “speed limiter” would inhibit overtaking. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali has rejected criticism of the series power units and said fans “don’t understand” what clipping is.

Hamilton acknowledged other factors make overtaking especially difficult in Mexico. The high altitude means the air pressure is lower which makes it harder to keep cars cool when running in traffic. He also thinks the track’s configuration could be improved.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Obviously the starts were fun, but it’s a very hard track to follow [other cars at] with the thin air and low downforce. I gave it everything to try and get close to Max.

“I don’t know if they need to change the last corner because it’s so quick. I don’t know, there could be a change to the track, maybe, to enable us to have a little bit better racing.

“But everyone having this [clipping] this year just diminishes any opportunity of that.”

Sports.title: Antonelli says doubters “added fuel to the fire” in his world championship pursuit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
New wold champion Andrea Kimi Antonelli says he was driven to disprove those who said he wasn’t ready for Formula 1.

Mercedes brought him up through the junior ranks quickly, skipping Formula 3 entirely and only spending a single season in Formula 2. Antonelli made his F1 debut last year, aged just 18, with Mercedes’ works F1 team rather than one of their customers.

Antonelli’s first season did not go entirely smoothly. He endured a nine-round spell during which he failed to score on seven occasions.

However he was competitive right from the start of his second season and quickly overtook team mate George Russell in the championship. Antonelli clinched the title yesterday with four rounds to spare.

He said that had been a satisfying response to those who suggested he wasn’t ready for F1.

“It’s always good to shut off some of the noise,” said Antonelli. “I think in many ways it does help to add fuel to the fire, the fact that some people said that I didn’t belong in Formula 1 or I wasn’t ready for it.

“At some points last year, it probably looked like that I wasn’t ready for it. But I think last year, being able to experience those moments made me much more ready ahead of this year. Experiencing really low and difficult situations, high-pressure moments, really helped me to face certain situations this year, and definitely they made me mature a lot as a driver and as a person.”

Antonelli clinched the title with nine grand prix wins, the most of any driver. But he admits there was room for improvement in his performance. “I’ve had moments where I could have done better, a lot better. It’s just a constant learning process.

“But I think last year, being able to race [with] Mercedes, obviously [going] straight under the spotlight, made me grow much, much faster than if I would have gone to a smaller team, for example.”

Sports.title: Leclerc has wrong mentality, says Hamilton: ‘It’s ‘do-or-die, either I win or none of us do” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari would have lost more wins this year if he had the same “kamikaze” mentality as team mate Charles Leclerc.

The seven-times world champion blamed his team mate for costing Ferrari victory in yesterday’s Mexican Grand Prix. Both he and Leclerc went off at turn four while fighting over the lead on lap one.

Hamilton said he’d noticed Leclerc’s battles with his predecessor Carlos Sainz Jnr cost Ferrari points in the past.

“Before I joined this team, when I was at Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos several races, where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win,” he said. “But it is one thing when that’s happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That’s significant.

“The guy [Leclerc] is 28 years old, so I don’t think it’s an age thing. I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like, “Do-or-die. Either I win or none of us do,” and it shouldn’t be that. It should be us having, getting that one-two.”

Hamilton pointed out he did not compromise Leclerc’s race when he won at Silverstone earlier this year. “In Silverstone, I could have gone all kamikaze on him and taken him off and lost us the win, but instead the one-two was there.” They finished first and third but were holding the top two positions before Hamilton pitted when the Safety Car was deployed.

“For me, I’m happy for the team to have experienced that, but I’m hopeful we’ll work towards a better working place in the future.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

In remarks similar to those of Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur, Hamilton said the result did not do justice to the effort made by the team.

“I think the core thing to remember, which maybe comes with age, is that every decision you make in the car impacts all the people that work in the background for the whole team,” he said. “So, working as a team is a part of our job and a part of our contract.

“We have to work as a team, which we could have easily done today. So, it’s a shame to see us lose this, as we did. That will just continue unless action is taken, if a real deep, serious conversation is had. So, it shouldn’t happen [again] moving forward.

“Of course, I’ve had close battles with team mates in the past, and you can’t always get it right, but nine times out of ten we should be able to. So, I think we’ll take it offline and we’ll have some good conversations, hopefully. For sure, it won’t be easy, but it must be done.”

However Hamilton admitted he’d experienced tougher situations previously at other teams, such as at Mercedes, where he and team mate Nico Rosberg once took each other out at the start of a race.

“I’ve had way worse times at Mercedes. There were some really bad moments. I don’t really see there being huge differences. I think it was managed well at Mercedes, and I think Fred’s doing his best.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Fred came and spoke to me before the race, and I think he was nervous. Of course, he wants [his] two drivers to do well.”

He said he would have had to explain his actions had he attacked his team mate from behind the way Leclerc did.

“From my side, if I’m coming from behind and I’m taking all the risk and it ends up that we lose as a team, then I think I have some answering to do, because it impacts a lot of people. But the other way around, I’m in the lead, and it was just unnecessary.

“I think we could have easily had that one-two today, which would have been huge for the team and for everyone back at the factory who’s worked so hard to bring us these upgrades. I don’t really know what will be done because up until now nothing really has been done.”

Sports.title: Antonelli “lost two seconds because I was crying” at end of Mexican GP | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli admitted he was already crying before he took the chequered flag to win the world championship.

The Mercedes driver finished third in Mexico, clinching the title in his second season as a Formula 1 driver. The 20-year-old was so emotional he was struggling to see the track and he lost 1.8 seconds to the leaders on his final lap.

“I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically,” Antonelli admitted. “I couldn’t see clearly ahead.

“I could see two Ferraris, somehow, with the tears. So it was very special.”

Antonelli became the youngest world champion in F1 history, just five years after moving from karts to cars. “A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment,” he said, “all the memories since karting all the way to here.

“It was a very special final lap, and definitely when I crossed the line, I let it all out because it was just achieving one of my biggest dreams. It was very special.”

The championship outcome was a foregone conclusion before the weekend began: Antonelli needed to score only two points to be certain of the title even if his closest rival won all the remaining rounds. Nonetheless he felt the weight of expectation during the weekend.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“I knew I was very close. However, I still needed to get the job done, and, of course, you still want to do a good race. You want to do a good performance, so that was the goal.

“But it hasn’t been the easiest weekend either. Physically, I haven’t been in the best shape, but also yesterday we had a bad qualifying execution, and emotions were a bit high overall.

“But I’m really happy that today we did a strong race and really happy that we managed to finish the job. And then now we’ve got a few races to go, and we’re just going to enjoy all the way and try to finish on a high.”

He made a careful start to the race, ceding a position to eventual winner Max Verstappen on the run to turn one. However he decided to risk more at the second standing start following a red flag period.

“At the start I was very cautious, and I gave a lot of room. So I was probably playing it very much on the safe side.

“But then I saw I had the pace, and especially that first stint, I knew we would be in the fight because the pace was very good on used tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Then with the red flag, it kind of all went back to zero. And in that moment I was like, ‘You know what? I’m just going to take more risks.’

“I had the opportunity to gain a few places, and that move on Charles [Leclerc] was crucial to get on the podium. I tried until the end to stay close, and it was very fun, the last stint, because we were all, I think, the three of us within two seconds, and we were all pushing. It was just difficult, of course, to overtake, but it was high intensity, and it was fun.

“Then on the last lap I just backed off because I just couldn’t see the track. I was getting emotional, and I said, ‘I’m just going to back off because otherwise I crash here.’ So it was just good to bring it home.”

Sports.title: Call this the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix says Verstappen after sixth Mexican GP win | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen joked Formula 1 should rename Mexico’s round of the world championship after him following his sixth victory in the race.

The Red Bull driver has now scored more wins in Mexico City than he has at any other venue. He became the fourth driver to score more than five wins at the same venue and the first to do so at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez

“They should actually call it the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix,” said Verstappen. “That would be great.”

His five previous wins at the track came between 2017 and 2023. Verstappen said he saw no obvious reason why he had been particularly successful at this venue.

“I honestly love being here,” he said. “I love the city, I love the environment, I love the fans, but I have no idea why.

“It just happens. Sometimes your car just comes alive and you’ve had good races and not a lot of bad luck sometimes as well. So it’s just always come together for me here and, of course, I happily take that.”

Verstappen said he was surprised to move into a strong position immediately after the start of the race, thanks partly to Ferrari drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton going off at turn four.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The first start already made my race a bit better, getting into turn one, and then, of course, the battle that I saw unfold in turn four put me in a quite nice spot.”

Leclerc received a five-second time penalty for his infringement and Verstappen jumped ahead of him when they pitted on the same lap.

“It was a bit tough, to be honest, I think Charles just pulled away. I could not really stay with him. I did not have the pace to follow him, but at the same time, I was still within that five-second window.

“So, then the team did a really good job to follow him in [to the pits]. It’s always very tough when you have a five-second penalty to actually make it exactly five seconds. So, I jumped him, and honestly, after that, it was quite tough.”

The race winner said he feared for his chances when the Safety Car was deployed following Valtteri Bottas’s crash. The race was stopped and restarted, and Verstappen maintained his lead ahead of Hamilton.

“Kimi [Antonelli] was flying, still, out there on the first set of tyres, and I just did not really have the grip for whatever reason. Charles was very close, but at the same time, it’s very hard to follow around here because everything overheats, and that probably helped me as well because I think at one point Charles had to back off just for cooling, and that was quite nice for me.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“But at the same time, when I saw the Safety Car come out just out of the last corner and I couldn’t box, I was like, ‘There’s no way this is happening now,’ because that was then probably game over for me.

“Then, of course, it ended up being a red flag, so then it reset everything. I was a bit worried because our starts this year have not been amazing, but luckily today, twice, they have actually been good, and that then made my way ’til the end.

“But it was not made easy. I mean, Lewis was in my gearbox, pushing hard. It was basically a qualifying lap ’til the end. Yeah, it was tough out there. It was a tough race to the end, just to not make any mistakes. But, of course, I’m happy to win today.”

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Uses Online Backlash To Fuel Shane Mosley Jr. Clash
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley figures getting rinsed across social media might actually work in his favor. Losing his WBO middleweight strap threw his name directly into feeds belonging to fans who had never watched him box. Now, he plans on using Shane Mosley Jr. to make an impression that actually sticks.

“Winning caps it all off, 100 percent,” Bentley said during their Zuffa Boxing 12 faceoff on Sky Sports. “I mean, everyone’s saying my name. I wouldn’t know about flowers yet, ’cause right now I’m getting rinsed online, but that’s all cool.” Bentley pointed out that casual fans tuning in because of the drama finally get to watch him perform. He fully expects to stop Mosley inside the distance.

Bentley clashes with Mosley this Saturday at Copper Box Arena in London. It was the exact matchup Bentley pushed for before taking on mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández. The WBO shut down his appeal, stripping his belt on the spot. While Bentley kept his spot on the card, the sanctioning drama created an instant buzz. The real casualty was the world title he could have carried into a massive unification clash.

That loss stings because Bentley still craves marquee matchups. He insists he technically remains the champion, keeping his sights locked on the middleweights signed to Zuffa. Carlos Adames got mentioned during the press festivities. Bentley made it clear he intends to hunt division leaders as a challenger, targeting the exact names he wanted during his title reign. Zuffa offers the platform, yet Saturday comes without any guarantees.

Mosley acknowledged Bentley lost his strap through boardroom politics rather than ring action, though he still expects to cruise to a points victory. Coming off a signature win against Serhii Bohachuk, Mosley wants the spotlight Bentley created. Invading London to steal a victory puts Mosley first in line for major fights under the promotional banner. Forcing Bentley into a messy boxing match could also ruin the knockout statement Bentley promised.

Bentley walked himself into a trap. Flattening an opponent who just upset Bohachuk forces the critics to shut their mouths after the WBO embarrassment. An emphatic stoppage forces Zuffa to open the checkbook for Adames. Scraping past Mosley on a dull decision does nothing for him, leaving him on the outside looking in with zero leverage. Internet trolls jumped on his neck the second the belt vanished. Saturday determines if Bentley backs up his mouth or becomes a punchline in his own backyard.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Walks Into Clarke Ambush At Copper Box
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith gets back in the ring against Cheavon Clarke on Saturday, November 7, at Copper Box Arena in London. The bout headlines Zuffa Boxing 12, putting the former WBO cruiserweight champion in front of a man holding an amateur victory over him from 2016.

Billam-Smith enters at 22-2 with 14 knockouts, aiming to hold his place near the front of the division. Clarke comes in at 12-2 with 9 knockouts, looking to make his previous success count on a major professional stage.

The preliminary bouts begin at 12 p.m. Eastern Time, which is 5 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time. The main card takes over at 2 p.m. Eastern, or 7 p.m. locally in the UK. The headline ring walks are expected around 5 p.m. Eastern and 10 p.m. Greenwich Mean Time, though that timing will shift depending on how quickly the supporting fights wrap up. Viewers in the United States and Canada can watch the card through Paramount Plus. Fans in the UK and Ireland can watch the main card on Sky Sports, with online streaming through NOW and the preliminary matches carried on Sky digital platforms.

The supporting lineup features Denzel Bentley taking on Shane Mosley Jr. in a ten round middleweight co-feature. Heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter meets Ivan Balaz on the main portion of the show, followed by a cruiserweight match between Lucas Roehrig and Connal McDonald, a middleweight bout featuring Sam Hickey against Amaury Massenaux, and Kayla Allen versus Julia Igel. The preliminary portion includes Zach Parker against Umar Dzambekov at light heavyweight, Masood Abdulah taking on Adan Palma, and the debut appearance of Vinnie Kemp.

Both main event fighters fought grueling bouts in June. Billam-Smith wore down Ryan Rozicki until Rozicki stayed on his stool after the seventh round. Clarke hit the canvas twice in the fourth round against Jack Massey, yet recovered to stop Massey three rounds later. Clarke owns the quicker hands over ten rounds, which means Billam-Smith cannot afford to spend long stretches following his opponent around the perimeter.

Billam-Smith must use his jab to establish distance, force Clarke toward the ropes, and work on the inside to sap Clarke of his bounce. Even if Billam-Smith lands clean early, Clarke has already shown he carries fight-ending power when wounded, meaning the former champion needs sharp discipline to avoid getting caught on the way in.

For Billam-Smith, he is entering that dangerous zone where a fighter’s style catches up with their shelf life, making this matchup against Clarke a massive upset potential.

Look at his recent stretch. Billam-Smith does not have easy nights. He does not box on the outside and slip shots; he relies on imposing physical will, eating three clean punches to land four of his own. By the final bell against Gilberto Ramirez, Brandon Glanton, and Ryan Rozicki, his face looked like ground beef. His skin splits if someone looks at him wrong, and the scar tissue around his eyes has become an open invitation for referees and ringside doctors to intervene.

When a pressure fighter like Billiam-Smith, who absorbs heavy punishment, starts racking up rounds at 35 or 36, the decline rarely happens gradually. It happens off a cliff. The punch resistance cracks, the reflexes slow by half a second, and suddenly shots that used to get brushed off start rattling the frame.

Clarke is precisely the wrong stylistic matchup for an aging, battle-worn brawler to face in a ten-round fight. He has the amateur pedigree and hand speed to exploit Billam-Smith’s porous defense. Billam-Smith comes forward in straight lines with his chin up. Clarke has already proven in the amateurs that his hand speed gives Billam-Smith fits, and fast combinations against an opponent with compromised scar tissue is a recipe for severe cuts early.

Despite his advanced age, Clarke still possesses real power and resilience. Jack Massey dropped Clarke twice in the fourth round, and Clarke still showed the composure and engine to recover and stop Massey three rounds later. If Billam-Smith hurts Clarke, he cannot just swarm carelessly, because Clarke throws violent counters when trapped.

At this point, the schedule works entirely against Billam-Smith. At ten rounds instead of twelve, the distance favors the explosive, faster starter. Billam-Smith typically needs eight or nine rounds of grinding pressure to break a man down. In a ten-rounder, if Clarke banks four of the first six rounds behind speed and angles, Billam-Smith runs out of road and has to chase recklessly.

If Billam-Smith gets dragged into another trench war where he has to swallow flush shots to make Clarke work, this has all the ingredients of an ambush. Clarke has the speed, the confidence from their amateur history, and the firepower to hand the former champion a costly defeat.

Sports.title: Mannix Says Munguía and Melikuziev Have Reached Terms
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev have reportedly come to terms for a WBA super middleweight title fight. Munguía named his mandatory challenger after beating Nikita Zon by unanimous decision Saturday in Riyadh, but Sergio Mora still doubts he’ll take the fight.

“I think Munguía is going to stay away from him,” Mora said during his discussion with Chris Mannix. “Well, I think he’s going to fight him. I don’t think he’s going to give up his belt, and everything I’ve been told [is] that they’ve come to terms on the fight,” Mannix said on his channel. He gave no date for the defense.

Mora had already picked Melikuziev before the Zon fight. He sees a natural 168-pounder who uses his southpaw angles better than Zon and hits harder. Mannix brought up Melikuziev’s close fight with Darius Fulghum, when he needed a knockdown in the 12th. That’s a fair reason to hesitate over picking Bektemir, but Munguía gave him something specific to work on in Riyadh.

When Zon hurt Munguía in the sixth, the champion bent forward and pulled his gloves up around his ears. Zon kept hooking at the sides of the guard. Mora thought a straight punch or an uppercut could have brought Munguía’s head up and given referee Tony Weeks a reason to stop it. Both men backed Weeks for letting it continue. Munguía came back to hurt Zon in the same round.

What would worry me about Bektemir is what happens before Munguía gets to the ropes. Munguía likes to walk a man down and get close enough to work with both hands.

Every step in gives a southpaw with good feet a chance to move outside his lead foot and send a left hand through the middle. Munguía can come back from one bad minute, as he showed against Zon. Against Melikuziev, he may have to solve that left hand every time he tries to get his own offense going.

Sports.title: Could Rocky Marciano Take Away Larry Holmes’s Jab?
Sports.content:
Larry Holmes was one win away from matching Rocky Marciano’s 49–0 record when Michael Spinks took his heavyweight title in September 1985. After losing a close unanimous decision, Holmes had something to say about the champion whose record he’d come up short of tying. “Marciano couldn’t wear my jockstrap,” he said.

I thought Spinks earned that decision by taking the final round, and I gave Holmes the rematch, which Spinks won by split decision. But the crack about Marciano got me thinking about something Holmes did in the ring. He sometimes left his left arm extended between jabs to keep a shorter man at a distance. Most fighters would try to get around it. I think Marciano would have started punching it.

Rocky could come up from his crouch with a short uppercut into the elbow or dig a hook into the upper arm when Holmes covered up. He’d take some clean jabs getting close enough to do it. But if those punches made Holmes think twice about leaving the arm out, Marciano would have more room to step in. A punch that looked wasted in the fourth could buy him a shot at the ribs in the tenth.

Holmes could make that a slow and painful trade for Marciano. A quick jab and half a step back would leave Rocky reaching for an arm that was already gone. If Marciano tried to cover the extra ground by ducking in from too far away, Holmes could catch him with the right uppercut. Rocky might do good work once he got his head against Holmes’s chest and still spend most of the round trying to get there.

The danger for Holmes would come when he started pulling straight back with his hands down. Marciano was behind against Jersey Joe Walcott before knocking him out in the 13th to win the title. In the Ezzard Charles rematch, he scored an eighth-round stoppage with his nose badly split. Holmes could be well ahead after ten rounds and still have to watch where his left hand came back after every jab. If it dropped to his waist, Marciano could throw his right over it without having to get all the way inside.

I’d take Holmes by decision over 15 rounds. I can see Marciano hurting him late, especially if the work on the arm took some snap off the jab. But Holmes could win the first two minutes of a round from a distance and make Rocky spend most of the last minute closing it. I’d give Holmes more of those rounds than I’d give Marciano the kind where he got close early and kept him there.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith Welcomes Oleksandr Usyk Fight
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith would welcome a fight with Oleksandr Usyk at cruiserweight, but it’s hard to see why Usyk would take it.

Billam-Smith faces Cheavon Clarke this Saturday in a fight that has generated little buzz. Even a strong win would leave him a long way from getting Usyk’s attention.

“Anyone would love to have that opportunity,” Billam-Smith said on talkSPORT when asked if he’d like to fight Usyk. He praised Usyk for what he accomplished in his first run at cruiserweight, including beating opponents in their own backyards. He also floated the possibility of Usyk fighting David Benavidez in May.

Benavidez is precisely why the Billam-Smith fight is so hard to picture. If Usyk can get Benavidez, there’s little reason to take a detour through Billam-Smith first. If he beats Benavidez, there’s even less reason to stick around for a fight that would be a much tougher sell.

Saudi backing could put a big purse on the table, but someone would have to be willing to take a hefty loss on the show. A former world champion settling an old score at the Copper Box is a decent Saturday main event. It would take a lot more than a win over Clarke to make Billam-Smith the opponent people want to see for one of Usyk’s last fights.

Billam-Smith tossing his name into the mix sounds like wishful thinking, because from a business standpoint, the numbers simply do not work. At cruiserweight, the appetite begins and ends with marquee matchups. Benavidez brings immense Mexican American star power and guaranteed crossover viewers. Jai Opetaia is viewed as the true elite at 200 pounds, a genuine pound-for-pound talent who can test Usyk athletically.

Those fights carry legitimate commercial intrigue and legacy value. Billam-Smith, by contrast, is a domestic UK ticket seller whose profile drops off steeply once you leave Britain. Expecting Saudi organizers to cut a massive check for an unheralded opponent when far bigger fights exist makes zero sense.

The winner of Tyson Fury versus Anthony Joshua remains a gigantic stadium draw for Usyk regardless of previous records. Fans would gladly line up for an undisputed rubber match or a fresh chapter with Daniel Dubois before Usyk hangs up the gloves.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Ordered To Fight Michael Zerafa For Vacant WBO Belt
Sports.content:
Yoenli Hernández could have to go through a second purse bid just to get his first WBO title fight. The WBO has authorized negotiations between Hernández and Michael Zerafa for its vacant middleweight belt after stripping Denzel Bentley, whose mandatory defense against Hernández had already gone to bid.

Zerafa, ranked fourth by the WBO, moves ahead of two contenders who are unavailable. No. 2 Vito Mielnicki Jr. is unavailable, and No. 3 Tim Tszyu is under contract to face Erislandy Lara. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri said formal notice would follow. The fighters’ teams will have 20 days from the issuance of that order to reach a deal.

Hernández Has Already Been Through One Purse Bid

“The parties shall have 20 days from the issuance of the formal negotiation order to reach terms, pursuant to WBO Regulations or purse bid proceedings,” Olivieri said on X.

Warriors Boxing was the only bidder for Bentley’s mandatory defense and secured the promotional rights with a $200,000 offer on September 29. Bentley stood to receive $150,000, with the remaining $50,000 going to Hernández. Bentley had asked to fight Shane Mosley Jr. first and defend against Hernández afterward, but the WBO denied his appeal on October 22. He kept the Mosley fight, scheduled for November 7 in London as his Zuffa Boxing debut, and the WBO stripped him.

That first bid shows why the next 20 days matter. Hernández’s promoter did what the WBO process required and put up the money to stage the defense. Bentley still had a fight he preferred to take, and Hernández came out of the process with the same No. 1 ranking he had going in. A deal with Zerafa would spare him another round of bidding and give both camps a chance to settle where the fight takes place and what they’ll be paid.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) brings the bigger punch, but his last fight gave Zerafa something to study. Francisco Verón took him the distance in August and held him to a majority decision. For all the talk about why Bentley took the Mosley fight, that result matters more to Zerafa. There are rounds to win against Hernández if Zerafa can keep him from setting his feet and make him work to close the distance.

The opening for Zerafa came from the two names above him being unavailable. What he can do with it is another matter. Hernández has the power to make this a short night if Zerafa stands in front of him, but the Cuban still has to show he can take charge when an opponent makes him work deep into a fight. That’s what makes the pairing worth seeing once the teams get it signed.

Sports.title: Can Anyone Outside Of  Terence Crawford Defeat Canelo At 168?
Sports.content:
On Halloween night, Canelo Alvarez defeated Christian Mbilli to become a three-time super-middleweight world champion, and now the question is: outside of Terence Crawford, can any other boxer defeat Canelo at 168?

When Christian Mbilli entered the ring to face Canelo Alvarez, a reasonable number of boxing pundits thought Mbilli was going to pull off the upset. Alvarez has a history of stamina issues, and many assumed Mbilli could take advantage.

The idea was for Mbilli to overwhelm Canelo with his high-volume punching, wear him down, take over in the later rounds, and win a close decision. Unfortunately for Mbilli, the bout didn’t go that way.

Canelo Alvarez was able to dictate the range and the pace of the fight. Canelo’s defense was sharp, his stamina was good, and on offense he dominated the action with skillful counterpunching and pinpoint accuracy.

Mbilli fought the wrong type of fight, as most of the bout took place at mid-range as opposed to close quarters. Mbilli gave Canelo too much respect, and on multiple occasions he looked confused.

Christian Mbilli was severely outclassed, and because of that, the fight looked like a glorified sparring session. As a result of the bout, Canelo Alvarez (64-3-2, 39 KOs) is the new WBC super-middleweight world champion.

The sport of boxing is based on levels, and on the night of October 31st, Canelo Alvarez proved he was levels above Christian Mbilli. Now fight fans are wondering: are any of the current top super-middleweights close to being on Canelo’s level?

Terence “Bud” Crawford defeated Canelo Alvarez with his skill set and his ring IQ. None of the top super-middleweights have a skill set compatible with Crawford’s, and none of them come close to Crawford when it comes to ring intelligence.

With that being said, one would ask, outside of a rematch with Crawford, what would be the ideal fight for Canelo at 168? If Terence Crawford can’t be convinced to come out of retirement, then Hamzah Sheeraz is probably the best candidate.

The former WBO world champion Hamzah Sheeraz is a 6-foot-3-inch super-middleweight who is skilled, and he can effectively fight from long range. On Halloween night, Sheeraz was ringside analyzing the fight.

Back in July 2025, Hamzah Sheeraz looked sharp as he stopped Edgar Berlanga in the 5th round. A year later, Sheeraz had a lackluster performance, as he scored a majority decision victory over Simon Zachenhuber.

Now Hamzah Sheeraz (24-0-1, 19 KOs) appears to be the frontrunner in regards to facing Canelo in 2027. If Sheeraz doesn’t get the match, then Canelo may choose to fight one of the other champions at 168.

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Targets Canelo Alvarez With BoMac Behind Him
Sports.content:
Lester Martinez would give Canelo Alvarez a dangerous first defense of his reclaimed WBC super middleweight title. The aggressive Guatemalan can punch and has Brian “BoMac” McIntyre in his corner, giving him access to the trainer who helped Terence Crawford beat Canelo.

“My dream now is to fight Canelo because he’s the champion,” Martinez said to Izquierdazo Boxeo in a quote shared by The Ring. His WBC interim title gives that ambition substance, although it does not establish that Canelo has been ordered to face him next.

The McIntyre connection makes this more interesting than another contender requesting a payday. BoMac knows what went into preparing Crawford for Canelo and could bring that knowledge into Martinez’s camp. The WBC lists McIntyre as Martinez’s trainer.

Crawford could also offer firsthand advice about Canelo’s timing, counterpunching and habits under pressure. His involvement in a potential camp has not been announced, but Martinez would have an obvious reason to seek his stablemate’s input.

Mbilli took too long to alter his approach when Canelo’s jab and head movement disrupted his pressure last weekend. He continued following Canelo without consistently changing how he attacked. Martinez would likely arrive expecting those tactics, with McIntyre preparing ways to get past the jab and vary his attack.

That would not make Lester immune to Canelo’s counters. It could, however, reduce the rounds spent trying to work out what to do next. BoMac could prepare alternatives before the opening bell and help Martinez adjust between rounds when Canelo starts frustrating him.

Martinez would still need to win with his own tools. He cannot copy Crawford’s performance. His route would involve sustained pressure, body punching and enough variation to prevent Canelo from anticipating each attack.

His 2025 draw with Mbilli gives him a relevant result against the man Canelo just defeated. Beating Canelo is another matter, but an aggressive puncher arriving with informed preparation would be a serious undertaking for the 36-year-old champion.

Ghana News.title: Egya Tur: The camera is watching
Ghana News.content:
The roads were unusually sane and peaceful this morning. A trotro actually stopped at a zebra crossing. I suspect the traffic cameras. Overnight, we appeared to have become a nation of considerate motorists. It seems the national character can be improved by installing a pole.

A policeman can be greeted, pleaded with and reminded that we are all brothers. A camera presents a constitutional difficulty: where does one put the “something small”?

There are, however, a few matters to resolve.

We are to observe speed limits on roads where the signs are missing. Perhaps the sign has gone to the scrap dealer, where it now regulates the speed of commerce. The motorist must nevertheless know what it said before it became a saucepan.

Of course, drivers should know the general limits. But a state capable of photographing my number plate should also be capable of putting up a sign I can read.

Then there are the roads themselves. On some stretches, the camera is an unnecessary expense. The potholes have been enforcing speed limits for years, without salaries, pensions or public education campaigns. Occasionally, they confiscate a tyre.

Now consider the restriction on preaching and hawking in moving buses. Should it be enforced, who will provide the entertainment?

The itinerant preacher has long performed an unrecognised public service. Between the heat, the humidity, the smells and the suspension, passengers need something to take their minds off the journey. A vigorous account of the torments of hell can make present conditions seem almost tolerable.

The hawker follows with one bottle capable of treating every condition the journey has aggravated.

Remove both and the passenger is left alone with the road. Sleep is no substitute. Just as the eyes close, a pothole delivers the next sermon.

Still, if this morning is anything to go by, technology deserves serious attention.

There is an old Fante joke about prisoners left sitting before a cannon. Their captors were nowhere in sight, but nobody dared leave. Even when nature called, a prisoner would respectfully address the unattended weapon:

“Egya tur, mereko sanchin maaba.”

“Sir Cannon, please, I am going to urinate and return.”

And return he did, to resume his imprisonment.

Nobody knew whether the cannon would fire. Nobody wished to conduct the experiment.

Perhaps I am overthinking this. This morning, we were all behaving ourselves. Why? Not because we feared a fine. We have never been particularly afraid of a fine we could negotiate. Nor had we acquired, overnight, a new respect for the law.

We behaved because we did not know what the camera would do. And that uncertainty is a very old kind of obedience.

Egya Tur has gone digital.

Let us hope the authorities are equally attentive to the signs and the roads.

Could we install a camera for that too?

Ghana News.title: Abu Jinapor escorted out of Parliament after refusing to withdraw passport allegation against Ablakwa
Ghana News.content:
The Member of Parliament for Damongo, Samuel Abu Jinapor, was escorted out of Parliament’s Chamber by a Parliamentary Marshal after refusing to withdraw an allegation that Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa was involved in the sale of diplomatic passports.

The November 3, incident occurred during the first sitting of Parliament’s Third Meeting of the Second Session, following a disagreement over the allegation against the Minister.

After his accusation, Majority Leader, James Agalga objected suggesting that the claim was not supported by facts.

On the back of this, the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, was asked by the Speaker to withdraw the allegation and removed from the Chamber by a Parliamentary Marshal.

Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin described the speaker's decision as "harsh, high-handed and unfair."

The confrontation comes amid growing criticism from the Minority over the issuance of Ghanaian diplomatic and service passports, with the caucus raising concerns about whether some beneficiaries met the requirements for obtaining the official travel documents.

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has particularly questioned the issuance of service passports to six individuals whose official positions, it claims, were either inaccurately described or did not exist.

The party has petitioned the United States Embassy in Ghana to suspend recognition of affected passports pending an independent verification of their eligibility.

Earlier on Tuesday, supporters of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), led by its youth wing, staged a demonstration in Accra dubbed ‘Yɛgye Yɛn Sika’, demanding accountability over the expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa.

The protesters questioned the reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians, citing alleged discrepancies in payment records, duplicate entries and gaps in supporting documentation.

They also raised concerns about the issuance of diplomatic and service passports, demanding greater transparency over the eligibility of recipients and the authorities responsible for approving the documents.

The NPP has called for the resignation of Mr Ablakwa or his dismissal by President John Dramani Mahama, arguing that the allegations surrounding the evacuation expenditure require an independent investigation.

The Foreign Affairs Minister has rejected allegations of financial wrongdoing and maintained that the evacuation expenditure should be subjected to an independent audit.

The parliamentary incident adds another dimension to the growing disagreement between the Majority and Minority over the Minister's handling of the evacuation exercise and the diplomatic passport controversy.

Ghana News.title: NDC will not shield officials involved in wrongdoing – Fifi Kwetey
Ghana News.content:
The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, says the party will not shield any of its members or government appointees found culpable of wrongdoing, insisting that President John Dramani Mahama shares its commitment to accountability.

Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said the party was determined to seek answers whenever concerns about possible wrongdoing emerged, rather than rush to defend those involved.

He said the approach represented a departure from what he described as a previous tendency among political organisations to protect their members when allegations arose.

"That I am fully aware of. That when something is going on, even the party, we are the first people to start calling to see what's going on. We want to know what's going on," he said.

"I suppose in the past when the number one instinct is to try to protect and defend and cover, now no. The intention is to say what's going on. We want to be clear."

Mr Kwetey said the NDC's commitment to accountability meant that no individual should be allowed to jeopardise the party's reputation or the country's interests.

He outlined what he described as a hierarchy in which the interests of the nation take precedence over those of the party, while the party's collective interest comes before that of any individual member.

"Like the good book says, it is better for one individual to perish than for the nation to perish. Same way, it is better for an individual to be sacrificed than for the party as a whole to take a fall. The same way, it is better for the party itself to be sacrificed than for the nation to be sacrificed," he said.

"So it's almost like that hierarchy. Individual is secondary to party. Party is secondary to nation."

The NDC General Secretary said President Mahama's position on accountability had made it easier for the party leadership to raise concerns with government officials.

He said the President was similarly interested in establishing the facts whenever questions arose about the conduct of ministers and chief executives.

"In this respect, I would say the president is in alignment, and therefore it gets easier," he said.

He added that the President's approach reinforced the party's efforts to seek explanations and ensure that the right steps were taken when concerns emerged.

The NDC government has faced public scrutiny over allegations and controversies involving public officials, including the World Cup visa controversy and questions surrounding the cost of evacuating Ghanaians from abroad.

Mr Kwetey's comments come amid broader public debate about the government's anti-corruption commitments and the extent to which officials within its own ranks will be held accountable.

Ghana News.title: Fifi Kwetey admits political mercenaries exist within NDC
Ghana News.content:
The General Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Fifi Kwetey, has acknowledged that political mercenaries operate within Ghana's political parties, including his own, warning that the practice undermines party discipline and national development.

Speaking on JoyNews' PM Express, Mr Kwetey said many people join political parties primarily for personal benefits rather than a commitment to the ideals and objectives of the organisations.

He described a political mercenary as someone whose involvement in a party is driven by personal interest rather than a shared national purpose.

"A mercenary is somebody who is literally in it just for himself. If he gets his benefit, he can motivate everybody because all he wants is himself. And that is not what it is that we should have," he said.

"We should have people who join a cause because first of all, they believe that this group will be able to make the country better."

Mr Kwetey said the NDC was working towards building a party in which collective interests take precedence over individual ambitions.

He acknowledged that the tendency for people to join political parties in anticipation of personal rewards had become common, partly because political organisations had allowed the practice to persist.

"Many people join parties fundamentally because of what they can get. And that sadly has been the reality. And because the political parties have allowed it. But that should not be," he said.

He stressed that party members must recognise that "the party as a collective is far more important than the individuals".

The NDC General Secretary's comments come amid broader concerns about money politics, patronage and indiscipline within Ghana's political parties.

The NDC has also faced allegations of vote-buying during its internal elections, raising questions about the influence of financial inducements in party organisation and leadership contests.

Mr Kwetey said the party would continue working towards a political culture in which members are driven by shared values and a commitment to national development rather than expectations of personal gain.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s US$10 billion New Economy programme will turn recovery into jobs – Dr. Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says the 2027 Budget will set out how the government plans to turn Ghana’s economic recovery into decent jobs for young people, better incomes for farmers and more opportunities for Ghanaian businesses to expand and hire.

Dr Forson is scheduled to present the budget to Parliament on Thursday, 12 November 2026. The budget will unveil the details of the New Economy programme, a four-year investment plan announced by President John Dramani Mahama.

“Ghanaians made sacrifices to get our economy back on its feet. Now, that recovery must mean decent jobs for our young people, better incomes for our farmers and room for Ghanaian businesses to grow and hire,” Dr Forson said.

“Next week, I will show how the New Economy will turn the gains we have made together into jobs and prosperity for all.”

The US$10 billion programme, which will run from 2027 to 2030, is designed to expand domestic production, increase the share of Ghana’s raw materials processed locally and help Ghanaian firms sell more at home and abroad.

The budget comes after Ghana completed the final review of its IMF-supported lending programme in July. Ghana Statistical Service figures show the economy grew by 6.0 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, while annual inflation stood at 5.2 per cent in September.

Dr. Forson signalled the shift towards job creation in the July Mid-Year Fiscal Policy Review. The November budget is expected to show which investments the government will prioritise in 2027 and how it intends to finance them while preserving the economic gains of the recovery.

Ghana News.title: IGNITE, brAInify train 50 police and immigration officers in AI
Ghana News.content:
Fifty officers from the Ghana Police Service's Criminal Investigations Department (CID) and the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) have received specialised training in the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to support criminal investigations and intelligence gathering.

The training, organised by IGNITE Social Enterprise in partnership with brAInify, took place in Accra on October 29, 2026.

It brought together senior personnel from the two security agencies, including officers from the CID's Anti-Human Trafficking Unit, Interpol, Cybersecurity, Financial Crime and Legal units.

The programme focused on practical applications of AI in managing complex case files, analysing financial transaction trails, identifying manipulated digital content and preparing intelligence reports for command-level decision-making.

Facilitated by two AI specialists from the United Arab Emirates, the workshop also covered the detection of synthetic media, including AI-generated images, audio and manipulated text.

Speaking at the event, IGNITE Global Advisory Board Member and Strategic Partner for Sub-Saharan Africa, Nathan Kwabena Anokye Adisi, popularly known as Bola Ray, said the use of AI could reduce the time officers spend processing administrative information and allow them to concentrate on analysis and decision-making.

He said the initiative was intended to equip security personnel with tools to extract useful insights from data and improve the quality of investigative outputs.

Assistant Superintendent of Immigration Rachael Klomegah described the training as timely, particularly in view of the growing use of AI-generated content and digital manipulation.

She said the skills acquired would help officers identify anomalies in AI-generated text, images and audio, which she considered important for border and identity protection.

A participant from the CID, Sergeant Salamata Sophiano, said the tools demonstrated during the workshop could improve the handling of existing investigations, particularly in structuring information and preparing intelligence reports.

She called for further training to help officers develop their proficiency in the use of the technology.

IGNITE's Regional Consultant for Sub-Saharan Africa, Paul Yao Dovi, said the adoption of AI in public institutions should be guided by integrity, transparency and compliance with relevant regulations.

All 50 participants received certificates after completing the programme.

The training was delivered through brAInify, an AI-powered digital education platform developed by IGNITE to support digital literacy and workforce skills development.

IGNITE Social Enterprise, headquartered in Hong Kong, describes itself as a global social enterprise focused on digital education, micro-entrepreneurship and social e-commerce.

brAInify is its digital learning platform, which the organisation says is designed to help individuals and professionals develop digital and AI-related skills.

Ghana News.title: E-Jobs4All opens applications for fully funded entrepreneurship programme
Ghana News.content:
Applications have opened for the Entrepreneurship Jobs for All (E-Jobs4All) programme, a fully funded initiative designed to equip aspiring and existing entrepreneurs in Ghana with business development skills, mentorship and access to investment opportunities.

The programme is a partnership between Queen’s University in Canada, the Community and Entrepreneurial Development Initiative (CEDI Ghana) and Leadogo Incorporated, Canada.

It seeks to support startups, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), students, unemployed persons and fresh graduates interested in establishing or expanding their businesses.

Under the initiative, participants will receive entrepreneurship and innovation training through the Dunin-Deshpande Innovation Centre at Queen’s University.

They will also benefit from advisory and mentorship services provided by experts from Leadogo Incorporated and the PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) network.

The programme will offer participants opportunities to pitch their business ideas to potential investors, alongside masterclasses, lecture series and networking opportunities with established entrepreneurs and business leaders.

Successful participants who complete all three courses will receive a Certificate of Specialisation in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, as well as a micro-credential from Queen’s University.

Application requirements and timeline

The programme is open to individuals committed to establishing or scaling up a business. Applicants must have basic English language proficiency and be willing to participate in virtual training sessions.

Registration is free, with tuition fees at Queen’s University and mentorship and coaching fees from Leadogo Incorporated fully covered under the scholarship arrangement.

Applications opened on November 1, 2026, and will close on November 30, 2026.

Successful applicants are expected to register for courses between January 11 and 15, 2027, ahead of lectures and masterclasses scheduled to run from January 18 to August 30, 2027.

The initiative is expected to provide entrepreneurs with access to international expertise, practical business knowledge and potential funding opportunities to support enterprise development and job creation in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Omenaa Mensah unveils modern sport & art campus for Tema youth
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian-Polish philanthropist and entrepreneur Omenaa Mensah has officially opened the Omenaa Sport & Art Campus in Tema, a multidisciplinary facility designed to nurture young talent, support vulnerable children, and serve local communities through sports, education, healthcare, and contemporary art.

The Campus, which opened on October 31, is located next to Kids Haven School, a facility where children who have experienced violence, severe neglect, and forced labour receive care and an opportunity to return to education.

The new complex will provide these children with access to professional sports facilities, contemporary art, healthcare, international creative residencies, and talent development programmes.

Speaking at the opening, Ms Mensah, Founder and President of the Omenaa Foundation, described the project as the fulfilment of a long-held dream to connect her two worlds.

"I am a woman of two worlds. Poland gave me education, opportunities and the strength to pursue my dreams. But Africa is my heart, my soul and my DNA. This is where my roots are, my father’s story and the heritage I have always carried within me," she said. "Omenaa Sport & Art Campus is the fulfilment of that dream. It is a place where love for my roots turns into real opportunities for future generations."

The Campus comprises three main areas: the Gym Center, Community Center, and Art Residence. The Community Center includes the Doctors Rooms medical clinic, PHENOMENAA CAFE, and the TOP CHARITY Creative Lab. It is complemented by sports fields, shared activity spaces, and a sculpture garden.

The Doctors Rooms will provide free paediatric care, diagnostics, and medicines to children from Kids Haven, other residential care facilities in Tema, deaf and hard-of-hearing children, and the wider community, with support from doctors and students from the Medical University of Warsaw.

Omenaa Mensah with traditional authorities and students

The sports fields and Gym Centre are designed to build discipline and confidence, featuring professional training equipment and a physiotherapy room. During the grand opening, children participated in a match alongside Ghanaian football legends Asamoah Gyan, Stephen Appiah, and Emmanuel Agyemang-Badu, as well as Polish sports stars Marcin Gortat and Radosław Majdan. "Ghana has so many talented young people. What matters is giving them the opportunity, encouragement and support to discover what they can do," said Asamoah Gyan.

The opening also featured the inauguration of Omenaa’s Museum of Ghanaian-Polish Relation and its first exhibition, "Common Ground," curated by Azu Nwagbogu and Natalia Bradbury. The exhibition explores memory, identity, cultural heritage, and cooperation across continents, featuring artists from Poland, Ghana, and other African countries. The Art Residence will host workshops led by international artists and vocational courses, including culinary training.

The project was funded through proceeds from TOP CHARITY, an initiative that has raised more than EUR 58 million since 2022 and supported over 300 projects worldwide, alongside business partners including Xtreme Brands, ASTON, DDB Design & Build, Wedel, and Toyota. The Omenaa Foundation also signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II Foundation to collaborate on environmental solutions, heritage restoration, and education in Kumasi and the wider Asante Kingdom.

The event was attended by prominent figures including DJ Cuppy, Pops Mensah-Bonsu, Bola Ray, and Miss Ghana 2026, Rumzia Sule. "I believe that Africa’s future belongs to its young generation. Our task is to give them the tools, the space, and the opportunities to develop their potential. Because every child, no matter where they were born, deserves an equal start in life," Ms Mensah added.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
