In a recent rare media interview, Mr Ajayi acknowledged that the SSS, like any human institution, could make mistakes. He promised, however, that the Service would continue to provide remedies whenever its actions result in injury or injustice.

“Where we admit our mistakes, we offer compensation and seek ways to improve our operations in tandem with the rule of law,” he said.

World.title: The public debt burden in Nigeria, By Umar Yakubu
World.content:
The DMO should publish the external debt stock, loan by loan, with the lender, date, terms and purpose of each facility, and publish the states and amounts involved whenever it restructures the debts of states. Every loan and bond should close with a public completion record that is independent of the agency that spent the money. Bond issuers, the Federal Government included, should publish the projects each issue will fund and report on them until the bond matures, and should not allocate money to works that official records already describe as finished.

Between 30 September 2025 and 31 March 2026, the domestic debt of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) rose from ₦78.93 billion to ₦389.88 billion, according to the Debt Management Office (DMO). That is about ₦311 billion in six months, or roughly ₦1.7 billion a day. The FCT Administration has put the increase down to more infrastructure work. However, there is no document, from the Administration or anyone else, that says who lent it the money, on what terms, with whose approval, or for which projects.

The FCT case is extreme, but it is not unusual. Loans in Nigeria are announced, approved and signed in public, often with a ceremony. What happens to the money afterwards is seldom written down anywhere an ordinary citizen can find it, and in cases like the FCT’s, even the borrowing itself is hard to see. Nigeria borrows in public but accounts for this in private. For most of our debts, the public records stop at the level of approval.

That is not what the law intends. Section 44(1) of the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 says any government in the federation that wants to borrow must specify the purpose of the borrowing and present a cost-benefit analysis detailing its economic and social benefits. If the purpose has to be stated before the loan is taken, there ought to be a record afterwards of whether this was achieved.

At the Center for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity (CeFTPI), we set out to build that record. The result is the Public Debt Integrity, an open database of Nigerian public borrowing and utilisation. The project aims to foster better accountability for public debts, so that every loan can be traced from the point of approval to what it built. It covers the foreign loans and domestic bonds of the Federal Government, the 36 states and the FCT, and ties every grade to the document it rests on. Where the record is silent, the database would say so rather than fill the gap. We would work from the lenders’ own registers, including those of the World Bank and the African Development Bank (AfDB), and from the DMO’s debt reports, bond and Sukuk offer documents, state budgets and audited accounts, and progress records of the Federal Ministry of Works. Each loan is graded by the same test: Does the public record show that the money was used for what it was borrowed for? We count a project as completed only where an independent official record says so. A borrower’s word about its own project is not enough.

Of 448 foreign loans to the Federal Government, the 36 states and the FCT worth $98.75 billion, where a dollar amount is stated, only 138, or 31 per cent have independent records of completion. For 241, or 54 per cent, the use of the money is not established, and 168 of those, worth $23.90 billion, have already ended. On the domestic side, it is worse. Of the 601 projects named in domestic bond and loan documents, 26 have records of completion. A low grade is a statement about the evidence, not about any official’s conduct. A loan graded “INSUFFICIENT” may well have been put to good use, but the trouble is that nobody can show it.

The Shomolu General Hospital in Lagos shows what the gaps look like up close. A Lagos State bond document of May 2023 listed the rehabilitation of the hospital as a ₦18.0 billion project, with nothing paid and the work at 0 per cent complete. The Series IV bond document of 20 November 2025 describes it as a ₦43.56 billion new hospital, with ₦12,001,840,630.57 recorded as paid to date, but the work still at 0 per cent completion. That same bond allocates a further ₦4.89 billion to the project.

The size of the debt makes all this more serious. The total public debt was ₦166.79 trillion on 30 June 2026, up from ₦17.36 trillion at the end of 2016. Some of that increase came from the securitisation of ₦22.71 trillion in Central Bank Ways and Means advances in 2023, and some from the fall of the naira, but most of the rest is new borrowing. Ten states now owe more than a full year’s revenue. Kaduna’s debt stands at 336.7 per cent of its 2025 revenue, and only five states and the FCT are at or below the 50 per cent guideline the Fiscal Responsibility Commission has cited from the DMO.

At the federal level, a $399.5 million loan from the Export-Import Bank of China paid for the National Public Security Communication System in Abuja and Lagos. The loan was fully disbursed and the network was installed from 2011. In July 2023, the Ministry of Police Affairs said the system had been dormant, partly vandalised and would have to be concessioned for repair.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On the Sokoto-Tambuwal-Jega-Kontagora-Makera road, the Ministry of Works records the commissioning and handover of Phases I and II on 25 November 2021. A month later, the 2021 Sukuk prospectus allocated another ₦1.5 billion to Section I of the same road. The prospectus does not say whether that money was meant to settle payments already due on the finished work, and we found no later official record that explains this.

The Loko-Oweto Bridge between Nasarawa and Benue states was dedicated for public use at a virtual commissioning on 23 May 2023. A year later, the Federal Ministry of Works’ scorecard of ongoing projects, dated 27 May 2024, still put the bridge and its approach roads at 95.19 per cent completion. Both records come from government. They cannot both be the full story.

Some debts cannot be traced to loans at all. The DMO’s external debt report of 30 June 2026 lists $912.5 million on four lines that could not be traced, in whole or in large part, to any published loan agreement, purpose or terms. The biggest is the $835.78 million owed to the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), up from $637.82 million three months earlier. Afreximbank had no line of its own in the debt stock at the end of 2025.

Then there is money raised without a list of projects. ₦550 billion of the Federal Government Sukuk, made up of the Works’ share of the 2023 issue and the whole of the 2025 issue, has no published list of the roads it is paying for. Investors who buy a Sukuk are told what assets stand behind it. The citizens who will repay it should be told at least as much.

…the National Assembly and the state houses of assembly should ask to see what earlier loans achieved before they approve new ones. The Fiscal Responsibility Act already requires a stated purpose; lawmakers can reasonably ask whether the last one was met… Nigeria will keep borrowing, as every country does. Borrowing in the name of the public comes with a duty to account to the public, and that duty does not end when the loan agreement is signed.

The size of the debt makes all this more serious. The total public debt was ₦166.79 trillion on 30 June 2026, up from ₦17.36 trillion at the end of 2016. Some of that increase came from the securitisation of ₦22.71 trillion in Central Bank Ways and Means advances in 2023, and some from the fall of the naira, but most of the rest is new borrowing. Ten states now owe more than a full year’s revenue. Kaduna’s debt stands at 336.7 per cent of its 2025 revenue, and only five states and the FCT are at or below the 50 per cent guideline the Fiscal Responsibility Commission has cited from the DMO.

The Center for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity (CeFTPI) wrote twice to the DMO, setting out some of these red flags and asking for clarification. The DMO acknowledged receipt of the correspondence but has not answered the questions asked till now. We are not assuming the worst, and some of these lines may well have ordinary explanations. But the DMO is the office that should be able to tell Nigerians who the country owes, for what, and on what terms.

A few changes would go a long way. The DMO should publish the external debt stock, loan by loan, with the lender, date, terms and purpose of each facility, and publish the states and amounts involved whenever it restructures the debts of states. Every loan and bond should close with a public completion record that is independent of the agency that spent the money. Bond issuers, the Federal Government included, should publish the projects each issue will fund and report on them until the bond matures, and should not allocate money to works that official records already describe as finished.

Finally, the National Assembly and the state houses of assembly should ask to see what earlier loans achieved before they approve new ones. The Fiscal Responsibility Act already requires a stated purpose; lawmakers can reasonably ask whether the last one was met.

Nigeria will keep borrowing, as every country does. Borrowing in the name of the public comes with a duty to account to the public, and that duty does not end when the loan agreement is signed.

Umar Yakubu is the executive director of the Center for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity.

World.title: Nearly 90% of Nigerian Adults Support Methane Emission Cuts – Report
World.content:
Nearly 90 per cent of Nigerian adults support measures to reduce methane emissions, one of the most potent greenhouse gases contributing to global warming, a new survey has found.

The figure represents a 17-percentage-point increase from the 72 per cent recorded in 2024. The survey also found that more than half (53 per cent) of Nigerian adults are very concerned about climate change.

The Global Methane Hub (GMH) commissioned the survey in collaboration with the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication (YPCCC), and it was published on 29 October.

Conducted across Nigeria and 17 other countries, the international survey sought to measure public awareness of climate change and methane emissions, and to examine attitudes towards solutions for reducing methane pollution.

The findings show that concern is even greater regarding immediate environmental threats. About 67 per cent of Nigerian respondents said they were very concerned about poor water quality, while 60 per cent expressed similar concerns about flooding and access to drinking water. Another 55 per cent were very concerned about poor air quality.

Researchers said the findings reflect the growing effects of climate change in Nigeria, where increasingly intense rainfall and flooding are putting communities, infrastructure and water systems at risk.

The findings also reinforce concerns PREMIUM TIMES has repeatedly highlighted about methane emissions across Nigeria’s oil and gas sector and their consequences for the lives and livelihoods of communities in oil-producing areas.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria faces significant methane emission challenges, largely driven by oil and gas production, routine gas flaring, venting and ageing infrastructure. Concerns have also persisted over the enforcement of regulations governing gas flaring and methane emissions.

Methane leaks and routine gas flaring in the Niger Delta have been linked to environmental pollution, contamination of local water sources, damage to farmlands and respiratory health risks.

In Bille, Rivers State, for instance, severe methane bubbling and contamination of water wells have reportedly created acute health and safety concerns for residents.

The continued burning and venting of associated gas also represents a significant economic loss, as billions of cubic feet of gas that could otherwise be captured and commercialised are wasted annually.

Growing environmental concerns

In July, heavy rainfall triggered widespread flooding across parts of Nigeria, including Lagos, as saturated soils increased the risk of flash floods. Authorities also warned that 27 states could be affected.

As the rainy season intensified, authorities subsequently placed 14 states on flood alert, highlighting the growing risks facing communities already struggling with flooding, deteriorating water quality and limited access to safe drinking water.

Methane is a short-lived climate pollutant and one of the most effective targets for slowing global warming in the near term. It is more than 80 times as potent as carbon dioxide over 20 years.

Reducing methane emissions can also deliver significant public health and economic benefits, including improved air quality and reduced pollution exposure.

“As flooding and water challenges put greater pressure on communities across Nigeria, the case for tackling methane is becoming increasingly clear,” said Marcelo Mena, Chief Executive Officer of the Global Methane Hub.

“This survey shows strong and growing support for methane action, with nearly nine in ten Nigerians now supporting efforts to reduce emissions. In the oil and gas sector, for example, cutting methane leaks, venting and flaring reduces pollution and safety risks for nearby communities while helping slow warming.

“It also makes Nigerian oil and gas more competitive, as buyers in markets like Europe increasingly demand lower-methane supply.”

Tengi George-Ikoli, Nigeria Country Manager at the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI), said Nigerians had legitimate reasons to be concerned about methane emissions and their effects on health, the environment and livelihoods.

“Nigerians are right to be concerned about methane emissions and the harm they cause to health, environments and livelihoods,” she said.

“In parts of the Niger Delta, those costs are already being felt, so communities are justified in calling for stronger enforcement of environmental regulations and for clear mechanisms to prevent, mitigate and respond to methane-related harm.

“As Nigeria expands its use of gas, reducing methane emissions must remain a priority to support liveable communities, protect vulnerable populations and help the country meet its climate commitments.”

Anthony Leiserowitz, Director of the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication, said understanding public awareness and perceptions was essential to effective communication and policymaking.

“Understanding what people know and think is essential to effective public communication and policymaking,” he said.

“Methane reduction is one of the fastest ways to limit global warming, making it critical that the public understands both the challenge and the solutions.

“This research helps provide the data needed to identify public knowledge gaps, strengthen communication campaigns, and help informed citizens participate in these climate change solutions.”

Key findings of the survey

The survey found that 69 per cent of Nigerian respondents believe climate change is caused by human activities, while 89 per cent support measures to reduce methane emissions.

It also found that nearly two-thirds (64 per cent) of respondents were familiar with methane.

Oil and gas companies were identified as both significant contributors to climate change and important actors capable of addressing it.

About 57 per cent of respondents ranked oil and gas companies among the three entities most responsible for climate change, while 78 per cent considered them very capable of making meaningful changes.

Nigerians want industries to address climate change

The findings show broad support for reducing methane emissions across the three major sectors responsible for most human-caused methane pollution: agriculture, waste and energy.

In agriculture, 84 per cent of respondents supported efforts to minimise methane emissions, while 88 per cent backed measures to reduce emissions from waste disposal.

Similarly, 88 per cent supported reducing methane emissions from energy production.

Overall, the 89 per cent support for methane reduction matched the proportion of respondents who backed broader climate action.

The report said the findings demonstrate widespread public support for industry-led interventions and stronger environmental protections.

It also noted that Nigerians see corruption as a major obstacle to enforcing environmental regulations effectively.

With strong majorities supporting methane reduction across all three sectors, the report said policymakers and industries have an opportunity to advance solutions that reduce pollution while strengthening environmental accountability.

Global support for methane reduction remains strong

The international survey covered 18 countries across four continents: Brazil, China, Denmark, Ethiopia, Germany, Greece, Indonesia, Italy, Malaysia, Morocco, Nigeria, Paraguay, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and Uruguay.

The online survey gathered responses from 12,189 adults, including at least 700 respondents in Nigeria.

Participants were asked questions about their perceptions of climate change, environmental concerns, awareness of methane emissions and support for specific policies to reduce methane pollution.

Across the countries surveyed, 85 per cent of respondents supported action to reduce methane emissions, indicating widespread international backing for efforts to tackle the pollutant.

Support was particularly strong in Asia, Africa and Latin America, reaching 94 per cent in South Korea, 91 per cent in Malaysia, 90 per cent in China and Brazil, and 89 per cent in Nigeria and South Africa.

The findings also showed that respondents who reported experiencing greater climate change impacts were more likely to support measures to reduce methane emissions.

Across regions, respondents expressed concern about the tangible effects of climate change in their communities, including extreme heat, wildfires, drought, flooding and deteriorating water quality.

Waste emerged as a particularly prominent area for methane reduction in several countries, alongside strong support for interventions in the energy and agriculture sectors.

The report further highlighted public expectations for governments and industries to take greater responsibility for reducing methane emissions.

Why reducing methane is critical to tackling climate change

The report described methane reduction as one of the fastest ways to slow global warming in the near term.

Methane accounts for approximately 30 per cent of the warming experienced since pre-industrial times and is more than 80 times as powerful as carbon dioxide over 20 years.

Unlike carbon dioxide, which can remain in the atmosphere for centuries, most methane breaks down within approximately a decade.

According to the report, cutting human-caused methane emissions by 45 per cent this decade could prevent nearly 0.3 degrees Celsius of warming by 2045, helping to keep international climate commitments within reach.

Reducing methane emissions would also improve air quality, protect agricultural production, create jobs, strengthen food systems, reduce health risks, and improve community resilience.

The report stressed that because methane pollution crosses national borders, coordinated action among governments, businesses, researchers and communities is essential to achieving significant reductions.

Melissa Bell, Senior Vice President of Research at Global Strategy Group, GMH’s research partner, said the consistent findings across countries demonstrated sustained public support for methane reduction.

“The consistency of these findings sends a clear signal: support for reducing methane emissions is strong and sustained,” she said.

“People are concerned about the impacts of climate change, they support action across the major sources of methane emissions, and they expect those with the greatest ability to make a difference to take responsibility.”

Survey methodology

Global Strategy Group conducted the 10-minute online survey between 3 and 25 August 2026. The questionnaire was translated into 13 languages and administered across Europe, South America, Africa and Asia.

Responses were collected from adults aged 18 and above who currently reside in the participating countries and have internet access.

The researchers applied weights for age, gender, geographical location, and education to ensure the samples represented adults with internet access in each country.

At least 700 responses were collected in 15 countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, China, Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea, Morocco, Brazil, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Germany, Greece, Spain, Italy and the United Arab Emirates.

The margin of error was ±3.7 per cent in these countries, except Morocco and Brazil, where it was ±3.6 per cent.

In Ethiopia, Paraguay and Uruguay, at least 400 responses were collected, with margins of error of ±4.9 per cent, ±4.5 per cent and ±3.9 per cent, respectively.

World.title: EFCC uncovers Chinese-operated illegal oil refinery in Ogun
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State, where underground tanks containing substances suspected to be diesel were discovered.

The facility was found deserted when operatives of the commission’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 stormed the premises on Saturday, 31 October, following intelligence gathering and surveillance of suspected illegal sludge oil refining activities.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, the EFCC’s Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale, said the discovery followed the commission’s earlier operation against four illegal lithium processing plants in the area.

Although no operators were found at the facility, EFCC said, operatives discovered waste products from the refining process and underground tanks suspected to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil.

“During the raid, underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing the sludge oil were also discovered. Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement read.

‘How illegal oil refinery worked’

The EFCC said preliminary investigations indicated that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing.

According to the commission, the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through chambers and filters in a process believed to produce diesel for sale in the Nigerian market.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Security personnel at the facility told EFCC operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities nor the name of the company behind the facility,” the Commission said.

It, however, said its operatives had taken over the premises as investigations seek to establish the identities of the alleged operators, the ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities.

The commission also said it was investigating the operation as a suspected case of economic sabotage.

The discovery comes after the EFCC’s earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in Ogere.

The case highlights the involvement of many Chinese nationals in the wideranging illegal activities in the Nigeria’s extractive industry.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the EFCC, on 23 October, arrested 15 people, 14 Chinese nationals and a Nigerian, over alleged illegal lithium-processing operations at four plants in Ogere, Ogun State. It stated that the suspects will be charged to court upon conclusion of investigations.

World.title: Atiku accuses SSS of plot to disrupt Sokoto campaign launch
World.content:
The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, on Tuesday accused the State Security Service (SSS) of recruiting protesters to disrupt his campaign launch in Sokoto on Wednesday.

Addressing journalists, Atiku alleged that the protesters were being assembled to create enough disorder for the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Sokoto State Government to impose a curfew and stop the event.

He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the alleged assembly points and claimed that trucks were transporting protesters to locations including a roundabout.

The protesters, he said, had already begun obstructing traffic, threatening motorists and assaulting some residents.

His campaign spokesperson, Phrank Shaibu, later shared a copy of the address with PREMIUM TIMES and confirmed that it had been delivered by Mr Atiku.

The claims have not been independently verified.

Mr Atiku also accused the state government of blocking the ADC’s access to public facilities and withholding logistical support. He described the alleged restrictions as part of efforts by President Bola Tinubu’s administration to weaken opposition parties before the 2027 elections and warned security agencies against interfering in political activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Despite the alleged obstacles, he said he would attend the launch.

“Our campaign will proceed, and I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state,” he said.

He urged supporters to remain peaceful and called on security agencies to protect residents and participants without favour.

The accusations came a day after the Sokoto State Government announced that it had sealed an ADC campaign office.

The Commissioner for Lands and Housing, Nasiru Dantsoho, said records showed that the building belonged to the defunct Savannah Bank, with no recorded transfer of ownership.

He said the government had written to the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) seeking clarification and, citing a recent confrontation involving political supporters, ordered the premises sealed pending a response. Anyone attempting unauthorised entry, he warned, risked prosecution.

An aide to the ADC governorship candidate confirmed the commissioner’s visit and the government’s enquiry about the building’s occupants, according to a Channels Television report.

Amnesty International also condemned the closure, accusing the state government of using the ownership dispute to restrict opposition activity and undermine freedom of association.

Mr Shaibu disputed the state’s authority to seal the property. He acknowledged that it belonged to Savannah Bank but maintained that the Sokoto State Government had no ownership stake.

Political parties had used the building for about two decades, most recently the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), he said.

Mr Shaibu said he visited the premises on Tuesday morning and found no physical restriction on access.

“As of this morning, when I visited the premises, there was no physical restriction on access. Some minor work was being carried out at the site,” he said.

His account did not establish whether the sealing order had been enforced earlier or whether access had subsequently been restored. The campaign did not provide documents establishing its right to occupy the property.

Mr Shaibu said ADC leaders had reported threats to the police, SSS and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which he said had assured the party that its campaign venue would be protected against interference by the Sokoto Marshals.

He maintained that the Marshals lacked legal authority to close the venue.

Although Atiku accused the SSS leadership of recruiting protesters, Mr Shaibu said the agency was among those approached for protection.

The dispute follows an alleged attack on the convoy of his ADC governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, near the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport on 30 October.

Mr Dan’iya accused personnel of the Sokoto Marshals and the state Community Guard of obstructing his convoy, firing shots and damaging his vehicle.

The Sokoto APC dismissed allegations of politically motivated violence, saying security deployments were linked to preparations for a traditional title conferment ceremony. The Sokoto State Police Command said it was investigating.

The ADC had originally planned to launch its presidential campaign on 31 October before shifting the date to 4 November.

Mr Shaibu said the party was still waiting for its leadership to announce a new venue for Wednesday’s event. He said the delay was deliberate and strategic.

World.title: Google Africa, Microsoft, others to headline DTN@100 national conversation
World.content:
The Managing Director of Google Africa, Alex Okosi, and Microsoft’s Chief Growth and AI Officer for the Middle East and Africa, Olatomiwa Williams, are among five prominent industry leaders scheduled to headline the National Conversation at the Times Heroes Award, the flagship event of the Daily Times Nigeria @100 Centenary Celebration.

Other panellists are technology entrepreneur and Founding Partner of Future Africa, Iyinoluwa Aboyeji; media entrepreneur and storyteller, Chude Jideonwo; and Founder and Creative Director of Africa Soft Power Group, Nkiru Balonwu.

The National Conversation, themed ‘Shaping the Future’, is scheduled for Tuesday at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos.

The event will also be streamed live on ARISE TV at about 5 p.m., while tickets are available through MyLagosApp.

Innovation, AI, digital economy

The discussion is expected to bring together perspectives from technology, media, business and the creative economy.

The conversations will centre on Nigeria’s next century, including innovation, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, youth development, and nation-building.

Experts profiles

Mr Okosi, who has more than two decades of experience in the media, entertainment, and technology industries, previously held senior positions at Viacom International Media Networks and YouTube, where he worked to expand opportunities for African creators. At Google, he leads initiatives focused on digital access, innovation and business growth across the continent.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Williams, also an experienced technology executive, has spent more than 20 years in information technology, digital transformation and business leadership.

She previously served as Country General Manager for Microsoft Nigeria and Ghana before assuming her current role, which focuses on growth and artificial intelligence initiatives across Microsoft’s Middle East and Africa Growth Markets. She also founded the Uzemi Technology Empowerment Initiative, which promotes women’s leadership in technology.

Mr Aboyeji is known for co-founding Andela and Flutterwave, two African technology companies that have attracted significant international investment. Through Future Africa, he supports and invests in African entrepreneurs developing solutions to challenges across the continent.

Mr Jideonwo, a lawyer, journalist, filmmaker and media entrepreneur, co-founded RED | For Africa, which built YNaija and The Future Awards Africa. He also hosts the interview platform #WithChude, where he explores personal experiences, resilience and transformation through conversations with public figures.

Ms Balonwu brings more than 25 years of experience spanning government, finance, technology, law, telecommunications and the creative industries. She founded Africa Soft Power Group, an initiative focused on strengthening Africa’s influence in global conversations around business, culture, investment and development.

Her work in the space dates back to 2017, when she established African Women on Board, an organisation focused on leadership, governance and women’s participation. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she expanded the initiative through the Africa Soft Power Project, creating a platform that connects policymakers, business leaders, academics, entrepreneurs and creatives.

The project has since evolved into an annual international gathering, with previous editions held in Kigali, Rwanda, before moving to Nairobi, Kenya, in 2025. Its 2026 edition marks its seventh year.

Ms Balonwu has also served as chief executive officer of Spinlet, a music streaming platform, and was the inaugural lecturer in Gender and Law at the University of Lagos. She currently advises the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria.

Times Heroes Award

The National Conversation is described as the intellectual centrepiece of the DTN@100 Times Heroes Award, organised by Folio Communications.

It is expected to provide a platform for discussions on the opportunities and challenges that will shape Nigeria’s development over the next century.

The Times Heroes Award forms part of the activities marking 100 years of the Daily Times Nigeria, Africa’s oldest surviving newspaper, and its contribution to journalism and national development.

World.title: Gov Soludo speaks on rift with Peter Obi, predicts 2027 result
World.content:
Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State said he and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, are great friends despite their political differences and ongoing rift.

Mr Soludo, who had been in a prolonged face-off with Mr Obi, spoke in an interview with BBC Igbo on Monday.

“Peter Obi and I are big friends. Even his family and my family are close.

“His wife is my child’s baptismal godmother while my wife is his child’s confirmation godmother,” he said.

The Anambra governor, who spoke largely in Igbo, stressed that his rift with the NDC candidate was completely political.

“When we talk of our political differences, everyone has their interests. We’re doing politics,” he stated.

Mr Soludo, a former governor of CBN, then recalled that when he was the APGA governorship candidate for the 2021 Anambra governorship election, which he won, Mr Obi had supported Oselake Obaze, the then PDP candidate.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“He (Obi) had a different vision. He had someone he believed was the right person to become governor of Anambra State.

“I was also seeking to be governor then, but he supported who he wanted as governor. However, I prevailed by the grace of God. And I don’t hold it against him,” he said.

Why Obi can’t defeat Tinubu in 2027

In late 2022, Mr Soludo predicted that Mr Obi, then Labour Party presidential candidate, would not win the 2023 presidential election, citing “lack of political structure” and poor voting strength of the South-east, where he hails from.

Speaking in an interview with the BBC, the Anambra governor said he stood by his words.

He suggested it would be much harder to defeat President Bola Tinubu in the forthcoming 2027 election because of incumbency advantage.

Mr Tinubu, who defeated Mr Obi in the 2023 election, is seeking re-election on the All Progressives Congress (APC) platform.

“If you didn’t disarm a warrior while he was lying down, you wouldn’t do so while he was standing,” Mr Soludo said, suggesting that Mr Obi was unlikely to defeat Mr Tinubu now, having not done so in 2023 when the president was not in power.

“Even if he has united opposition, it does not guarantee that he will defeat an incumbent (President Tinubu),” he added.

The Anambra governor argued that the low South-east voting strength meant that Mr Obi needed to collaborate with other regions to become president.

“I was the one who asked him to come to pick the APGA presidential ticket in early March 2022.

“That was before he contested for president in 2023. But asking him to pick the party’s ticket didn’t mean he was going to win. It was for us to use the avenue to unite Igbo people.

“When we are united, you can then go into alliance with other regions to seek power,” he stated.

World.title: Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was reportedly left distraught and broke down in tears in the dressing room after the accidental collision that preceded the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, with teammates rallying around him to offer support.

According to The Sun UK, the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international was seen praying and crying following the incident during Monday’s Segunda División match between Tenerife and Andorra.

Owono’s knee struck De Miguel’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball in the closing stages of the encounter. The 30-year-old striker was left motionless on the pitch, prompting distress among players, some of whom were reportedly seen in tears.

The goalkeeper was shown a straight red card before the referee abandoned the match in second-half stoppage time.

De Miguel was taken to hospital after reportedly suffering a cardiac arrest on the way, with paramedics said to have resuscitated him. Tenerife initially described his condition as “stable but serious” on Monday night, but he died on Tuesday morning.

The Sun, citing Spanish newspaper AS, reported that Andorra players showed great concern for Owono during their journey back from Tenerife, with the goalkeeper visibly shaken by the tragedy.

Journalist Ivan Alvarez also told COPE radio that Owono had intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before learning of his death.

The goalkeeper has reportedly deactivated his social media accounts since the incident and is said to be seeking an opportunity to offer his condolences to the bereaved family before making a public statement.

Meanwhile, a judge is expected to open an investigation into De Miguel’s death, although a Canary Islands court source described the incident as an “accidental collision on the playing field”.

The source explained that a judicial investigation is automatically opened in cases of deaths not resulting from natural causes, including accidents.

Owono is not expected to face criminal sanctions, according to the report, although he could still face sporting disciplinary action.

De Miguel’s partner, Maria, and their one-year-old daughter, Carla, were reportedly watching from the stands when the incident

occurred.

Tenerife have expressed their grief over the striker’s death, while UEFA has announced that a moment of silence will be observed at all its matches this week in his memory.

Vanguard News

World.title: DSS DG frees four suspected IPOB members, pays N20m compensation
World.content:
The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DGSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi has set free and approved an initial payment of N20 million to four suspects, out of which, each suspect is to receive five million Naira as compensation after being cleared of alleged membership of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB).

Security sources disclosed that the suspects; Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022, in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State.

“The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” disclosed one of the sources.

While receiving the four, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, Counsel to the suspects, commended the Service for their relentless efforts towards safeguarding Nigeria’s security, particularly acknowledging the DGSS’ genuine attempt at upholding human rights.

Furthermore, he noted the high level of hygiene and professionalism within the Service, being the best he has witnessed in over 20 years of interacting with DSS personnel. He reiterated his earlier public statement that President Tinubu made the right choice in appointing Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi as DSS DG.

Expressing gratitude to the DSS boss, Emele Uduma Ibe who spoke on behalf of others, described the day as the happiest of his life, noting that the experience had taught him a valuable lesson which he would share with others. He offered prayers for God’s continued blessings upon the DSS boss and the management of the Service.

Recall that upon assuming office in 2024, the DG ordered a review of over 300 inherited terrorism cases. Currently, the DSS panel has been able to decongest its facility to about 100 after thorough investigations, paying over a billion naira in compensation.

The DSS boss awarded N20 million and covered the medical bills of a Jos based businessman, who was shot erroneously by service personnel in Plateau State. Chineze Ozoadibe was also compensated with N10 million after she was wrongfully arrested, Sunday Ifedi who was also compensated with 10 million naira after investigation cleared him of ties with IPOB, likewise Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor was also paid N5 million after investigation absolved him of IPOB allegations.



This is aside other numerous cases that the DSS has handled quietly which never made news outside the Agency.

“Like other compensated suspects, the DSS will also offer psychological, medical support to these four in addition the initial amount given,” I’m confident the DSS will also help further reintegration into the society, revealed a source.

The DG- DSS in a recent maiden media interview admitted that, as humans, the DSS is prone to mistakes. However, where there is injury, Mr Ajayi said there must be remedy. “Where we admit our mistakes, we offer compensation, and seek ways to improve operations in tandem with the rule of law,”

World.title: 2027: Why youth share of voters dropped – INEC
World.content:
INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan

….As UniJos wins campus debate finale

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why youths now make up 29.79 per cent of the voters’ register being prepared for the 2027 general election, down from 39.65 per cent in the 2023 register.

Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, gave the explanation on Tuesday at the grand finale of the INEC Campus Debate at the Law Theatre of the University of Abuja.

He said the drop does not mean fewer young people are interested in elections, but that many who counted as youths in 2023 have simply grown older.

“Some questions have been asked, why has the number reduced compared to what we have in 2023? But the truth of the matter is that there has been progressive migration of the categories of persons that were youth in 2023, they have now migrated into different age groups”, Amupitan explained.

He said the register, “which is currently being reviewed through claims and objection,” puts youth representation at 29.79 per cent. The 2023 register had 37,060,399 youths aged 18 to 34, or 39.65 per cent of the 93.4 million registered voters.

Amupitan said the debate was part of the commission’s effort to confront voter apathy among young people. “Our plan is to catch them young,” he said.

He said earlier outings showed how little many young people know about the electoral process. “When they ask who is the INEC chairman, unfortunately none of them could get it,” he said.

The University of Jos won the final, which was held under the theme “Nigeria’s Electoral Process and Democracy.” Bayero University, Kano, came second, the University of Ibadan third, and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, fourth.

Amupitan, who is a University of Jos alumnus, said the judges’ decision could not be faulted. “From the quality of the debate, it was, honestly, it could go either way and they have done justice to it,” he said.

He said the judges took a long time to compute the scores. “They were also trying to use technology with their phone making some computations and arithmetics just to ensure that there is accurate delivery,” he said.

Amupitan said the result was so clear that no debater or university should think of going to court. “It will be needless for any of the parties or debaters to think of going to court. So that is why we are not establishing any election petition, any tribunal to review what has been done,” he said light-heartedly.

He also told the Director of Voter Education and Publicity to keep track of the finalists, saying he would have employed them immediately if the law allowed.

“They are not qualified to have been given automatic employment, if not I will have done that by now,” he said. He added that they must first graduate and complete the National Youth Service Corps NYSC.

He noted that a debater from Bayero University, Kano, studies medicine, while the two debaters from the University of Jos study law.

The INEC chairman told the audience that elections under his watch have shown improvement. “I am just one year 10 days in office,” he said, adding that the commission had conducted four off-cycle elections: the Anambra governorship election, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) area council elections in February, the Ekiti governorship election in June and the Osun governorship election in August.

“Go back to history, Anambra election and Osun election used to be inconclusive. But under our watch, we have ensured to a large extent that those elections are conclusive”, he said.

On women’s participation, he said the commission has a gender and inclusivity department. He noted that Belgium requires equality in the occupation of political offices, “but we don’t have such a law in Nigeria yet.”

To the finalists, he said: “You have spoken with conviction, with candor and with discipline.”

The Vice Chancellor of the University of Abuja, Professor Hakeem Babatunde Fawehinmi, urged young Nigerians to collect their voter cards, turn out to vote and hold leaders accountable.

He commended INEC for the initiative and said debate teaches young people to manage disagreement. “It can be argued that debate is the opposite of violence,” he said.

World.title: Reps probe Ebola preparedness, prisons seek emergency funding
World.content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives has commenced an assessment of Nigeria’s preparedness against the Ebola Virus Disease, as the Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) called for dedicated emergency funding, medical equipment and improved healthcare facilities in custodial centres to prevent a possible outbreak.

The Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Nwakuche, made the call on Tuesday at a one-day public hearing organised by the joint House Committees on Infectious Diseases, Healthcare Services, Aviation and Interior at the National Assembly, Abuja.

Nwakuche said custodial centres were particularly vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks because of overcrowding, shared facilities, frequent human interaction and varying levels of healthcare infrastructure.

He warned that an outbreak in correctional facilities could have serious consequences for inmates, personnel, visitors and surrounding communities.

The Controller-General said the Correctional Service needed to be formally integrated into national and sub-national public health emergency preparedness and response frameworks, particularly those addressing infectious disease outbreaks.

“Effective prevention and containment of Ebola Virus Disease within custodial centres require adequate protective equipment, medical supplies, trained personnel and emergency response facilities,” he said.

He identified personal protective equipment, hand sanitisers, disinfectants, screening equipment, ambulances and designated isolation spaces as essential requirements for preventing and controlling infections in custodial facilities.

Nwakuche also called for dedicated emergency response funding to support disease surveillance, medical interventions, procurement of essential supplies and regular training of correctional personnel.

He said the Service was committed to collaborating with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, state ministries of health and other relevant agencies to strengthen surveillance, testing, referrals and emergency response.

He further recommended periodic assessments of custodial facilities to determine their level of preparedness and compliance with infection prevention and control standards.

Declaring the hearing open, Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, said the recent confirmation of an imported Ebola case in Nigeria underscored the need for sustained vigilance, stressing that public health security was inseparable from national security.

Abbas said although the Federal Government had activated emergency response mechanisms, strengthened surveillance and contact tracing, and established a Presidential Task Force, the measures should not result in complacency.

He noted that the evacuation of the confirmed imported case and the absence of established onward transmission should strengthen the country’s resolve to prevent a recurrence.

The Speaker recalled that the 2014 Ebola outbreak demonstrated how early detection, decisive intervention and effective coordination could determine whether an outbreak was contained or escalated into a national health emergency.

He said the public hearing was designed to assess the adequacy of Nigeria’s disease surveillance systems, laboratory capacity, isolation facilities, emergency response infrastructure and availability of protective equipment for healthcare workers.

The lawmakers are also expected to examine screening arrangements at airports and other entry points, inter-agency coordination, utilisation of emergency health funds and the preparedness of state governments.

Abbas stressed that disease containment should not be left to the Federal Government alone, saying all tiers of government must understand and fulfil their responsibilities during public health emergencies.

He also cautioned against misinformation, urging public institutions to provide Nigerians with accurate, timely and consistent information during health emergencies.

The Speaker, however, clarified that there were no active cases of Ebola Virus Disease in Nigeria at the time of the hearing, adding that the exercise was not intended to create public panic but to strengthen confidence through preparedness, transparency and accountability.

He assured that the House would consider recommendations from the hearing and pursue legislative interventions where necessary.

Earlier, Chairman of the Joint Committee on Infectious Diseases, Amobi Godwin Ogah, said the hearing followed a resolution of the House arising from a motion he sponsored on the need for the Executive to strengthen preventive and emergency medical measures against the spread of Ebola.

Ogah said reports of the outbreak in October had generated fear and apprehension among Nigerians, particularly in view of the country’s experience during the 2014 outbreak.

He recalled that the previous outbreak had taken a physical, psychological and economic toll on the country, claiming the lives of several prominent Nigerians.

He said the House had initiated consultations to establish the level of preparedness of relevant government agencies, particularly in screening travellers arriving in and departing from the country through airports.

Ogah commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for establishing a Presidential Task Force on the Ebola outbreak and releasing N10 billion to support containment efforts.

He also praised the NCDC for coordinating efforts to prevent the spread of the disease.

The committee chairman expressed optimism over reports that two additional suspected cases identified in the North-East had tested negative for Ebola, describing the development as encouraging for the country’s containment efforts.

He said the hearing would enable ministries, departments, agencies, development partners and other stakeholders to explain measures already taken and identify additional steps required to protect Nigerians.

World.title: Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The Ondo State Police Command has uncovered a suspected counterfeit dollar printing operation in Odigbo Local Government Area, arresting one suspect and recovering three bags of suspected fake United States dollar notes.

The operation followed an investigation into an alleged $6,000 currency fraud involving a businessman in Okitipupa.

The police said the case began after Yusuf Nasiru, of Sabo, Okitipupa, lodged a complaint on October 28, 2026, alleging that two men, Peter Desmond and Olami Toro, both from Ode-Irele, approached him at his shop on October 25 to exchange dollars for naira.

According to the complainant, he handed over $6,000, valued at about N8.6 million, to the men.

However, while waiting for the naira equivalent, the suspects allegedly returned the dollars, claiming they did not have enough money to complete the transaction, before leaving.

Nasiru later discovered that the returned notes were counterfeit and reported the matter to the police.

The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said operatives of the Okitipupa Division commenced an investigation following receipt of the complaint.

He said intelligence gathering and technical tracking led the operatives to one of the suspects, Peter Desmond, at Kiniso Village, via Ajue, in Odigbo LGA.

“Acting on credible intelligence from community members, operatives raided the hideout on October 29, 2026, believed to be used for producing and printing counterfeit dollar notes to defraud unsuspecting members of the public,” Abayomi said.

He disclosed that one suspect was arrested during the raid, while other occupants of the premises escaped through a perimeter fence.

A search of the premises, he said, led to the recovery of three bags containing suspected counterfeit US dollar notes and a small wooden box, which had been taken into police custody as exhibits.

Abayomi added that the arrested suspect had provided useful information to assist the ongoing investigation.

He said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, had directed that the investigation be intensified to apprehend other suspects, establish the full extent of the alleged criminal network and prosecute those found culpable.

The command cautioned residents against engaging in suspicious foreign currency transactions with unverified individuals or accepting seemingly attractive exchange offers outside authorised channels.

It also advised members of the public to authenticate foreign currencies before accepting them and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station.

The police assured residents of their commitment to combating financial crimes and protecting lives and property across the state.

World.title: Nigeria’s exports rise 25% in two years — NPA
World.content:
Nigerian Ports Authority.

By Godwin Oritse

The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators.

The Managing Director of NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, disclosed this while speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH).

He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports.

Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials.

“Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said.

He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals.

The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes.

He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment.

Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries.

He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation.

The NPA managing director also attributed Nigeria’s improved performance in global port rankings to increased efficiency, technology adoption and collaboration with industry stakeholders.

He said two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking.

Dantsoho further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, alongside an increase in cargo volumes.

He said the authority was monitoring port performance across West and Central Africa through a regional dashboard, adding that the data showed improvements in Nigeria’s port efficiency as well as progress in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya.

According to him, the NPA plans to sustain partnerships with major industry players in countries including Morocco and South Africa to improve port operations and regional trade.

On infrastructure development, Dantsoho said the Federal Government was planning to invest $1 billion in the expansion and modernisation of Apapa Port as part of its medium- to long-term strategy.

He said the project would require substantial private-sector participation, adding that the NPA was working with APM Terminals and other investors to mobilise the required capital.

The authority was also pursuing technology partnerships to improve port operations, he said.

Dantsoho disclosed that the NPA had partnered with a Singaporean firm to develop a single-window system, while discussions were ongoing with a company from Abu Dhabi to develop a port community system.

He said the initiatives were expected to improve coordination among port stakeholders, simplify processes and enhance efficiency.

World.title: Ondo Amotekun arrests 301 suspects, deploys 1,200 officers
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun, says it arrested 301 suspected kidnappers and other criminals between August and October 2026.

The State Commander, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, disclosed this while parading 15 suspects, including those allegedly involved in the abduction of a poultry farmer, Afolabi Ajayi, in Imafon community, Akure North Local Government Area, and the killing of a woman.

Adeleye also announced the launch of Operation Laafia DanDan, a security initiative aimed at tackling criminal activities during the ember months and yuletide.

He said the corps had secured the conviction of 27 suspects, who were either serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions attached to options of fines.

“Across the board, within these months under review, we arrested 301 suspects. Out of these 301 suspects, we have secured conviction of 27 serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions for those that have option of fine.

“Using alternative dispute resolution on many cases, we were able to resolve 102 cases,” he said.

Adeleye attributed the achievements to the support of Amotekun ambassadors across the 18 local government areas, intelligence officers, local task forces, vigilantes and personnel of the corps.

He said the agency was winding down its previous operation to begin full deployment for the ember months, with intelligence-led surveillance across the state, particularly on major highways, in urban centres and forest reserves.

According to him, the new operation will feature increased patrols by Amotekun Rangers in forests, as well as electronic and physical monitoring of identified crime-prone locations.

“We have redesigned a scheme whereby we will have a different operation for this period to guarantee safety of lives and property in Ondo State and for those commuting.

“We want to reassure the public that the state remains safe as we are determined to continue 24/7 patrol across all major roads, forest reserves and the metropolis,” he said.

The commander disclosed that about 1,200 personnel would be deployed across the 18 local government areas, with particular attention to border communities and routes.

He also presented a kidnap victim who was recently rescued without payment of ransom.

Adeleye said the corps had commenced training and retraining of personnel on arrest procedures and prosecution, adding that suspects whose investigations had been concluded would be charged to court.

On the 15 suspects paraded, he said four were arrested for alleged violations of the state’s anti-grazing law, two for breach of law and order, while nine were arrested in connection with kidnapping.

He said three suspects linked to the abduction of poultry farmer Ajayi and the killing of the woman had been arrested, adding that they were identified by the victim and had allegedly confessed to the offences.

Other suspects, according to him, included individuals linked to a kidnapping incident in Ore, Ondo State, about two months ago, and a 22-year-old man identified as Mohammed, arrested over an alleged kidnapping case in Alagbaka.

Adeleye said two other suspects, Usman and Suleiman, were arrested for alleged violations of the anti-grazing law.

He added that Peter, 26, Lawal, 26, and Gabriel were arrested over alleged burglary and stealing, while a 40-year-old suspect was accused of specialising in stealing television sets and mobile phones. Recovered items were also displayed.

The commander further said four suspects — Dada, 26, Seyi, 24, Hassan, 22, and Sunday, 19 — were arrested while allegedly removing roofing materials from government schools in Ile-Oluji and Elegbeka.

Adeleye urged residents to provide timely information to security agencies to support efforts to prevent crime and protect lives and property.

World.title: Okorocha to Uzodimma: Stop insulting judges, appeal up to the Supreme Court
World.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA — A former governor of Imo State, Rochas Okorocha, whom the court recently declared the authentic candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 senatorial election in Imo West, has warned his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, to stop what he described as unwarranted attacks on judges.

Okorocha, who spoke at the Federal High Court premises in Abuja after signing processes at the registry in connection with the ongoing legal dispute over the senatorial ticket, urged Governor Uzodimma to exercise his right of appeal, even up to the Supreme Court.

He also called on the governor to restrain his supporters, whom he accused of continuing to denigrate the judiciary over a lost case.

He said: “I listened to the news yesterday and it was so horrible, so terrible, that Governor Hope’s aides, namely his Deputy Chief of Staff and the National Vice Chairman of the APC, could berate a judge, insult a judge.

“To use his words, he said the judgment was rubbish and procured, and that the judge should go and look at himself in the mirror. I think that is terrible. And the other one, who is called his Deputy Chief of Staff and whose wife is even a judge, could be insulting the judge because of a judgment.

“So, it means that whenever the judgment is for Hope, it is good, but whenever it is against him, the Judiciary is evil.

“I think this is very uncivilized. I want him to caution his attack dogs and his people to refrain from insulting judges. It doesn’t represent this nation well, and I feel particularly hurt.

“I was made to understand that he has called all his aides, commissioners and everybody to go on the attack. You see, they are doing all that. Can’t he wait patiently and try to get the appeal through? At least the Supreme Court is there.

“So it is very shocking and very surprising. I don’t know what they expected: that the judge should have said that the election was held on the 16th for Hope, when the actual date is the 18th?

“Or that he would have said that Hope emerged by consensus, which is not true? Or the paper signed only by the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) of Imo State and sent to the National Chairman, saying that it was by consensus and that Hope’s election took place two days before the time?

“I don’t understand what their quarrel is all about. I want to say once more: let us protect the sanctity of the Judiciary and let us allow justice to prevail in all matters. Hope has been a very big and unusual beneficiary of the court, and I think he should have respected it.”

Okorocha challenged Uzodimma to fault his claims in public rather than attacking judges and the Judiciary, adding: “If you (Uzodimma) think any of the things I am saying is not true and that the judgment is not true, Hope should come on television or come and speak.

“Why is he (Uzodimma) hiding and using attack dogs here and there to attack judges? That is very bad, and that shows what it means.”

While accusing Governor Uzodimma of allegedly presenting forged documents during the hearing of the case, Okorocha expressed optimism that he would also win at the appellate court.

He said: “In fact, if you look at the documents certified by INEC, according to Hope, and look at the inconsistencies and irregularities, then you could say that even the judge has no choice. Even a judge who wants to do wrong cannot do wrong in this case.”

He also hailed the judiciary, which he said had served justice in the matter.

“I salute the Nigerian Judiciary, honestly. Whatever you might say, they’re still very good. And I believe that the right thing should be done.”

It will be recalled that the Federal High Court in Abuja on October 29 nullified the emergence of Governor Uzodimma as candidate of the APC for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027.

The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodimma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by INEC.

According to the court, it was the former governor, Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party.

Consequently, it ordered INEC to recognise Senator Okorocha forthwith and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll.

The court further issued an order barring Governor Uzodimma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election.

World.title: Atiku Decries Intimidation of ADC Members, Denial of Using Public Facilities for Campaigns in Sokoto
World.content:
*Vows to address rally in Sokoto Wednesday

*PDP chairmen petition IG over harassment by APC govs

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Former Vice President and the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar has decried the violence and political intimidation of members of his party in Sokoto State by the state government as well as refusal of the use of public facilities for rallies and campaigns.

He vowed that irrespective of the actions of security agencies and the state government denial of public facilities for campaigns and rallies that he will address a rally in Sokoto State in Wednesday.

He also accused the leadership of the Department of State Security of recruiting thugs to obstruct ADC campaigns in Sokoto State

This is coming as the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP States chairmen has petitioned Police Inspector General over Intimidation and Harassment by APC Governors

Addressing a press conference Tuesday in Abuja, the former vice president said, “I address you today with a heavy but resolute heart. What is unfolding in Sokoto is not ordinary political competition. It is a calculated campaign to frustrate the African Democratic Congress, obstruct our campaign and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose.”

According to Atiku, “Public facilities that should be available to every political party for legitimate campaign activities have been blocked. Logistical support has been withheld. These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field.

“More disturbing still, the information available to us is that the leadership of the Department of State Services is recruiting people to stage protests in Sokoto. The objective is to create disorder, give the APC controlled state government a pretext to impose a curfew and prevent our campaign take off from holding as scheduled.

“We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road. Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade.”

He continued, “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis. I call on every officer involved to stop immediately and return to the constitutional duty of impartial service.”, Atiku stated

Blaming the current administration for this breach of peace, Atiku said, “For three and a half years, the Tinubu administration has devoted too much energy to weakening credible opposition and too little to solving the problems facing Nigerians. It has pursued a politics of absorption and intimidation, while drawing former opposition figures into the APC and narrowing the space for political competition. The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one party state in all but name.

“The government is afraid of the people’s verdict. It has unleashed a crushing cost of living crisis and now appears determined to frustrate Nigerians’ democratic right to choose a different path. Food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials have become unaffordable for millions. Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive. That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.

“I will make life affordable again. We will support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. We will pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, so that support reaches consumers through measurable relief while also strengthening domestic industry. Nigerians deserve policies that put food on the table, restore opportunity and make daily life manageable again.

“The APC has still not recovered from the abysmal failure of its last rally in Kaduna. It should have taken that as a warning that Nigerians are withdrawing their confidence. Instead, it has chosen intimidation and obstruction. These are the last kicks of a dying horse. The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence”, he said .

The ADC Presidential candidate said that “The 2027 general election will be a defining moment in our democratic history. This is more than a contest between parties or candidates. It is a choice between a government that has shown indifference to people’s suffering and Nigerians who have endured enough and want their votes to count.

“The ADC will resist every gimmick, administrative roadblock and underhand manoeuvre designed to exclude the opposition or impose a one party reality on Nigeria. We will not be intimidated into silence or irrelevance. Our campaign will proceed, and I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state.

“I call on the people of Sokoto to remain calm and peaceful. Do not allow anyone to provoke you or turn a political gathering into a security crisis. I also urge the security agencies to protect commuters, residents and rally participants without favour. The authorities must ensure that our rally can hold peacefully and without interference.”

According to Atiku, “To the voters of Nigeria, remain resolute. Stand your ground. Democratic freedom is not a gift from any government. It is your right. Do not allow anyone to intimidate you or checkmate your will.

“As the Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, I give you my word: I will lead this campaign and I will not abandon the field. We will confront every attempt to restrict democratic participation with firmness, organisation and faith in the Nigerian people.

“The ADC will stand with officers who refuse to be used against democracy and who remain faithful to the Constitution. Those who choose to betray their duty and collude in the suppression of political freedom will be held accountable under the law.

“Nigeria belongs to its people, not to any party or temporary occupant of power. We will defend that truth and the people’s right to choose.

Meanwhile , the chairman of the PDP states chairman’s forum, Austin Nwachukwu said at a meeting with the party’s National Working Committee, NWC at the PDP National Secretariat that the APC governors are intimidating and harassing members of the party in their states

According to Nwachukwu, “l just want to use opportunity to also bring to the notice of our National Working Committee that some states in the country, especially where we don’t have APC governors, are very antagonistic to our candidates and members.

“We have painstakingly produced very good candidates for the forthcoming elections and this is not going well with the governors of some states.

“For example, last week, the forum leadership was forced to go to Ebonyi State to address a draconian issue that have been brewing there, where intimidation, harassment, arrest, killings have become the order of the day, under the watch of the governor of Ebonyi state, His Excellency, Governor Nwifuru.

“We made a presentation, and with me here is a copy of the petition that we’re unfolding to the Inspector General of Police today, and to other relevant security agencies, the killings and harassment of our candidates and governorship candidate, especially in various states of the country, must stop.”, the chairman of the PDP states chairmen forum stated

He said that “the forum will not take it lightly anymore if any of our candidates are harassed, intimidated, or killed because of mere elections. It’s a contest. Winner must emerge.

“So on that notes, my colleagues, on the National Working Committee, I want to welcome all of us to this meeting and wish us a very happy deliberations. Thank you.

Thank you very much, Chairman”, Nwachukwu stated

The national chairman of the party, Abdulrahman Mohammed assured that the party will look into their petition.

He also assured the states chairmen of the party that the PDP is very much in the party as all their candidates have been recognised by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC

He boasted that the party nominated candidates at all levels that are capable of winning any election.

World.title: DSS Says Sowore’s Bid to Make Its Lawyer Witness in Alleged Cyberbullying Trial Dilatory, Judge Fixes Ruling for Nov 9
World.content:
The Department of State Services (DSS), on Tuesday, told the Federal High Court in Abuja that the bid by African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, to turn its lead counsel, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, into his witness, is the politician’s ploy to delay his trial for allegedly cyberbullying President Bola Tinubu.

The DSS told the court that the subpoena Sowore issued on its lead counsel was in bad faith and strange in law and in criminal trial. Under Section 192 of the Evidence Act, stated the lawyer, no legal practitioner is permitted to disclose any communication made to him in the course of his engagement unless with the consent of his client.

The DSS added that Sowore’s subpoena was an abuse of court process calculated to annoy and irritate its lead counsel.

The submission by the DSS came as the trial judge, Justice Mohammed Garba Umar, fixed November 9, to deliver ruling on Sowore’s

application.

The judge fixed the date after taking arguments for and against the application by counsel on both sides.

At Tuesday’s proceedings, Kenneth Cyril-Ita, who represented the DSS, asked the court to set aside the subpoena issued against Kehinde, SAN, by Sowore seeking to turn the DSS lead lawyer into a witness in the trial.

Sowore, through his lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide Fusika, SAN, had served a subpoena on the DSS lead counsel to appear in court to give evidence in respect of the trial of the defendant for allegedly cyberbullying President Tinubu.

In his motion on notice against the execution of the subpoena, Cyril-Ita told the Court that the evidence sought to be given through the subpoena witness is irrelevant to Sowore’s alleged cyberbullying trial. Contrary to Sowore’s claim, the DSS lawyer said there was no application before the Court to suspend or adjourn the trial till 2027.

“By not setting aside the subpoena, the Court is being invited to deprive the Federal Republic of Nigeria, a counsel of its choice in the prosecution of the matter as counsel cannot be a witness and counsel at the same time in the same matter,” he stated.

“The evidence of whether the Complainant will ask for adjournment or not in the matter as shown in the publication sought to be tendered is a matter allegedly caught by section 83(3) of the Evidence Act,” he continued.

He, therefore, urged Justice Umar to set aside the subpoena and direct Sowore to continue his defence in the charges against him.

In his argument, Ruben Adakole, who represented Sowore, asked the Court to uphold the subpoena against the DSS lead counsel as requested by the defendant to make him his witness.

Thereafter, Justice Umar adjourned to November 9, to deliver his decision on the matter.

World.title: 2027: Obi Warns Govs Against Electoral Manipulation, Says Nigerians Will Resist Rigging
World.content:
• Accuses governors of prioritising political survival over performance

• Insists leadership must be earned through service, not intimidation

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja
