The Peter Obi Media Office has warned state governors against alleged attempts to manipulate the 2027 general election, declaring that Nigerians will resist any process that undermines the credibility of the polls.

The media office, which accused some governors of allegedly working behind the scenes to compromise the democratic process, said political leaders should focus on presenting their records of performance rather than seeking to retain power through electoral manipulation.

It maintained that any electoral process that failed to meet the standards of freedom, fairness and transparency would be rejected by Nigerians, who, it said, were determined to exercise their democratic rights.

In a statement issued Tuesday by its spokesman, Indris Zekeri Jnr, the Peter Obi Media Office said governors should recognise that political leadership is a privilege earned through service and not an entitlement to be retained through deceit, intimidation or interference with elections.

The statement, titled, ‘Nigerians Will Choose the Best Product in the Marketplace,’ accused some governors of becoming increasingly desperate as the 2027 general election approaches.

“Instead of presenting their records of service, performance and achievements, they are turning to electoral manipulation and safeguards for rigging,” the statement alleged.

It warned that attempts to undermine the democratic process would not permanently suppress the will of the electorate, insisting that Nigerians had become increasingly determined to reject leaders they considered undeserving of another mandate.

Part of the statement read: “The 2027 election will be a defining moment for our nation. Nigerians are resolved to reclaim their country through the power of their votes.

“Let it be known that no degree of rigging, intimidation or political manoeuvring can permanently silence the will of the people.”

The media office further argued that political leaders should be judged by their records and capacity to address the country’s challenges rather than their ability to deploy political influence to retain power.

It also reiterated its position that Peter Obi remained a preferred choice among Nigerians, citing what it described as his commitment to competence, character, compassion and responsible leadership.

According to the statement, Obi represents an alternative leadership proposition capable of addressing Nigeria’s challenges and restoring national dignity, prosperity and hope.

The media office urged political officeholders to respect the sovereignty of the electorate, stressing that the authority to determine who governs the country ultimately rests with the people.

It added that Nigerians were prepared to defend their votes in the 2027 elections, warning that electoral manipulation, intimidation and political manoeuvring would not override their democratic aspirations.

“The mandate rests with the people. Nigeria must function again, and it will be OK,” the statement added.

World.title: SON Unveils Cylinder Recirculation Scheme to Curtail Spread of Unsafe Units
World.content:
* Targets 43m certified units

The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) has launched the National Cylinder Recirculation Programme (NCRP) to curtail the spread of unsafe, expired and substandard liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders across the country.

Unveiled at the Nigerian Alliance for Clean Cooking (NACC) Conference 2026 in Abuja, the N2.27 trillion national initiative sets out a coordinated regulatory framework to register, inspect, track and recirculate LPG cylinders across all six geopolitical zones.

The programme targets the deployment of at least 43 million certified cylinders and the establishment of 42 Authorized Requalification Facilities (ARFs) nationwide to replace unsafe units currently in circulation.

Under the new system, every cylinder will be onboarded onto a central National Cylinder Registry and assigned a unique QR code, enabling regulators and industry participants to trace each unit from manufacture through distribution, inspection, and maintenance.

Cylinders returned through approved retail channels will undergo testing at ARFs, where units meeting national quality standards will re-enter the market, while defective ones will be impounded for corrective action or safe disposal.

Delivering the keynote address, Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr. Jumoke Oduwole, represented by the ministry’s Director of Weights and Measures, Dr. Salim Mohammed, described the rollout as a transformative investment in public safety, industrial growth and skilled job creation aimed at establishing long-term stability in the LPG sector.

“This programme is more than a regulatory initiative; it is a transformative N2.27 trillion national investment in safety, industrialization and human development. By deploying at least 43 million certified cylinders and establishing 42 requalification centres nationwide, we are creating thousands of skilled jobs and laying the foundation for long-term sector planning,” she said.

During a panel session on expanding clean cooking access, industry leaders and regulatory officials highlighted the operational requirements needed to scale the framework.

Mr. Sabo Ahmed Barau, representing the Executive Director of Health, Safety, and Community Relations at the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), stressed that regulatory oversight will cover all stages from bulk storage to last-mile delivery to safeguard Nigerian households.

Addressing investment needs, Managing Director of FuelTree, Dr. ‘Bekeme Olowola, represented by the company’s Chief Technologist, Mr. Femi Oye, stated that verifiable empirical data through digital tracking is essential for unlocking commercial equity, grants and specialized climate financing.

On distribution, Founder of Falcon Corporation and Century One, Prof. Joseph Aigbedion, noted that primary storage infrastructure must be linked with arterial, community-level distribution clusters to reach families effectively.

CEO of Cook-Blue and Chiffinity Intelligence Consult, Princess Odiaka, highlighted the role of composite cylinders and community-based models in widening access, citing a “Trash-to-Cook” initiative in rural households.

She said: “Through our ‘Trash-to-Cook’ initiative, rural women exchange recyclable household waste to pay for clean gas refills. By turning discarded waste into currency, we address affordability, clean up the environment, and deliver clean cooking as an accessible service right to their doorsteps.”

SON is executing the NCRP in collaboration with government agencies and industry partners, including the NMDPRA, the National Council on Climate Change (NCCC), and the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs.

Following its domestic launch, Nigeria plans to present its digital safety and traceability framework to the international community at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

World.title: 2027: Indigenes Vow to Defend ‘Ogun for Ogun’ Mandate, As Adebutu, Deputy Tour Wards
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta

Indigenes of Ogun State have restated their resolve to protect their heritage and ensure that the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate of prominent stakeholders in the state is actualised in the 2027 governorship election in the state.

They made this pledge in their separate remarks during the ward-to-ward tours embarked upon by the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, declaring their support for the candidates ahead of the poll.

Adebutu and Kolapo have in the past weeks been touring wards across all the local government areas in Ogun, mobilising indigenes and intimating them with their seven-point agenda tagged: ‘ITURA DE.’

Many grassroots dwellers who were meeting Adebutu and Kolapo for the first time were excited to receive the candidates to their communities as they welcomed them with fanfare.

Indigenes also had the opportunity of having town hall discussions with the PDP candidates where they enumerated the challenges they are facing in their various communities.

They urged Adebutu to fix their deplorable roads and assist farmers with seedlings and modern agricultural equipment to enable them to produce food in large quantity for the state.

Speaking at different ward engagements, stakeholders resolved to mobilise support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate, stressing that: “It will be a slap on our dear state if a stranger is allowed to rule over us.”

At Alagada Ward, Obafemi Owode LGA, Mrs. Folasade Ogunye, a market leader, said she was backing the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ movement because indigenes understand the pains of the grassroots.

She said: “We, the women of Obafemi Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and our struggles.

“Apart from that, it would be a disservice to the memory of our heroes for an outsider to dictate the fortune of our people. That is why we have pledged to go from house to house to secure this mandate. It is about our pride as Ogun indigenes.”

At Alapakooni community in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of the state, some members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), set some bunches of brooms ablaze, saying they decided to dump the party because they could not continue to support a candidate who has not been able to state his true identity.

Tunde Akinola, a community youth coordinator at Alapakooni Ward, said: “We decided to join this ward meeting today with our incoming governor Adebutu because we love our state and can’t trade it on the altar of politics. We want to follow the person we know and that will deliver.”

A stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, identified as Deji Bamidele, said: “In this community, farming is our life but we have been left with cutlasses while other states use tractors. When Adebutu explained ITURA DE and how agriculture will be mechanised, we saw hope.

“We are committing our farmers’ cooperative of over 300 members to this ‘Ogun for Ogun’ cause to ensure our land is governed by our own.”

At Owode Ward 3, Obafemi Owode LGA, Alhaja Sariyu Bankole, a retired teacher, said her commitment was driven by the need to protect Ogun’s political legacy.

“We cannot mortgage our heritage. Ogun State is the home of great leaders. Allowing non-indigenes to take over will erase our history. I have told all my former students and their parents in this ward that we must vote for our own. That is our covenant,” she stated.

Similarly, in Ward 10, Sagamu LGA, Comrade Bayo Oduwole, a youth leader, said the youth were tired of being spectators.

“Courageous indigenes of this state have said we should not allow strangers to rule over us and we agree completely. The ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is not about tribalism, it is about competence and belonging. We know Adebutu’s family history here. We know all that they have done. We know how compassionate Iya Sunnah has been. We will mobilise our youth with voter education and door-to-door campaigns to ensure victory,” he said.

In his response, Adebutu thanked the indigenes for their warm reception and reaffirmed his commitment to the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate.

“This tour has shown me that our people are yearning for true homegrown leadership. The ITURA DE agenda is not just a slogan, it is a social contract to restore dignity, fix our roads, empower our farmers, create jobs for our youth and return Ogun State to true glory. We are not just campaigning, we are listening, and we will deliver,” he said.

Also speaking, the Ogun PDP deputy governorship candidate, Yemi Kolapo, assured residents that their administration would be inclusive and grassroots-driven.

She said: “What we have seen in all the wards we have visited is genuine love for Ogun State. As a mother and a daughter of this soil, I assure you that our government will prioritise women, children, education and primary healthcare. We will not disappoint you. This ‘Ogun for Ogun’ mandate is a mandate for all of us to save our state from dangerous intrusion.”

World.title: Senate Hails Return of Peace At NVRI Vom After Appointment Crisis
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Senate Committee on Livestock and Animal Husbandry has commended the management of the National Veterinary Research Institute (NVRI), Vom, and affiliated animal production institutions for restoring peace and strengthening relations with their host communities following tensions that arose over the appointment of a new provost earlier this year.

A member of the committee and senator representing Plateau Central, Senator Diket Satso Plang, led the oversight visit to the NVRI complex in Vom as part of the Senate’s constitutional responsibility to assess the operations of federal institutions under its purview and evaluate developments following the protests that greeted the appointment of Professor Abdullahi Ahmed as Provost of the Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology (FCAHPT).

The July protests had raised concerns within the host community and temporarily disrupted activities at the institution.

However, during the visit, committee members were informed that extensive consultations involving institutional management, community leaders, youth groups and other stakeholders had successfully resolved the issues and restored normalcy.

Addressing management and heads of the co-hosted institutions, Senator Plang and members of the committee expressed satisfaction with the prevailing atmosphere of peace and cooperation, noting that the crisis had been resolved through dialogue and mutual understanding.

The committee praised the leadership of the institution for fostering inclusiveness and collaboration among staff drawn from different ethnic and cultural backgrounds, describing the development as a model for national unity and peaceful coexistence.

Committee members also reflected on the historical significance of the veterinary research hub in Vom, recalling that the Nigerian Institute for Veterinary Research was established in 1924 and has remained a cornerstone of animal health research and development in the country for more than a century. They noted that the facility has continued to expand with the growth of other specialised institutions dedicated to animal production and laboratory technology.

Reaffirming the National Assembly’s commitment to supporting livestock development and veterinary research, Senator Plang assured the management that the Senate would continue to provide legislative backing through appropriations, oversight and policy support to strengthen the institutions’ mandates and enhance their contributions to national food security.

The lawmakers also commended traditional rulers, community leaders and youth representatives for embracing dialogue and demonstrating restraint during the period of disagreement, stressing that sustained engagement remains essential to preserving peace and promoting development.

Speaking during the engagement, the Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of the National Veterinary Research Institute, Dr. Dashe Yakubu Gunya, disclosed that the institution had achieved what he described as about 95 per cent peace and stability following the resolution of the dispute.

He attributed the breakthrough to the intervention and support of critical stakeholders, including political leaders in Plateau State, Governor Caleb Mutfwang, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, traditional institutions and members of the host community who chose the path of dialogue despite the initial agitation.

Dr. Gunya particularly acknowledged the role played by the Gbong Gwom Jos, the District Head of Vwang and community leaders for their willingness to listen and work towards a peaceful settlement of the issues.

He also expressed appreciation to the Federal Government, the minister overseeing the sector and President Tinubu for embracing a conciliatory approach that prioritised peace and community harmony.

According to him, while substantial progress has been made, discussions are continuing to address the remaining concerns raised by the host community, particularly in the area of corporate social responsibility.

He disclosed that the Federal College of Animal Health and Production Technology and the Federal College of Veterinary and Medical Laboratory Technology were working on initiatives aimed at mobilising resources and expanding support for the host community as part of efforts to consolidate peace and strengthen relations between the institutions and their neighbours.

The Senate delegation subsequently pledged to maintain close engagement with the institutions and surrounding communities to ensure that the gains achieved through dialogue are sustained and translated into long-term development and stability in the area.

World.title: State Police: National Assembly Begins Process to Transmit Bill to Tinubu
World.content:
* CNA says 28 state Assemblies complete approval

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The National Assembly has begun administrative processes to transmit the constitutional amendment bill seeking the establishment of state police to President Bola Tinubu for assent, following its approval by 28 state Houses of Assembly.

The development marks a significant step towards the proposed decentralisation of Nigeria’s policing system, after the number of approving state legislatures exceeded the constitutionally prescribed threshold of 24 states.

The Clerk to the National Assembly (CNA), Kamoru Ogunlana, disclosed this Tuesday in a statement, confirming that his office had received and verified reports from 28 state Houses of Assembly indicating their approval of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, seeking to provide for the establishment of State Police Services and related matters.

Ogunlana explained that Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution requires the approval of not less than two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly, equivalent to 24 states, before a constitutional alteration can proceed.

With 28 state legislatures having endorsed the proposed amendment, the constitutional requirement has been satisfied, paving the way for the National Assembly to commence the process of transmitting the bill to the president.

According to the statement, the bill was transmitted by the Clerk to the National Assembly to the 36 state Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, for their consideration and approval, with a request that their decisions be communicated to the National Assembly within 30 days.

Although the stipulated period expired on October 15, Ogunlana said his office would continue to receive reports from the state legislatures until the bill was transmitted for presidential assent.

He said the National Assembly had undertaken the necessary administrative verification of the reports and accompanying votes and proceedings to establish their authenticity and ensure that the records accurately reflected the decisions taken by the respective state legislatures.

The Clerk also clarified that Section 9 of the Constitution did not expressly prescribe a Third Reading for a Constitution Alteration Bill, unlike the procedure applicable to ordinary bills.

“In view of the approvals secured from the required number of state Houses of Assembly, the necessary administrative processes are being undertaken to facilitate the transmission of the Bill to His Excellency, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, for assent, in accordance with the Acts Authentication Act, CAP A2, (LFN) 2004,” he stated.

The proposed establishment of state police has remained a major issue in Nigeria’s constitutional and security reform discussions, particularly amid persistent challenges posed by terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminality across the country.

Proponents of decentralised policing have argued that allowing state governments to establish and operate their own police services would strengthen local intelligence gathering, improve community policing and facilitate quicker responses to security threats.

They have also maintained that the centralised policing structure has placed considerable pressure on the Nigeria Police Force, given the country’s size, population and diverse security challenges.

However, the proposal has generated concerns over possible political interference and abuse of state police institutions by governors, particularly against political opponents and perceived critics.

Other concerns relate to funding, operational independence, accountability, human rights protection and the need to establish clear constitutional boundaries between federal and state policing authorities.

Consequently, the process of establishing state police is expected to require additional legislative and institutional arrangements to determine the operational framework, recruitment procedures, funding mechanisms and oversight responsibilities of the proposed services.

The National Assembly, in the statement, described the approvals secured from the state legislatures as a significant step in the ongoing efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture and deepen the country’s federal system.

It also expressed appreciation to the state Houses of Assembly for their cooperation and timely response in considering the constitutional amendment.

Ogunlana assured Nigerians that his office would continue to provide accurate and timely information on developments relating to the constitutional amendment process.

World.title: Securty Operatives Rescue Eight Kidnap Victims in Kaduna
World.content:
John Shiklam in Kaduna

Eight persons abducted by bandits in Millennium City and Marraban Rido, areas of Kaduna metropolis have been rescued in a joint operations by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force and the Nigerian Army.

The Kaduna State Commissioner of Police, Muhammad Rabiu, disclosed this at a press conference on Tuesday at DSS Command headquarters in Kaduna.

He said the operation was “part of sustained efforts to identify, disrupt and dismantle criminal networks responsible for recurring abductions in the Millennium City General Area and its environs”.

He noted that the area had witnessed recurring incidents of kidnapping, generating considerable public concern and attracting media attention over the safety of residents and other stakeholders.

He identified the victims as Jamila Muhammad, 27, wife of Abdulkadir Bello; Talatu Yakubu, 40; Yunana Bawa, 30; Calista Bishop, 27; Chidinma Onuwere, 36; Eucharia Obi, 41; Godiya Victor, 50; and Miracle Alex, and an eight-year-old girl.

The commissioner said the successive breakthrough demonstrated the determination of security agencies to ensure the rescue of kidnap victims and dismantle criminal networks operating across the state.

He acknowledged the strategic coordination and contributions of the ONSA, the operational support of the Nigeria Police Force, the intelligence-driven efforts of the DSS and the involvement of the Nigerian Army in the operations.

Rabiu also commended the Kaduna State government for its continued support and cooperation with security agencies in tackling kidnapping and banditry.

The police commissioner assured residents that the government, working with security agencies, was intensifying efforts to eliminate kidnapping and banditry across Kaduna State.

He added that the ongoing security operations would be sustained and strengthened to deny criminal elements freedom of action.

Rabiu assured the people of additional deployment of personnel and equipment, including 30 vans and eight armoured personal carriers to ensure a secured environment.

Rabiu, however, called on residents to complement the efforts of security agencies by remaining vigilant and providing credible, accurate and actionable intelligence on the activities, identities and movements of suspected kidnappers, bandits and other criminal elements in their communities.

He assured members of the public that information supplied to security agencies would be treated with the necessary confidentiality and acted upon appropriately.

He also urged traditional and community leaders and other stakeholders to support the campaign against insecurity.

World.title: Fed-up recipient opens up about SASSA review struggles
World.content:
The SASSA review system has come under scrutiny yet again, as the agency vows increased stricter action in 2027. One reader of The South African, Rita Cronje, gives insight into what the process feels like from the queue.

Her grant was stopped in August 2026, she says, so she emailed her Limpopo office. To which the reply was she had to report to a local branch for SASSA review. “I spent three days standing in the heat to finally query my August grant,” she said.

Thinking the process was resolved, she received her September and October grants. However, August, the very month in question, is still to materialise in her bank account. The most frustrating part? The agency simply says she needs to return to a SASSA branch to rectify the original review.



SASSA REVIEW STRUGGLES

So, what exactly is happening with the SASSA review process? And why does the South African Social Security Agency appear to be so scattered on the matter?

February 2026: SASSA told Parliament it had reviewed about 240 000 grants and suspended about 70 000 . About 495 000 beneficiaries had been flagged by income verification technology.

grants and suspended about . About beneficiaries had been flagged by income verification technology. April to June 2026: SASSA put 105 600 beneficiaries under review and suspended 56 807, that’s about 54%.

As ever, the agency insists it doesn’t cancel grants ‘abruptly.’ However, it appears the knock-on effect is that payments may become delayed over successive months. And it is this exact scenario that Cronje is tangled up in.

NATIONAL TREASURY’S TARGET

Finance Minister Gondongwana did not okay any October 2026 top-ups for the first time in two years. Image: File

Moreover, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana’s October 2026 MTBPS counted R13 billion in expected savings from SASSA reviews. That and fraud detection make up the biggest part of a R38 billion budget adjustment over the medium term to 2030. Plus, the Treasury wants to see stricter verification cut ‘core’ beneficiary numbers from 17.8 million in 2026/27 to 17.1 million by 2029/30, saving a further R6.2 billion.



Meanwhile, the Institute for Economic Justice (IEJ) say the SASSA review system is ‘arbitrary’ and in some cases ‘unconstitutional.’ They argue the process creates burden, so, are there better ways to do it?

Why do one-time stokvel payouts and/or family gifts trigger suspensions? Should single, one-off lump-sum deposits be treated differently from regular income?

Is there a faster digital route for SASSA review? SRD applicants can check status and appeal online, but permanent grant recipients can only travel to an office.

Could there be a secure upload portal documents, with a reference number and call-back system?

SASSA pretends in its promotional material that it pays grants to “reach the right people at the right time and place.” However, for pensioners like Rita Cronje, stuck in the heat for days with nothing to show for it, there doesn’t appear to be a ‘right time.’

But what do you think? Can the SASSA review process be handled better? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: More than 1.4 million South Africans cast special votes ahead of Election Day
World.content:
Gauteng has the largest registered voting population in South Africa, accounting for nearly a quarter of all registered voters. Image: IEC

More than 1.4 million South Africans have already cast their ballots in the 2026 Local Government Elections, with the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) declaring itself ready for Wednesday’s nationwide vote.

The two-day special voting process concluded on Tuesday, 3 November, with 1 425 942 voters recorded as having cast their ballots.

Of these, 974 852 voted at voting stations, while 451 090 cast their ballots through home visits.



READ | Free coffees, beers, doughnuts and more: Outlets rewarding voters this Election Day

Preliminary numbers

The IEC said approximately 2.6 million voters had been approved for special voting because they would otherwise be unable to vote on Election Day.

That means just under 55% of those who applied for a special vote actually ended up casting their vote.



The figures are preliminary and were expected to be finalised on Tuesday evening.

Gauteng records the most special votes

Gauteng recorded the highest number of special votes, with 264 898, followed by KwaZulu-Natal and the Eastern Cape.

The provincial breakdown was:

Gauteng: 264,898

KwaZulu-Natal: 208,846

Eastern Cape: 207,258

Limpopo: 180,627

Mpumalanga: 149,714

Western Cape: 148,493

North West: 126,187

Free State: 75,946

Northern Cape: 63,973

The IEC confirmed that special ballots had been securely stored and would be counted alongside ballots cast on Election Day.



They will form part of the overall results announced for each voting station.

29.2 million voters registered

The IEC says it is operationally ready for Wednesday’s election, with arrangements in place across all nine provinces.

A total of 29.2 million voters are registered to participate in the 2026 Local Government Elections, with 23 696 voting stations established nationwide.



Approximately 188 000 IEC officials have been deployed to support the process. The Commission says ballot papers and essential election materials have been distributed, with logistical and security arrangements in place.

Voting stations will open at 07:00 and close at 21:00 on Wednesday, 4 November.

What voters need to take to the polls

The IEC has reminded voters that they may only cast their ballots at the voting station where they are registered.



Voters must present one of the following identity documents:

A green bar-coded South African ID book

A smart ID card

A valid Temporary Identity Certificate issued by Home Affairs

Voters can check their registration details, voting station and sequence number through the following channels:

WhatsApp: 060 088 0000

060 088 0000 IEC Contact Centre: 0800 11 8000

0800 11 8000 SMS: 32810 (R1 per SMS)

32810 (R1 per SMS) Website: www.elections.org.za

Providing a sequence number to election officials can help them locate a voter’s details more quickly.



Campaigning ends at midnight

Political parties, independent candidates and their supporters must stop campaigning at midnight on Tuesday, 3 November.

Door-to-door campaigning, canvassing, demonstrations and political rallies will no longer be permitted after the deadline.

The IEC also reminded contestants that campaigning and attempts to influence voters inside or in the immediate vicinity of voting stations are prohibited.



Voters may wear party colours, however, provided they do not engage in prohibited campaigning or attempts to influence others.

Important rules inside voting stations

The Commission has urged voters to protect the secrecy of their ballots and follow the rules inside voting stations.

Ballot papers must be marked privately in the designated voting booth. Taking photographs of completed or marked ballot papers is strictly prohibited.



Voters must also avoid intimidating or obstructing other voters or election officials. Dangerous weapons are not permitted inside voting stations, and disruptive behaviour is prohibited.

The IEC has further urged South Africans to verify election-related information through official channels before sharing it on social media, warning that false or misleading information can undermine confidence in the electoral process.

The Commission has called on voters, political parties, independent candidates and observers to help ensure a peaceful and orderly Election Day.

World.title: What time do polls CLOSE on voting day, and what if you’re still in the queue?
World.content:
An election official marking a citizen with indelible ink to prevent double voting. Image: IEC/ Facebook

Wednesday 4 November has been declared a public holiday in South Africa to give as many people as possible a chance to go voting and have a say in how their municipalities are run.

However, some employees will still have to put in a shift, while others have a long way to travel to get to their local voting booth.

And what happens if you’re still waiting in a queue when polling stations close?



Check out our cheat sheet below to confirm all your voting day logistics for the 2026 local government elections…

Voting hours and the rules around queues

Voting stations will open at 07:00 and remain open until late on Election Day (if you need a coffee, Wimpy is offering free brews for voters. Find out more here).

The closing time does not necessarily mean voters still waiting in line will miss out.



According to the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), voting stations will close at 21:00 on Wednesday, 4 November.

Voters are encouraged to arrive early to avoid the possibility of lengthy queues, particularly towards the end of the day.

Those who have not yet voted should also remember that municipal election voters must cast their ballots at the station where they are registered.



Can you still vote if you’re in the queue at 21:00?

Yes. Being in the queue before the official closing time means you should still get an opportunity to cast your ballot.

The Local Government: Municipal Electoral Act makes provision for this, stating: “Voting at a voting station must continue until every voter has voted who—

(a) is entitled to vote at that voting station; and

(b) has reported for voting at that voting station before the closing time.”

In other words, eligible voters who have reported to their registered voting station before 21:00 must be allowed to vote, even if they have to wait beyond the official closing time.



The IEC’s 2021 Municipal Elections Observer Handbook also instructs presiding officers to bring people waiting to vote inside the voting station’s boundaries before closing.

So, while it’s best not to leave voting until the last minute, arriving before 21:00 should ensure you aren’t turned away simply because of a long queue.

How to check your voter registration details

Before heading to the polls, voters can confirm that their registration details are correct and check where they are registered to vote.



Voters can check their details through any of the following channels:

IEC website: www.elections.org.za

SMS: Send your 13-digit ID number to 32810

WhatsApp: Send “Hi” to the IEC on 060 088 0000

Which ID documents are accepted for voting?

Voters must bring an acceptable identity document to the voting station. The accepted documents are:



A smart ID card

A green barcoded ID book

A valid temporary identity certificate

The IEC has cautioned voters that driver’s licences, passports, student cards and photocopies of identity documents are not accepted for voting purposes.

What happens at the voting station?

Once you arrive at your registered voting station, an election official will verify your identity and registration details.



Your name will be checked against the voters’ roll before your thumbnail is marked with indelible ink to prevent double voting.

You will then receive your ballot papers. The number of ballots you receive depends on whether you are registered in a metropolitan municipality or a local municipality.

How many ballot papers will you receive?

Metropolitan municipalities

These are large urban areas governed by a single metropolitan council. They include cities such as Cape Town, Johannesburg, Tshwane, eThekwini and Nelson Mandela Bay.



Voters registered in a metropolitan municipality will receive two ballot papers:

Ward ballot: Used to elect a ward councillor

Proportional representation (PR) ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation in the metropolitan council

Local municipalities

These are smaller towns and surrounding rural areas. They fall within district municipalities, which provide certain services and coordinate development across several local municipalities.



Voters registered in a local municipality will receive three ballot papers:

Ward ballot: Used to elect a ward councillor

Local council PR ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation on the local municipal council

District PR ballot: Used to choose a political party for representation on the district municipal council

How to cast your vote correctly:

Take your ballot papers into the voting booth and vote in private

Make one clear X inside the box next to your chosen candidate or political party on each ballot paper

Do not write your name, sign the ballot paper or make unnecessary marks, as this could make your ballot invalid

If you make a mistake, do not put the ballot paper in the ballot box. Return it to the Presiding Officer and ask for assistance

Once you have voted, fold your ballot papers to keep your choices private and place them in the ballot box as directed by election officials

World.title: Venue, time announced for Ramaphosa’s local elections vote

World.title: South Africa getting FOUR new R2 coins
World.content:
Four new R2 coins commemorate important historical milestones for the country. Do you know what they are? Image: SARB/Fotor

Have you noticed any of the four new R2 coins circulating in South Africa? The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) says the series of four commemorative coins is all about important milestones in history and democracy. Known as the Milestones of Freedom campaign, the four new R2 coins were launched by President Cyril Ramaphosa at the Union Buildings back in June 2026. And here are what each celebrates in 2026 …

FOUR NEW R2 COINS

125 years since Charlotte Maxeke’s university graduation in 1901.

since Charlotte Maxeke’s university graduation in 1901. 70 years since the Women’s March to Pretoria.

since the Women’s March to Pretoria. 50 years since the 1976 Soweto uprising.

since the 1976 Soweto uprising. 30 years since the adoption of South Africa’s Constitution.

Firstly, the 1976 uprising coin was released back in June. Two more, Maxeke and the Women’s March against apartheid pass laws, followed in August. And finally, the constitutional anniversary coin concludes the series. The two August Women’s month releases are also historic in that they are the first African commemorative coins to feature women.

STILL LEGAL TENDER

SARB Governor, Lesetja Kganyago, says: “However beautiful the new R2 coins may be, the coins remain ordinary legal tender – not collectables – so their face value is unchanged, and they belong in circulation.” Furthermore, the distinction between collectable and ordinary legal tender is important.



The SA Mint does produce numerous coins at the opposite end of the scale. These are limited-edition precious-metal pieces aimed at collectors and often worth a lot of money. Meanwhile, commemorative circulation coins are made to be used in everyday transactions.

2026 AFRICAN RANGE

These high-value coins form part of the SA Mint’s 2026 African Range, with artwork from Dylan Lewis. Image: File

You may recall, its last creation was the striking 2026 African Range. This was the SA Mint’s first-ever high-relief proof coin series. They featured designs based on sculptures by internationally acclaimed South African artist Dylan Lewis. The collection followed five stages of a cheetah hunting. And formats included quarter-, one-, two- and five-ounce gold pieces, two- and five-ounce silver coins, and one-kilogram gold and silver versions, limited to just 100.

The contrast between this and South Africa’s four new R2 coins shows the two sides of the coin-making process. One is rare, high-value objects intended for collectors, while the other is an ordinary R2 coin designed to travel from hand to hand with a special message if you ever take the time to notice and appreciate it …



But what do you think? Have you seen any of the new R2 coins yet? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: 'We are ready' : Gauteng police deployed in hot spot areas amid voting
World.content:
MIDRAND - Police in Gauteng have been deployed ahead of Wednesday's local government elections to monitor potential hotspot areas.

This comes as Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Fred Kekana says they have identified more than 180 high-risk areas in the province.

Speaking to eNCA on the sidelines at the National Results Operations Centre (ROC) in Midrand, Kekana said law enforcement will be on high alert to ensure that there are no disruptions during the electoral process.

The same attention will also be given to medium-risk areas, he added.

World.title: NPA secures forfeiture order for R100k bribe linked to Tembisa Hospital corruption
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The National Prosecuting Authority has secured a final court order forfeiting R100,000 linked to corruption at Tembisa Hospital.

The money was seized in November 2025 after former hospital official Zacharia Tshisele and police sergeant Papi Blonde Tsie allegedly offered it to an investigating officer to avoid arrest.

The attempted bribe was reported, leading to an undercover operation in which police arrested the two men.

READ | Tembisa Hospital looting | Who is Stefan Govindraju?

The High Court in Johannesburg granted the forfeiture order after Tshisele failed to oppose the application.

The money will go to the Criminal Assets Recovery Account.

World.title: Petrol price barely budges as diesel gets November cut
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The price of petrol is coming down by one cent.

Diesel will show a more significant drop of between R1.10 and R1.20 from midnight.

The oil price has been soaring and South Africans would have been in for higher prices after both petrol and diesel hit records in October.

But Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced in the medium-term budget that the general fuel levy will be cut in November by R1.50 per litre for petrol and R3 for diesel.

The fuel levy relief would have been more significant but an additional slate levy has been added.

The Slate levy is used periodically to refund fuel importers for the difference between what they actually pay for fuel and the regulated price they can sell it at.

World.title: AGOA Fallout | Govt must save US duty-free trade deal: Cosatu
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cosatu urged the government on Tuesday to directly engage with the United States to rescue a trade deal on which thousands of jobs depend.

Washington announced Monday it would remove South Africa and Rwanda from the Africa-US trade preference programme from January 1, citing practices that created "barriers".

This could cost between 3,000 and 10,000 jobs in the agriculture and manufacturing sectors, a representative of the trade union federation told AFP.

Some of the companies most at risk are based in small towns, for example the citrus-producing areas of the Western Cape province, Matthew Parks said.

"There's a danger of creating ghost towns," said Parks, the federation's parliamentary coordinator.

It is critical the government "put in place an urgent package of support for at-risk workers, companies, industries and communities", Cosatu said.

About 10 percent of South African exports to the US entered under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) programme in 2025, Trade Minister Parks Tau said Monday.

South Africa's largest trade union federation has urged the government to use the period before the exit takes effect to negotiate "a favourable set of solutions to avert this potential blow to the South African economy and jobs".

"We are meeting with government to encourage them to go to the US, use the next 60 days to negotiate a possible package deal," Parks said. "That'll be critical."

"We also need to make clear to the US as well that some of the benefits they have enjoyed with South Africa through AGOA would also be at risk of expiry."

Washington is, for example, keen to continue to import critical minerals from South Africa, he said.

"It's a two-way street."

World.title: Two arrested in Eastern Cape for impersonating IEC official
World.content:
GQEBERHA - Two people have been arrested in the Eastern Cape for allegedly impersonating an Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) official.

It is alleged that at about 4.30am on 2 November 2026, the suspects arrived at Ngcobo Police Station to collect voting material, claiming they had been sent by the presiding officer.

However, the presiding officer was already at the station and had not authorised anyone to collect the material.

The suspects were identified before leaving the station, and the voting material was confiscated. Both have been arrested and are being processed.

Eastern Cape Provincial Commissioner Lieutenant General Vuyisile Ncata condemned the incident, stating that any attempt to interfere with the electoral process would not be tolerated.

“We will not tolerate any interference with the electoral process. The arrest of the two suspects demonstrates our commitment to upholding the integrity of the elections. Anyone who impersonates an IEC official will face the full might of the law,” said Ncata.

World.title: 'Criminals will not be on holiday' | Mkhwanazi warns police ahead of elections
World.content:
DURBAN - Security agencies have joined forces to ensure free, fair, and credible municipal elections, with police officers deployed across KwaZulu-Natal to safeguard voters and protect voting stations.

KwaZulu-Natal Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi says members of the SAPS Task Team will escort election materials from warehouses to voting stations and ensure their safe return after voting concludes.

Officers will also maintain a visible presence at polling stations, protect voters, and respond to criminal activity.

Addressing members of various security agencies, Mkhwanazi stressed that all officers have a shared responsibility to safeguard the electoral process, regardless of their respective departments or disciplines.

“You are standing here in different uniforms, from different disciplines, different government security agencies, but we only have one mission, and the mission is to deliver a free, fair, and credible election for our country.”

He reminded officers that they are not political party representatives and must remain impartial, treating all political parties and independent candidates equally.

Mkhwanazi also urged members to remain vigilant, warning that election deployments must not distract officers from their responsibility to fight crime.

He cautioned that criminals would remain active on election day and instructed officers to respond decisively to any criminal activity, including incidents involving dangerous weapons or attempts to disrupt voters' constitutional rights.

“Criminals will not be on holiday tomorrow. Some of them will not even vote. So, do not turn a blind eye to crime committed in your presence.”

He said officers must not compromise law enforcement simply because they have been assigned election duties.

Mkhwanazi added that lessons from previous elections must inform this year's security operations, stressing that officers must act within the law and the Electoral Act.

World.title: 'Cursed' Peru town hopes Pope Leo brings better luck
World.content:
ZANA - A luckless Peruvian town that has for centuries been dismissed as cursed is hoping for a new lease on life when Pope Leo visits this month.

Under Spanish colonial rule in the 16th century, Zana -- home to around 4,000 souls -- was a wealthy centre of commerce dotted with grandiose churches.

But three centuries after it was nearly destroyed by a flood of biblical proportions, vultures now roost in its ruined steeples.

Zana's identity is strongly associated with Catholicism, thanks to legends of divine punishment -- before the flood, it was regularly attacked by pirates -- to the death in the town in 1606 of Toribio de Mogrovejo, a Spanish missionary who converted Indigenous Peruvians to Christianity.

Saint Toribio, who denounced abuses by the Spanish crown, has been feted as a role model by Leo, who will celebrate the 300th anniversary of his canonisation in Zana in northern Peru during a three-country tour of South America.

"The curse is over," said Maria Colchado, a 63-year-old homemaker who is helping prepare the town for the visit on November 14.

Colchado is one of the volunteers in charge of maintaining the modest church that will receive Pope Leo, who served as archbishop in this region from 2015 to 2023.

The facade is currently getting a lick of new white and burgundy paint, financed by the sale of raffle tickets.

Pope Leo, who recently underwent surgery for lung cancer, will wrap up his first Latin American tour in Peru, after visiting Uruguay and Argentina.

World.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Americans deliver their verdict on Donald Trump's tumultuous second presidency Tuesday in midterm elections that threaten to shatter his grip on Washington, with Democrats poised to seize the House and challenge for control of the Senate.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.

The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war against Iran.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

The 80-year-old's approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.

In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country's future.

"I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy," she told AFP.

- Economic discontent -

Republicans insist that Trump's tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.

But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington's Reflecting Pool.

World.title: Do not be lazy, get to work, Gachagua tells opposition
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua. [Courtesy, X]

Democracy for Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua has called out the United Alternative Government leaders telling them to drop laziness and go out and mobilise.

Speaking at his Wamunyoro home when he received a group of leaders from Nyeri County, the DCP leader said the only wat to send President William Ruto home was through voter mobilisation.

“For us to send Ruto home we must mobilise 18 million votes, these numbers cannot be mobilised in hotel rooms, boardrooms, press conferences or writing letters, you must go out there and persuade the people of Kenya to register votes and come out and vote,” he said.

Gachagua added that Kenyans were not stupid and they can see leaders who have been working and who are not.

“Some people are imagining that my work is to chase Ruto and give you the seat as flagbearer. No, si hata mimi nataka? Gachagua said.

“If I helped Ruto to be president, why can I not also help myself? Si mimi nafanya kazi?”

Gachagua who also welcomed former Kitui governor Charity Ngilu said that he was committed to the opposition producing one candidate to battle it out with Ruto at the ballot in the 2027 polls.

“I am the most committed person in the entire United Opposition. I have proven by action that I am a serious mobiliser,” said the former Gachagua.

He said that Ngilu was key player in the National Alliance of Rainbow Coalition (NARC) in the 2002 polls and that she had shared the winning strategy with him and he was confident of victory in 2027.

“I benefited greatly from Hon. Ngilu’s wisdom as she took me through how NARC was crafted and implemented.” Democracy for Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua and his spouse Dorcas together with former Kitui governor Charity Ngilu (C) at his Wamunyoro home. [Courtesy, X]

At the same time Gachagua answered Democratic Party leader Justin Muturi and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i over bullying claims saying he was only telling them the truth about a presidential campaign.

The DCP leader said that the leaders should reduce their match their TV appearances, hotel meetings and press releases with getting boots on the ground to meet the people.

He said that the 2027 Presidential contest was about votes and all leaders should mobilise and make sure the opposition secures more votes than Ruto.

“And we must discuss numbers. Some are uncomfortable discussing numbers. They must be discussed. I believe in numbers.”

The ex-deputy president said that since he left the country, opposition activities had gone down and only his DCP party allied leaders were busy criss-crossing the country and now that he is back the opposition is lively.

“There is no other formula for sending William Ruto home unless you go out and mobilise numbers,”

He said that no one in the opposition can teach him on how to send Ruto home, saying that he played a key role in delivering the Presidency in 2022 and would do the same in 2027.

“My work is to ensure Ruto goes home. I am not sleeping. All the meetings here at Wamunyoro are on how to send Ruto home,” he said.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.

World.title: Not so fast! Court blocks Bomas expansion
World.content:
Contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site. [File, Standard]

The Environment and Lands Court has blocked the government from continuing with the construction of a car park inside the Nairobi National Park.

Justice Grace Kemei, in her ruling, said that the contractors hired are barred from clearing vegetation, cutting trees, excavating, grading, fencing, constructing routes, and undertaking any works at the disputed site.

World.title: Kikuyu PCEA church loses 2.7-acre illegally acquired land
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

The Presbyterian Church of East Africa (PCEA) has lost its 2.7-acre piece of land to a school.

This is after the Environment and Lands Court at Thika established that the land under the church's Ruguthi Women's Guild was a school playground and was illegally allocated.

Presiding Judge Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property, and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent.

According to her, the land had been reserved for use as a playground by Kanyiha, Lusigetti and Njumbi Primary Schools.

The verdict follows a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya, with the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) participating as an interested party.

In a statement on Monday, EACC's head of Corporate Affairs and Communication Stephen Karuga said the anti-graft agency presented evidence demonstrating that the land had been reserved for public use and therefore, any allocation to third parties was irregular. Justice Jacqueline Mogeni, in her verdict, said the land in contention was public property and its registration in the name of the said church was irregular and fraudulent. [Courtesy, EACC]

"Our investigations established that the land was set aside in 1957 by the former County Council of Kiambu for use as a school playing field," Karuga said, adding, "the investigations further revealed that there was no letter of offer or acceptance, no evidence of payment of rent rates and no proof that the Women's Guild had paid any consideration to the council for the land."

According to Karuga, the judgement safeguards a vital public facility used by more than 1,300 pupils, ensuring that the playground remains available for learning, sports and recreation for the current and future generations.

As a result, the judge said the allocation, transfer and registration of the land LR. NO KARAI/350 and subsequent issuance of a title deed in 2001 was unprocedural, illegal, null and void.

"An order of Mandamus is hereby issued directing the 3rd respondent, the Land Registrar, Kiambu Chief Land Registrar, to forthwith cancel and revoke the Title Deed and all register entries in respect of the land issued to the 1st respondent on Dec 6, 2001, or at any subsequent date," the Judge said.

The judge further ordered that the said parcel of land be handed over to the Board of Management of the two schools and the Education Ministry.

"An order of permanent injunction is hereby issued restraining the 1st respondent, whether by herself, her church officials, agents, servants, assigns or anyone claiming through her, from entering into, taking possession of, fencing, depositing construction materials upon, transferring, charging, developing or in any other manner dealing or interfering with the land," she ordered.

World.title: Sakaja protests release of 14 suspects linked to Eastleigh collapsed building
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja has protested the release of suspects linked to the collapsed building in Eastleigh.

While pushing for the county to have prosecutorial powers, Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court.

Sakaja in statement posted on his X account (formerly Twitter) said City Hall had taken enforcement action against those involved after establishing change of user from a residential property to a commercial had been approved.

According to Sakaja, architectural plans required to authorise construction had not been approved.

The Governor said County officers arrested the suspects and handed them over to Kamukunji Police Station because county governments no longer hold prosecutorial powers they previously held.

“We enforced the law and arrested those involved. However, because we do not have prosecutorial powers, the suspects were handed over to Kamukunji Police Station. They were reportedly released on a cash bail of Sh50,000 without being taken to court,” Sakaja said.

“We want the police to explain why the suspects were released without being presented in court and why construction was allowed to continue. These are serious questions that must be answered,” he added.

A police occurrence book entry from Kamukunji Police Station indicates that 14 suspects were booked into custody on June 17, 2026, over the alleged offences relating to contravention of city planning laws.

Enforcement action and arrests were made severally by the county officials and most recently in July after failing to comply with the enforcement order below. However the suspects were released on a 50k bail at Kamukunji police on the very same day. Prosecution of the same was also denied. We have repeatedly asked for the resumption of the power to prosecute such violations of such county and county related laws after this was taken away from County governments in 2024 (one such letter to the office of the DPP is attached). Meanwhile, several such cases have either been rejected by prosecutors (who are independent of the County), dismissed by the justice system or have had minimal fines imposed. Fining a developer 50k for an illegal development with hundreds of millions without orders to stop and remove the offensive development is completely unreasonable. I raised this in the Senate a fortnight ago and we shall keep pushing for a review of this position. All of these instances, where enforcement action has been curtailed, blocked or interfered with, will be published to the public. October 25, 2026

The entry, recorded under OB No. 98/17/06/2026, names the suspects and states that they were booked by Nairobi City County officers before being placed in police cells.

A separate Kenya Police Service record indicates that 10 suspects were subsequently released on a cash bail of Sh50,000.

The entry, recorded at 9.44pm, states that the release was carried out on the instructions of the Officer Commanding Station (OCS), identified in the record as C.I. Onyapidi, through Corporal Awadh.

The record references receipt number 2039434 and states that the suspects left the station without complaints.

However, the documents do not, on their own, establish the specific charges against the suspects, the legal basis for the bail arrangement or whether they were subsequently presented in court.

The discrepancy between the 14 suspects recorded as booked into custody and the 10 named in the release entry also raises questions about the subsequent status of the other suspects. Sakaja demanded answers from Kamukunji Police on how the suspects were arrested in June but released on Sh50,000 bail without being charged in court. [GPS]

Sakaja said a June 2025 enforcement notice adds another dimension to the questions surrounding the property and the enforcement of planning regulations.

The notice, issued by Nairobi City County over alleged construction works undertaken without the required development permission, cited the Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019, and county by-laws.

It directed the recipient to stop the works and remove the development described as illegal, warning that the County could undertake the required action and recover the costs if the directives were not followed.

The notice also provided for an appeal to the County Physical and Land Use Planning Liaison Committee.

Sakaja clarified that approval to change a property’s use from private to commercial-cum-residential does not amount to approval of architectural plans authorising construction.

He said the County approved the change of use but did not approve the architectural plans, yet construction proceeded.

I have seen some people peddling a fake approval document alleging that the Eastleigh development was approved. It is telling that this is the same document that the Eastleigh developer used to get NCA approval. They allege that the development was approved in January of 2024. This is not true. The application for development as shown below was made in November of 2024, it could not have been approved in February of the same year.
