World.title: Virgin Media O2 to cut thousands of jobs and slash costs
World.content:
London – British telecoms group Virgin Media O2 said Tuesday that it would cut thousands of jobs in a sweeping cost-saving programme, helped by greater use of AI, to reduce its debt pile.

The telecoms group said it expected to save around £300 million ($400 million) in staff expenses, as part of a broader plan to slash costs by around £800 million a year by 2029.

The group, which employs 16,000 people, did not confirm how many jobs would be axed but said the number would be in the thousands.

“While many of these decisions are tough, they are necessary for our future success and growth,” chief executive Lutz Schuler said in a statement.

“Given the market conditions we face, the regulatory backdrop in fibre and the technological changes sweeping across all areas of the economy, standing still and doing what we’ve always done is not an option,” he said.

Most of the job losses over the next two years will come from restructuring at its head office, including cuts to senior leadership roles, rather than positions that involve direct dealings with customers.

“The company also expects a greater use of AI tools and digital channels to drive efficiency, productivity and better customer experience,” the group said, adding that it has launched a voice AI agent to handle broadband fault calls.

The group said it would give further updates on the restructuring plan with its annual earnings release in February.

– £22 billion debt –

Virgin Media O2 is under pressure from investors to slim its huge pile of debt, which totals more than £22 billion.

The job losses were announced alongside the group’s third-quarter earnings, which saw revenue fall 5.7 percent from a year earlier to £2.4 billion.

While it returned to a net profit of £1.5 million in the July-September period, it also lost more than 23,000 customers across its internet and phone services.

To help save costs, the group is halting the roll-out of its fibre network upgrades beyond existing commitments.

It is also reviewing its use of contractors and suppliers.

“The result of these changes will be a leaner business that has fewer layers, greater focus, optimised investment and faster decision making,” the group said.

It cited “a tough macroeconomic climate” and “an intensely competitive and shrinking broadband market” as reasons for the job cuts.

Spanish operator Telefonica and US group Liberty Global merged their UK units O2 and Virgin Media in 2021.

The group had already cut 2,000 jobs in 2023 following wider culls across the British telecoms sector.

World.title: Iran hangs two young men in latest executions over protests: NGOs
World.content:
Paris – Iran on Tuesday hanged two young men on charges related to nationwide protests in January, as rights groups accused authorities of subjecting them to torture and an unfair trial.

Amirhossein Maleki, 20, and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, 19, were executed after being convicted over events in a square in the central city of Isfahan during the protests that authorities say caused the deaths of four members of the security forces, Norway-based NGO Iran Human Rights (IHR) said.

Iran has now executed 36 men over the protests, IHR said, in a wave of hangings rights groups see as a bid to spread fear throughout society after the mass protests that they say were put down in a crackdown that left thousands dead.

The Iranian judiciary said that Maleki and Ebrahimi had been hanged over “brutal and atrocious actions (that) led to the martyrdom of four police officers” and that their death sentences had been upheld by the supreme court, according to the Mizan news agency.

The case centres on events in Alikhani Square in Isfahan, which was a hub of protests activity on the nights of January 8 and 9. Seven other men have already been executed in the same case and three more are at risk of execution, according to IHR.

It said the entire case has been marked by “torture, forced confessions and gross violations of due process in this case”, with authorities using “the deaths of four security officers to justify these executions, although none of those executed were charged with murder”.

The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) which also confirmed the executions, said defendants and their lawyers had limited access to case files and noted “allegations that pressure and torture were used during the investigation”.

Iran in October also arrested one of the most prominent lawyers defending protesters in the case, Amirsalar Davoudi.

The Hengaw rights group, also based in Norway, said “Ebrahimi was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture during interrogation in an attempt to extract forced confessions”.

The two men were sentenced to death on the capital charges of “waging war against God” and “corruption on earth”, according to Mizan.

IHR also said Ebrahimi was subjected to mock executions and “his 16-year-old brother was also tortured and had confessed against him”.

“The scale of torture and violations of due process in this case is appalling,” IHR director Mahmood Amiry Moghaddam told AFP.

World.title: West Ham sack head coach Nuno after poor start to Championship season
World.content:
London – West Ham sacked head coach Nuno Espirito Santo on Tuesday after a disappointing start to the Championship season.

The 52-year-old Portuguese manager oversaw the Hammers’ relegation from the Premier League last season but stayed with the London club.

Many viewed them as favourites to win automatic promotion back to the top flight but they are currently eighth in the second-tier table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough, after 13 games.

West Ham had a good run after a shaky start to the season but have lost their past two league games, against Southampton and West Brom.

Nuno, who previously managed Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest, was appointed in September last year but was unable to keep West Ham in the Premier League.

“West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect,” the club said in a statement.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.”

Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeping coach Rui Barbosa have also left the club.

West Ham said the process of recruiting a new head coach was already under way.

World.title: Iraq targets 2028 WTO accession as ITC proposes national trade strategy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi federal government is actively accelerating its accession procedures to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), targeting full membership compliance by 2028, according to Executive Director of the International Trade Centre (ITC) Pamela Coke-Hamilton.

Speaking on the Dinar Iqtisadi program broadcast by Al-Iraqiya News, Coke-Hamilton confirmed that the ITC continues to support Baghdad through technical reviews of domestic trade legislation, regulatory alignment, and capacity-building across both public institutions and the private sector.

Following Iraq’s submission of its market access offer on goods in September, authorities are finalizing the corresponding services offer. Coke-Hamilton noted that strong political commitment was evident in her high-level consultations with Iraq’s foreign and trade ministers, identifying the reform implementation schedule as the primary challenge.

Full WTO accession is projected to bolster international investor confidence by institutionalizing transparent, predictable commercial frameworks.

Coke-Hamilton outlined a formal proposal submitted to the Iraqi government to establish a comprehensive National Trade and Investment Strategy linked directly to Iraq’s National Development Plan (2024–2028).

Designed to identify promising non-oil sectors and expand employment for youth and women, the initiative responds to critical structural vulnerabilities highlighted by recent transit volatility in the Strait of Hormuz, where a single maritime disruption can yield an estimated $60 billion in economic shocks.

To insulate the sovereign economy from severe hydrocarbon price shocks, Coke-Hamilton emphasized priority diversification toward construction, tourism, information technology, and agro-industrial manufacturing.

Highlighting that micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) drive roughly 90% of Iraq’s domestic economic activity, Coke-Hamilton detailed the tangible footprint of ITC programs on the ground.

The SAAVI project, launched in 2020, has supported over 4,000 Iraqi farmers, generating a 70% increase in agricultural yield and exports, while ongoing programs like “Jobs” and “Masar” continue expanding vocational and technical apprenticeships in solar installation, green construction, and hospitality.

Iraqi produce—including commercial potato, tomato, and poultry varieties—has met modern retail standards to secure shelf placement in supermarket chains like Carrefour.

However, Coke-Hamilton warned that Iraqi agro-food exports remain constrained by the absence of internationally accredited domestic testing laboratories, forcing local exporters to send food samples abroad for testing at substantial logistical cost.

In the commercial sector, she noted that the Iraqi National Trade Fair facilitated more than $83 million in sales, attracting multinational conglomerates including Siemens, Alcatel, Nokia, and General Electric, reflecting Iraq’s emerging position as a viable regional hub for cross-border investment and trade integration.

World.title: Nvidia orders data center clients to reduce China exposure: FT
World.content:
San Francisco – US chipmaking giant Nvidia is ordering its data center partners to scale back work with Chinese customers, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday.

Nvidia’s cloud computing clients must now sell at least 51 percent of their services to non-Chinese companies, the FT reported, citing five people with knowledge of the matter.

The new rules only affect future contracts and not existing agreements, the report said.

Nvidia neither confirmed nor denied the report to AFP, but said in a statement that “datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation that American model and application makers need to compete worldwide.”

“Longstanding U.S. policy encourages every cloud to build on American infrastructure and to win business everywhere they can,” the statement said.

“America cannot win the AI race unless America’s AI infrastructure wins worldwide — if the world’s clouds rely on foreign-made chips, the model and application layers will be foreign-built as well.”

Asked about the report, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she was not aware of it.

“As a matter of principle, we consistently hope that all parties can provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for companies from all countries, including Chinese companies,” she said.

China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector.

In recent months, the two countries have traded accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security.

Nvidia is the world’s most valuable company thanks to the global drive to build data centres packed with specialist computer chips and other hardware that runs AI systems.

World.title: India to oppose EU carbon tax at COP31, firms on fossil fuel use for its energy needs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India will remain committed to protecting interests of its domestic industry against unilateral trade barriers such as European Unionâs carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) and wonât support any move to phase out fossil fuels, keeping in view the countryâs energy requirement for its development goals, said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav on Tuesday.

His remarks came as he prepares to lead a team of negotiators to the annual UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, next week.

Speaking about the countryâs overall stand during the climate negotiation, Yadav said India will play a âconstructive and bridge-building roleâ, seeking an outcome that moves from commitments to implementation and support.

Turkish presidency of COP31, scheduled from Nov 9 to 20, has invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the leaders' summit of the UN climate conference.



It is, however, not yet clear whether Modi will attend the Summit, scheduled for Nov 11-12.

On COP31âs proposed â35-by-35â electrification goal that aims to raise electricityâs share of global final energy demand from about 23% today to 35% by 2035, the minister said India will underline that voluntary initiatives under Presidency Action Agenda should remain separate from negotiations and that uniform global targets must respect national circumstances.





Though the minister preferred not to comment on the presidencyâs global electrification goal, his emphasis on respecting ânational circumstancesâ clearly indicates that India would weigh all options before committing to any such global target which will not be part of the formal negotiation process.

As far as CBAM, which entered its operational regime on Jan 1, is concerned, India opposed the proposal from the time it was conceived, arguing that such a unilateral move placed an additional burden on businesses in developing economies due to embedded emissions in their products.

CBAM is a tool to put a price, through imposing a border tax, on carbon-intensive goods, like iron and steel, aluminium and cement, that are entering the 27 EU nations.

Even all the BRICS nations, including China, Russia, South Africa, Brazil and others, formally opposed it and any other such trade barriers, calling them âunilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist measuresâ, when they assembled here for the annual summit under Indiaâs chairship in Sept.

World.title: EC allows voters deleted from draft electoral rolls to use Form 6 for re-inclusion
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Tuesday allowed previously enrolled voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to submit Form 6 to seek their inclusion in the final list.

In a letter to all state chief electoral officers, the poll body said it had received reports that some voters were hesitant to submit Form 6. The EC said that voters were concerned about requiring to declare that their names are being included in the electoral rolls for the first time.

"Therefore, such electors believe that submission of Form 6, in view of their previous enrolment, would amount to making a false declaration and render them liable for prosecution under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950," it said.



The EC's clarification comes days after the Supreme Court said that no one would be prosecuted for using Form 6 to get their names included in the electoral rolls again.

The observation was made by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL challenging the large-scale exclusion of names from Maharashtra's draft electoral roll. The bench was responding to senior advocate Aravind Datar's submission that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to making a false declaration under oath.





âNo one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists," the CJI said.

The bench also said, âIf we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists.â

What is Form 6?

Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion of their name in the electoral roll.

According to the Election Commission's guidelines, the application is addressed to the Electoral Registration Officer of the constituency where the applicant ordinarily resides.

The form requires basic details such as the applicant's name, details of a relative, Aadhaar information, gender, date of birth and present ordinary residence. Applicants are also required to complete a declaration. The guidelines warn that making a false statement in the declaration is punishable under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

Every religion has both good and bad people; we shouldn't make such generalisations... We should avoid them. That is exactly what the BJP wants; why should we fall into their trap?"

Rai, who represents the Ghosi Lok Sabha constituency in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, firmly repudiated the AISA leader's rhetoric riddled with "sweeping generalisations".



"In this day and age, the kind of rhetoric being used is simply unacceptable. There is no basis for it. We shouldn't make sweeping generalisations about any caste, community, religion, or region," he said.

Akhilesh Yadav's party is not the only one to shrug off Bora's statement, as Uddhav Sena leader Priyanka Chaturvedi also called her assertions "unfortunate", saying radical thinking, be it from the Right or the Left, is harmful to the nation.





"It is highly unfortunate. While I believe this may be an old video, it reveals a mindset that asserts rapes happen in temples, are committed by priests, and that Brahmin women are unsafe. I generally avoid focusing on caste, but as a Brahmin woman myself, I must ask: is it appropriate to use such derogatory language? I have always maintained that this kind of radical thinkingâwhether from the Left or the Rightâis harmful to the nation," the former Rajya Sabha member said.

She, however, said she would like to "sit down with Neha Bora and explain that not everything should be viewed through the lens of caste or religion".

"She is young, talented, bright, and smart, with the drive to fight for a cause; she ought to use her intellect more constructively," Chaturvedi said.

Earlier, the BJP targeted Bora over a video showing her criticising the âBrahmanical systemâ, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing her of spreading âHindu hateâ.

Sharing the video on X, Bhandari called Bora the âposter girlâ of what he described as Rahul Gandhiâs anti-Hindu politics.

In the video, Bora is heard speaking about women's safety and criticising the Brahmanical system. She reportedly referred to the Unnao and Kathua cases while making her remarks.

Bhandari also linked her comments to an earlier statement by Rahul Gandhi on the safety of women.

"Neha Bora poster girl of Rahul Gandhi displays her Hindu hate," Bhandari wrote.

He added, "She is inspired from Rahul Gandhi who earlier had said 'Mandiro main ladkiyon ke sath ched chad hoti hai'."

"Congress Hates Hindus, loves vote bank! Congress Soch is a threat to India's unity!" Bhandari posted.

The remarks triggered a political row after the video surfaced on social media. However, the clip is undated, and the circumstances in which Bora made the comments could not be independently verified.

Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

She took part in an October 10 demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups in Delhi. Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.

The AISA president also backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally against the CEC, urging people to join the opposition's demonstration in Delhi.

She has also appeared alongside Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders during protests against the poll body chief. Bora was also present at "mock" Parliament which was organised to symbolically "impeach" Gyanesh Kumar.

World.title: West Bengal's first relocated tigress captured on sojourn in Assam, returned to Buxa
World.content:
Dooars Rani was released in Buxa on October 2 and crossed into Assam's Raimona National Park on October 25

The three-year-old tigress, who was recently relocated to West Bengal's Buxa Tiger Reserve from Bihar, was captured on a foray into Assam and returned to West Bengal on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

The tigress, Dooars Rani (BTR-TF-1/ T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. She crossed into Assam's Raimona National Park on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of habitat.

"On Tuesday, we tranquilised the tigress, caged her, and brought her back to Buxa. Initially we let her explore and captured her today only when she came close to human settlements. However, there is nothing to panic about now. The tigress is also safe and healthy," said Forest Minister Manoj Oraon. The minister has been present in Assam for the last four days to monitor the tigress.

According to the officials, the tigress crossed the Sankosh River and a road in Gosaigaon in Assam to enter Raimona looking for habitat. Her movement area was traced up to 25 km from the Bengal border.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore. "She is not the property of any government. It is the nature of tigers to explore. She will likely cross into Raimona or any other area again. Our team will continue to monitor her," said the minister.

More translocations planned

On October 2, the tigress was translocated from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released in the presence of Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The CM said three more tigers would be released in Buxa over the next two months, and the initiative would not only help in conservation but also in boosting tourism.

Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, but there have been no reports of a tiger’s presence in the region of late. According to an official statement by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort, and the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has been implemented collaboratively since 2018.

Forest officials say this new tigress from Bihar will be subjected to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping, and field-based monitoring to assess her movement, adaptation, health, and behaviour.

World.title: Mundathikode fireworks tragedy: judicial commission finds 7,000 kg of explosives stored against permitted 15 kg
World.content:
The judicial commission appointed by the State government to investigate the Mundathikode fireworks tragedy has submitted its report to the government. The commission headed by retired Justice C.N. Ramachandran Nair handed over the report to Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala at his chamber.

A massive explosion occurred at a fireworks unit in Mundathikode, Thrissur, on April 21, 2026, while fireworks materials were being prepared for the Thiruvambady faction ahead of Thrissur Pooram. Sixteen people were killed and 40 injured in the tragedy.

The commission found that explosives in quantities far exceeding the permitted limit had been stored at the unit. While permission had been granted to store only 15 kg of explosive materials, those who had undertaken the fireworks contract had stocked around 7,000 kg at the site.

The report also identified the extensive use of potassium chlorate, a banned explosive substance, in the manufacture of fireworks as the cause of the explosion.

According to the commission, friction between chemicals amid high temperatures triggered the fire, which eventually led to the massive explosion.

World.title: NDA dominates GVMC polls, wins majority wards
World.content:
The NDA has registered a landslide victory in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, securing victory in 81% of the total wards and delivering a decisive mandate in its favour across the city.

Of the 120 wards, the NDA has emerged victorious in 98, with the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) winning 64 wards. The Jana Sena Party (JSP) has won 26 wards, while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won eight wards, taking the alliance’s combined tally to 98. In contrast, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) managed to win 13 wards, a significant setback for the party. Independent candidates also made their presence felt by winning eight wards, while the CPI(M) secured one ward.

According to sources, the NDA win in 98 wards reflected across the city’s East, West, North and South zones, as well as in Bheemunipatnam and Gajuwaka, which have traditionally been considered strongholds of the TDP.

NDA-backed candidates emerged victorious in a majority of wards in these areas, consolidating the alliance’s position across the municipal corporation.

Many sitting corporators as well as first-time candidates backed by the NDA registered convincing victories, with many securing substantial margins over their opponents.

Significantly, the NDA made considerable gains in several wards in the South Zone, where political observers and local leaders had anticipated a stronger showing by the YSRCP.

The CPI(M) secured one victory. In Ward 105 of the Aganampudi zone, CPI(M) candidate M. Krishnaiah defeated his TDP rival K. Vijay Kumar. This was the only victory for the Left parties among the officially declared results.

The election results also threw up victories for several Independent candidates and party rebels. TDP rebel candidate Kaki Govinda Reddy, who contested from Ward 86, defeated the YSRCP candidate by a margin of more than 200 votes, while the NDA-backed JSP candidate failed to make a significant impact.

Independent candidates Pampana Rajyalakshmi from Ward 41 and Battina Naveen from Ward 39 were among those who emerged victorious, defeating candidates backed by major political parties.

World.title: Poland plunges into crisis over fight for control of constitutional tribunal
World.content:
Shortly after 6 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026), Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal announced that the Tribunal’s president, Bogdan Święczkowski and vice-president, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been suspended for a month. The order was signed by judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of five Sejm(lower house of the Parliament)-elected judges whose oaths President Karol Nawrocki has refused to accept. Police cordoned off the Tribunal building as a mass of protesters tried to force their way through, and Mr. Nawrocki turned his Senegal-bound plane back to Warsaw. Just before 1 a.m., he walked into the Tribunal and addressed the present members of the judicial body, “You are not Constitutional Tribunal judges”. A decade-long legal dispute had moved into the building itself.

The Tribunal has 15 judges, each elected by the Sejm for nine years. It can strike down laws and review bills the President sends for referral to it before his decision to sign or veto.

World.title: Iran president says return to war benefits 'no one', after reported U.S. strikes
World.content:
Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that a return to war would benefit "no one", hours after reported U.S. strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.

It came as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump's grip on power.

Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", while deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran retained the right to "legitimate self-defence" after the strikes.

But Mr. Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue", adding that "no one will benefit from this war" if it reignited, and emphasising that the country's supreme leader had recently granted the government new powers to negotiate issues previously "off-limits".

The U.S. strikes, reported by The Wall Street Journal, CNN, The New York Times and other outlets, hit Qeshm island in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets.

Unnamed U.S. officials cited by the outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes.

U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.

'Iran wants a settlement'

The U.S. and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months.

Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokesperson told AFP, "No".

The reported Qeshm attack came just hours after Mr. Trump signalled a deal with Iran "could happen", as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought.

"Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible," Mr. Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.

Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies.

Mr. Ghalibaf said the ball was in Washington's court.

"The countries of the region should know that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran stands ready for battle with its finger on the trigger, it has also given the American side a powerful and rational response," he said in a televised speech. "The ball is now in America's court to prevent war."

'Committed'

Qatar, a mediator in protracted indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal in the war.

"Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them," Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters.

Both sides "are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented," he added.

"We remain hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal to take place," he said, adding Doha was working "towards an interim deal".

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Monday (November 2) confirmed indirect negotiations were taking place.

"Given the sensitivity and gravity of the current situation, consultations and deliberations are very intensive," Araghchi told state media.

Reopen the strait

U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance said both he and Mr. Trump were optimistic about securing an agreement.

"We've certainly made some progress. We'll see if we can make some more," Mr. Vance told reporters on Monday (November 2).

A senior Iranian official said that Tehran was ready to reopen Hormuz, a key route for global oil and gas supplies, within two days but only if Washington agreed to its long-standing list of demands.

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen the strait, with demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," Tehran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.

Billboard in Tehran

In the lead-up to Tuesday's (November 3) vote, Mr. Trump kept up his threats against Tehran, saying on Sunday (November 1) that the United States may have to give Iran "the hammer" at some unspecified time.

On Saturday (October 31), the U.S. leader said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if the U.S. resumes the war.

Authorities in Tehran installed a huge billboard in the heart of the capital, AFP journalists said on Tuesday (November 3).

Over a photo of the U.S. president, it reads: "We will kill Trump".

World.title: Southern India has grown wetter over seven decades, finds IMD study
World.content:
Southern India has become wetter over the past seven decades, as the area classified as having a hot semi-arid climate has nearly halved from about 30% to 16% of the peninsula between 1951-1980 and 1991-2020, according to a study by scientists from the India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune.

Published in MAUSAM, the IMD’s peer-reviewed journal, the study found that much of the peninsula’s hot semi-arid regions had transitioned into the tropical savannah climate zone, which receives more rainfall and has a prolonged dry season.

This zone now covers nearly three-fourths of peninsular India, compared with about three-fifths in the 1950s. The study, titled ‘Identifying the climate zones shifts of Indian meteorological subdivisions: insights from historical records’, uses the Köppen-Geiger climate classification system to assess changes across India’s meteorological subdivisions.

North-west India gets drier, hotter

The researchers mapped India’s climate zones across successive 30-year periods, using the IMD’s rainfall and temperature observations from 1951 to 2020. They found that most of the shift in southern India had occurred during the two most recent periods, 1981-2010 and 1991-2020, primarily because of an increase in rainfall.

The trend in southern India contrasts with that in north-west India, where the hot semi-arid zone has expanded from western to eastern Uttar Pradesh amid declining rainfall. Day- and night-time temperatures, meanwhile, have increased across the country.

Farm impact

The researchers said changes in climate zones could have implications for agriculture, particularly in determining suitable crops and sowing periods. They stressed the need to monitor these shifts and incorporate them into long-term agricultural planning.

This year, the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai declared the onset of the northeast monsoon on October 15, 2026, five days ahead of its normal date. The IMD has forecast a normal northeast monsoon for Tamil Nadu, against the seasonal average of 44 cm. While the Cauvery delta and southern districts are likely to receive normal to above-normal rainfall, the north interior districts are expected to receive below-normal rainfall.

Tamil Nadu ended the June-September southwest monsoon with a 20% rainfall deficit. The country as a whole recorded a 12.6% deficit during the season, as El Niño conditions contributed to the weakening of the southwest monsoon.

Ananya Karmakar of IMD Pune, the lead author of the study, said the long-term increase in rainfall over the peninsula was an important factor to consider in water and agricultural planning in Tamil Nadu, given the State’s dependence on the northeast monsoon.

Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD’s Director-General of Meteorology and a co-author of the study, said the department’s seasonal forecasts and advisories to farmers took into account both long-term climate trends and seasonal variations.

World.title: AIDWA-led women protesters in Mumbai seek disbursal of pending assistance
World.content:
Women from different parts of Maharashtra gathered in Mumbai on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to protest against the stalled instalments of the Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana. They sought immediate disbursal of pending instalments under the scheme. They also demanded streamlining of the e-KYC process at the earliest. “Why have you arbitrarily stopped our instalments? When the elections were there, you gave us the money. Now that there is no election, you have suddenly stopped the funds. How was our e-KYC done earlier? Why is the portal shut now? Why are there no answers? You had promised us ₹2,100 when you were running for elections. Now, you have stopped even the ₹1,500,” said Vaishali Chorge from Chandiwali.

Also read | Pre-poll promises, post-poll precarity

She was among the several women who participated in a protest led by the All India Democratic Women’s Association (AIDWA) in Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

CPI(M) leader and AIDWA’s founding member Brinda Karat told The Hindu, “It is about the principle of accountability. In our democracy, when you make a promise, what happens when you don’t remain answerable? You take the vote. And then, who is accountable? You have betrayed these women whom you had promised ₹2,100 a month. This is not a freebie. Women’s work in India is identified as the social community, gender which does the most work.”

Meena Janjal from Akola said several women in her region were landless labourers. “These illiterate women did not know about KYC. So their money stopped some time ago. But even those women who had done their e-KYC have been facing issues this year. They have not received their instalment since February 2026,” she said.

High cost of living

Several women said the cost of living had gone up with the prices of fuel, food, vegetables, daily items of living shooting up. “At such a time, this money gave us some relief. It helped us buy medicines for the family or books for the children,” said Afsana Hazrat Ali Sheikh.

Priya Ambure used to get her instalments regularly till a year ago. “I work as a house help in Mumbai. My husband earns too. We are not rich. The prices of everything we need each month have gone up. May it be wheat, sugar or rice. We live on rent. Increase the instalment from ₹1,500 to ₹2,100. Because that is what you had promised to us before elections. And start the disbursal again,” she said.

Delegation meets officials

A delegation of AIDWA leaders led by Mariam Dhawale met Maharashtra government officials and Minister Chhagan Bhujbal with the demands. “We were asked to submit the applications of all those women whose e-KYC has been completed. Once these applications are given at the tehsil level, their instalments will be released, the government has told us. We have also been told to give the details of ration shops which have not been providing allocated ration to the families below poverty line. The government has said it will cancel the licence of such shops. The arrears of the honorarium for the mid day meal workers will also be cleared in two days, we have been promised,” Prachi Hatiwlekar, State General Secretary of the AIDWA, told The Hindu.

World.title: Three arrested for abusing woman, smashing her car in Koramangala over road rage
World.content:
Three men who allegedly abused a woman motorist, hurled a stone at her car, smashed the car’s windows and damaged the vehicle with helmets following a road-rage incident have been arrested by the Koramangala police.

The incident occurred around 11.10 a.m. on October 28, when the woman was driving along the Ring Road near the BDA Complex in Koramangala’s 3rd Block. According to her complaint, three men riding a white scooter allegedly hit the right side of her car and subsequently moved alongside the vehicle to pick a quarrel with her.

When she asked them to drive carefully, the accused allegedly abused her using obscene and derogatory language, including sexually coloured remarks targeting her and her mother.

When the woman objected, the men allegedly attempted to break the left-side window of her car. After failing to do so, one of them picked up a large stone lying on the roadside and hurled it at the vehicle. They then removed their helmets and repeatedly struck the car, damaging its left side and breaking the rear-view mirror.

When the woman got down to question them, one of the accused allegedly attempted to assault her. The trio subsequently fled the scene. The entire incident was recorded on a mobile phone by one of the passersby and was uploaded to social media.

On Tuesday, the police traced and arrested all three accused identified as Shivakumar, 20, Ismail Zabiullah, 25, and Prashanth Pennaswamy, 27. The trio are working odd jobs.

World.title: Pakistan successfully tests its first indigenously developed air-to-air missile Fa’az: ISPR
World.content:
Pakistan on Tuesday performed a successful flight test of the country’s first indigenously developed air-to-air missile, Fa’az, “marking another significant milestone in the advancement of national aerospace and defence capabilities”, the military’s media wing said.

According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and can engage enemy targets at longer ranges.

“Fa’az will significantly enhance [the] operational flexibility of [the] Pakistan Air Force, further strengthening the country’s overall defence posture. The successful flight test underscores the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry,” the statement added.

The launch was witnessed by senior military officers, scientists and engineers involved in the development of the system, the ISPR said.

It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and the service chiefs congratulated the scientists.

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi issued a statement congratulating the nation on the test.

“Our scientists and engineers have once again achieved a remarkable feat that makes the nation proud,” the ministry quoted him as saying. “The successful test of the indigenously developed Fa’az missile marks a significant advancement in the field of defence.”

We are all proud of Pakistan’s distinguished scientists and engineers.”

Pakistan successfully tested two surface-to-surface missiles last month; the Fatah-2 extended range (ER) hypersonic ballistic missile was tested on Oct 13, and the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile was tested a week before that.

ISPR said that the Fatah-2 ER is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

“It is capable of engaging targets with high precision and defeating [the] enemy’s missile defence systems due to its unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features,” it added.

For Fatah-IV ER, ISPR said: “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.”

It noted that the test “also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability”.

More to follow

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs5.45 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs3.68
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.68.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs369.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs391.52.

The prices are applicable for Nov 4 (Wednesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference today, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

He also hinted at the latest reduction in fuel prices, saying “even better news will come before us”.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: 'We made a deal months ago': Trump says US will stop $4 billion funding to Israel at end of 2026
World.content:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he made a deal with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Washington would stop $4 billion in funding to Israel after the end of this year.

Speaking to Fox News’ ‘Fox and Friends’, Trump said Israel no longer needed the funding and that some Democrats and left-wing politicians were using the US financial support to Israel as a talking point to criticise Republicans.

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump told the broadcaster.

“We’ve already agreed that by the end of this year we won’t be paying Israel. Now we’ll help Israel if they need it.”

There was no immediate comment from Netanyahu’s office on Trump’s remarks.

It was not immediately clear which exact funding Trump meant.

A memorandum of understanding that provides $3.8bn in annual US military aid to Israel is approaching its expiration date in 2028, and conversations have been under way on how Washington’s assistance to Israel would evolve beyond that date.

“They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world,” Trump added.

Netanyahu said in a May interview with CBS that he hoped to wean Israel off US military support within a decade. In a June letter to a US congressman, he wrote that the time had come for Israel “to move from aid recipient to partner”.

US public support for Israel has fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats.

A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48 per cent of voters and 66pc of Democrats believe the United States is too supportive of Israel, up from 16pc and 20pc when the question was first asked in 2017.

Support for Israel among Democratic voters has plummeted, candidates critical of Israel are winning Democratic primaries, and even moderate lawmakers are increasingly willing to challenge decades of US support for Israel.

“The left uses the $4bn payment that everybody knows about — well, it’s no secret — as a signal of unfairness, and we can’t allow that to happen,” Trump said.

“We were giving them $4bn, we are, but it gets cut off at the end of the year. Why? Because they don’t need it.”

World.title: Soldier martyred, 17 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operations in Balochistan: ISPR
World.content:
A soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, the military’s media affairs wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces conducted the IBOs on Nov 1 on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy Fitna al Hindustan”.

The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

The statement said the first IBO was conducted in the Sanni area of Kachhi district. During the operation, “terrorists’ attempt to establish [a] road block in the city was thwarted by proactive action of security forces,“ resulting in the killing of 10 terrorists.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered,” it added.

Separately, security forces busted a terrorist hideout in Kharan and after an intense fire exchange, “seven Indian-sponsored khawarij were sent to hell”.

ISPR said that weapons and ammunition were also recovered during this operation. The statement added that Sepoy Hikmatullah, who was 25 years old and a resident of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district, was martyred during the IBO.

“Sanitisation operations are being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorist found in the area,” it added.

ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the “menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”.

In a statement, President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for killing 17 terrorists and also paid tribute to Sepoy Hikmatullah.

“[His] sacrifice for the defence of the homeland and for peace and security will always be remembered,” the president said, extending “heartfelt” condolences and sympathy to the bereaved family.

“Operations under Azm-i-Istehkam will continue until the complete eradication of terrorism sponsored and supported from abroad,” President Zardari added.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the security forces on the successful operations. In a post on X, the interior ministry said he also commended the professional capabilities of security forces in “thwarting the terrorists’ nefarious designs”.

He also paid tribute to the martyred soldier, saying that the “brave sons of the security forces are a source of pride for the nation”.

“The security forces remain committed to the complete eradication of Indian-sponsored terrorists,” he said.

World.title: CM Maryam incensed at Chaudhry Salik's claims of corruption in Punjab, sends him Rs5bn defamation notice
World.content:
LAHORE: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks.

During a private television channel talk show on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi.

However, he also took a swipe at the present provincial administration, alleging that political considerations were increasingly shaping development priorities and influencing the allocation of public funds. He said he regularly heard complaints of corruption in Punjab, alleging that a disproportionate share of the province’s development budget was being channelled towards Lahore.

Addressing a ceremony in Attock on Tuesday, CM Maryam said: “There is a federal minister … somebody sent me his statement about corruption in Punjab. Today, I am sending him a defamation notice.”

She said that she would not hear “false allegations of corruption”.

“If you have evidence, bring it forth — otherwise I will drag you to court,” she said. She also asked him why he remained a minister in a government that he considered corrupt.

The chief minister went on to say that the reason behind the anger of the PML-Q leader was neither a matter of corruption nor progress. The issue, she said, was that she changed the deputy commissioner (DC) of Gujrat a few days ago whereas Salik had wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed.

“I will not allow anyone to interfere in the will of the people,” she said.

Maryam also took exception to Salik’s comments calling Elahi the “best-ever chief minister” in Punjab.

“The Gujrat that Pervez Elahi handed me — I went there about two years ago and it was raining. Believe me … the water was up to here,” she said, gesturing to her neck.

“My Land Cruiser was completely submerged,” she said.

“It looked less like Gujrat and more like a village … now, go and look at Gujrat. Now, when it rains, the rainwater doesn’t accumulate. That work was not done by the Chaudhrys,” she said.

Subsequently, the PML-N posted on X that a defamation notice had been sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman, Muhammad Iqbal.

The notice said that the office of chief minister carried “substantial” public responsibility and required “the highest degree of integrity, credibility and public confidence”, which made any allegations of dishonesty or corruption — disseminated to “millions of viewers” via electronic or digital media — a serious matter.

It said that during the interview, Butt had “introduced and led the discussion” regarding alleged corruption in Punjab, while Salik “proceeded to make sweeping and baseless allegations against the provincial administration”.

“The manner in which the subject was introduced and pursued was not a neutral request for clarification of any identified incident, investigation or documented complaint,” the notice said.

“Rather, it provided a platform for the propagation of serious allegations without first identifying any verifiable material or establishing their factual foundation,” it added.

The notice said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province.

“The most alarming aspect of the aforesaid statements is the express admission that he possesses no evidence to substantiate the allegations,” it added.

It stated that the chief minister considered the conduct of all three individuals named in the notice “serious and unacceptable”: Salik for his “false statements”, Butt for his editorial conduct and Muhammad Iqbal for facilitating and broadcasting the allegations.

The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question.

It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages. The notice gave a period of seven days for these actions and warned that failure to comply would lead to legal proceedings.

‘I responded honestly’

Speaking to the media in the wake of CM Maryam’s comments, Salik said he was sticking to his statement. In remarks aired by Geo News, he said: “God save us from pride and arrogance”.

Asked about providing evidence for the corruption allegations, he said: “Please go and listen to the interview again.”

He also refuted the claim that the row had to do with distracting from the matter of new provinces.

“It was an interview, someone asked a question and I responded honestly,” he said.

“Yes, there definitely is [corruption],” he added.

Responding to the remarks, CM Maryam said: “So, levelling false accusations is considered humility, while offering a response is deemed arrogance? Bravo!”

During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending, particularly the use of official aircraft, arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

His comments had also prompted a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised the PML-Q leader not to “bite the hand that feeds him”.

Bokhari had also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request for appointment of a DC of his choice being turned down.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote.

While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

World.title: Imran's nephew denied jail meeting this time; PTI open to possible alliance with JUI-F
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was again denied a meeting with his family and lawyers on Tuesday – a prescribed day by the Islamabad High Court for meetings at the Adiala jail.

The denial comes just a day after Imran’s lawyer, Barrister Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet him and his incarcerated wife Bushra Bibi for consultations on a legal case.

The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives , Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months.

Speaking to Dawn on Tuesday, Advocate Awais Younas Chaudhry said a son of Imran’s sister Uzma Khanum, Abdullah Khan, reached Adiala jail as a family member to meet the PTI founder.

However, authorities did not grant him permission, said Chaudhry, who had submitted a list of lawyers and party leaders to the Adiala jail administration for meetings with Imran.

Chaudhry, whose name was also included in the list, said that lawyers, including PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, also reached the prison, but were not allowed to meet the ex-premier.

Imran’s sisters — Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan — used to stage frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release.

However, the three sisters have remained detained since late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

Potential JUI-F support

Meanwhile, PTI has hinted that it can get support from Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in the struggle against the government.

Speaking to the media, the PTI secretary general remarked that no one was terming Fazl a “saviour”, but the PTI would welcome everyone who would stand by the party and struggle against the incumbent government.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” Raja said.

“We do not depend on anyone, and we do not have expectations from anyone,” Raja stated. However, he emphasised that the party wanted its caravan to grow, hinting towards a possible PTI–JUI-F alliance if Fazl offers to join.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Since mid-October, the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Gohar refutes rumour that Imran ‘happy’ about KP governor’s rule

Separately, the PTI chairman dismissed the notion that Imran himself wanted his party’s government in KP to be sacked and was happy with the imposition of governor’s rule.

“It is not correct,” Barrister Gohar said.

Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar informed him, after his meeting with Imran, that the jailed ex-premier was already aware of the measures and he did not say that it was a positive step as they did not talk much about politics.

The federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder.

Replying to a question, Gohar claimed that Barrister Safdar did not bring any political message from jail. Nevertheless, the PTI chairman welcomed Monday’s meeting with Imran as a positive development.

He hoped that the political tension would end, rejecting the reports of any forward bloc in PTI’s KP wing.

Last month, there were rumours of a group of KP MPAs endorsing Ali Amin Gandapur as the acting provincial president in the absence of Junaid Akbar.

However, PTI soon clarified that Akbar remained the party’s president for KP and named Senator Noorul Haq Qadri to take over his duties in his absence.

Similarly, after several PTI parliamentarians questioned the party’s decisions and overreliance on Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is non-functional during governor’s rule — PTI reaffirmed its support for him.

In its latest clarification a day ago, PTI insisted there was no “factionalism” or “division” within the party, and warned of action against any member who violates party discipline or policy.

World.title: Govt assures public of meeting winter gas demand, hints at 'good news' for fuel prices
World.content:
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik on Tuesday assured the public that the government will make utmost efforts to meet the demand for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) during the winter months.

His remarks come as LPG supply has been disrupted due to the closure of Iranian border crossings, resulting in gas cylinders being sold at twice the official rate in the open market. LPG is widely used for rickshaws, but also for cooking and other purposes by those not on the piped gas network.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, Malik said, “Seeing people’s distress and also knowing that from December and January, winter will be at its peak […] even if the most expensive fuel has to be purchased for the piped network, we will bring it in and try to meet demand through LNG (liquefied natural gas).”

The minister assured the public that the government will make “utmost efforts” to ensure piped supply of domestic gas for meal times. Besides this, LPG will be needed for other needs and by those without piped connections, he noted.

Speaking on fuel prices, Malik recalled the latest reduction and noted that the international market had closed lower on Tuesday.

“Even better news will come before us,” he said, regarding Tuesday’s revision of petrol and diesel prices.

Under a newly announced arrangement , oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion for 30 days, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

In his press briefing today, Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for LPG. He observed that the country was facing “numerous challenges” regarding the availability of LPG.

The minister added that some individuals were trying to exploit the situation after the supply “dried up on our western border”, with consumers being offered LPG at Rs700-800 per kilogramme.

Malik elaborated that the total demand for LPG was approximately 2.4 million tonnes, amounting to about 6,500 to 7,000 tonnes per day. Of this, the country locally produces roughly 2,000 to 2,500 tonnes, depending on which crude they use and how much LPG is produced with it, he added.

However, “nearly half or more than half” of the demand used to come through the western border, where “difficulties have arisen”, he said. The rest of the demand is fulfilled from two terminals — Engro and SSGC LPG — with a combined storage capacity of around 14,000 tonnes, the minister said.

Malik further said that efforts were under way to build the country’s energy security architecture from scratch, regretting that no work had so far been done on fuel storage or refineries.

“Before the war, nobody ever paid attention to how Pakistan needs to work on its infrastructure and energy security,” he observed.

Recalling that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif chaired a meeting earlier in the day on the matter, he added that the premier was personally spearheading efforts to “rebuild the entire system from scratch”.

“The war may certainly have caught us in its crossfire, but it meant we had to set our own house in order, right? We neither worked on storage, nor on refineries, nor on the LPG chain,” Malik remarked. The minister noted that the majority of the world had shifted from pressurised containers to refrigerated and cryogenic cargoes.

He lamented that small pressurised ships were not easily available, while Very Large Gas Carriers (VLGCs) could not dock either, just like Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs).

“Even if it comes, where do we store it?”

Responding to a query, Malik said, “Domestic [demand] comes first and after that, the space we have carved out is only done by restricting it to the three meal times.”

He said domestic demand was expected to surge by 400 to 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), so “we will do whatever curtailment we have to accordingly”.

The minister said PM Shehbaz had directed that the necessary alternative arrangements for RLNG be made as well for power, adding: “But for November, we are well covered for both requirements.”

In his remarks alongside Malik, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar emphasised that the prime minister prioritised the public’s interests and made “strong and bold” decisions, such as the fuel subsidy scheme.

Speaking about the LPG sector, he said, “The monopoly has been abolished, the quota system under which a few people engaged in profiteering has been abolished, discretion has been eliminated, the process has been made transparent [and] competition has been introduced.”

He noted that PM Shehbaz had directed Malik to draft a plan for LPG supply during the winter and ensure there was no load-shedding during meal times.

“Overall, if you look at it, even in the most difficult circumstances, PM Shehbaz has not abandoned the public. Reforms were carried out, structural reforms were introduced, the process was made transparent and the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) started publishing all the details on its website,” Tarar said.

‘To bring competition in sector’

Expanding upon the pricing mechanism, the petroleum minister said that, internationally, Saudi oil giant Aramco determined the LPG price through its contract price (CP), similar to how Platts determined the oil rate.

Malik added that the price was issued on a monthly basis, with Ogra notifying the rate. Therefore, “the government does not have much of a role in it”, he said.

He stressed the provision of LPG to the public at a “fair” price.

“It cannot be that if the price in the international market is Rs1,000, we can provide it locally for Rs500,” he said. The minister explained that Ogra notified the recent increase in the LPG price because Aramco had announced the CP price of $756 per tonne, compared to $540 per tonne in March.

Malik lamented that the gas sector was not properly formalised, remarking that the more formal a player was in the LPG market, the more troubled they were because they “could not compete against the informal sector”.

“So, the decision made for this is that competition be introduced into this sector, and through competition, efforts be made to import the cheapest possible fuel and its availability to the public at that price should be ensured, no matter what challenges arise.”

The minister noted that under the 2016 LPG policy, Ogra was to decide the price for locally produced LPG based on the CP, or the Free On Board (FOB) price, notified by Aramco. He said the situation had been fine since there were no import costs attached under this system.

However, as the demand for fuel grew — so much so that 70 per cent of the need was currently being met through imports — the FOB formula did not cover the import cost and people shifted towards the “grey channel” instead of importing.

“Therefore, it has now been decided that this sector will be opened up for competition,” he announced.

To correct collusion and cartelisation, the government has directed the state’s major companies — Pakistan State Oil Company, SSGC LPG, and Pakistan LNG Limited — to book bulk deals on government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) bases, Malik said.

“And they have made a lot of progress in that,” he added.

World.title: Americans vote in midterms set to upend Trump presidency
World.content:
Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections, with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and impose the first significant checks on Donald Trump’s chaotic second term in the White House.

Multiple polls predict Democrats will take control of the House of Representatives and have a shot at seizing the Senate on the back of voter resentment at a deeply unpopular president, soaring energy costs and the dragging conflict with Iran.

Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court justices and senior officials.

Voters cast their ballots inside a polling location in the social hall at St Patrick’s Church on November 3, 2026 in Youngstown, Ohio. — AFP

Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in an Atlanta suburb, told AFP he “voted for mostly Democratic candidates”.

“It’s just about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things,” Comer said. “It needs to change for the everyday person and I’m an everyday person.”

Trump defended his record in a final TV phone-in pitch to voters on Tuesday, saying he had rebuilt the country through his immigration crackdown, war on Iran and tariff policy.

“We have to keep America great. We’re great now. We were terrible two years ago,” Trump told “Fox & Friends”.

The election amounts to a nationwide judgment on Trump, with the mood turning sharply against Republicans amid anger over soaring living costs and the war on Iran.

All 435 House seats and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are at stake, along with governorships in 36 states. Democrats need only three House gains and a net four seats in the Senate to wrest both chambers from Republican hands.

Trump returned to office last year promising to bring down prices, but inflation, tariffs and fuel costs inflated by the Middle East conflict have squeezed Americans.

A person holds a sticker, during the US midterm elections, in Durham, North Carolina, US, November 3. — Reuters

The 80-year-old’s approval rating has hovered near the low 30s.

In the suburbs of Atlanta, Georgia, retired teacher Jane Callum, 77, was among Democrats canvassing for Senator Jon Ossoff, who framed the race as a watershed moment for the country’s future.

“I really feel an obligation to do everything that I possibly can to change the direction that our country is going in now, and put it more on the path to democracy and away from autocracy,” she told AFP.

Economic discontent

Republicans insist that Trump’s tax cuts and immigration crackdown will benefit Americans, and they are portraying Democratic candidates as left-wing radicals.

But in his final public campaign appearance Monday, Trump barely touched on the economy and spent most of the time in a rambling talk about his problem-plagued renovation of Washington’s Reflecting Pool.

Democratic US Senate candidate Chris Pappas speaks to members of the media after voting in the US midterm elections at Webster Elementary School in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, November 3. — Reuters

“This is the last day before the midterm elections, the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime,” he said, 26 minutes into the speech, before quickly returning to talking about renovations.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer branded it a “pathetic closing message.”

Some Republican supporters remain confident.

“We’re going to win. As a matter of fact, we’ve probably already won,” Texas military veteran Yvonne Clouser told AFP.

But while Republicans hold a 53-47 Senate majority, the battlefield is extending into conservative states like Kansas, Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Alaska.

Democrats must also defend competitive seats, including in Michigan, where a bitter internal dispute saw congresswoman Haley Stevens endorse Republican Mike Rogers rather than the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed.

Decision Desk HQ’s final forecast forecasted 241 House seats for Democrats against 194 for Republicans, and a narrower 52-48 Democratic Senate majority.

Disputed results?

More than 57 million Americans had already voted early before Tuesday, indicating high engagement.

A voter poses with their “I Voted” sticker after submitting their ballot at a polling place in the Marine on St Croix City Hall on November 3, 2026 in Marine on St Croix, Minnesota. — AFP

The campaign has attracted more than $11 billion in political advertising, while billionaire Trump ally Elon Musk has poured hundreds of millions of dollars into Republican political efforts.

As soon as polls close, concerns will mount over whether results will be accepted by the Republicans.

Trump, who tried to overturn his 2020 election defeat, has repeatedly alleged widespread voter fraud and accused Democrats — with no evidence — of cheating.

The Justice Department, run by a close Trump ally, has already sued to potentially block certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses, although a court ruled against the effort on the eve of the election.

And the Supreme Court rejected on Monday an emergency bid to force California to set aside the mail-in ballots of more than 20,000 people on the grounds they may not be American citizens.

Trump, who will watch the midterms results at the White House on Tuesday night, signalled that if he does lose control of Congress he could simply defy Democrats.

“I veto everything,” he told a podcast on Monday, although he said he might strike deals with Democrats eventually.

Justice Department to monitor elections in all 50 states

The US Justice Department announced that it was deploying approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers across all 50 states for the first time in its history.

The move comes amid Trump’s repeated claims of election fraud and concerns raised by his administration about non-citizens voting and the integrity of the electoral process.

The department described the deployment as “the largest election-monitoring effort in its history”, saying it was intended to “protect voting rights, ensure election integrity and promote transparency”.

Trump has repeatedly questioned the integrity of American elections, challenging his 2020 defeat and claiming that non-citizens pose a threat to the fairness of the voting system. His administration has stepped up efforts to investigate suspected non-citizen voting, although research and election officials indicate that such cases are exceedingly rare.

The expanded monitoring effort has also raised questions about the federal government’s role in elections, which are primarily administered by state and local authorities. The Justice Department is part of the executive branch headed by Trump, unlike the courts, which exercise an independent judicial function.

The department said the monitoring programme, coordinated by its Civil Rights Division, would focus on ensuring compliance with federal voting rights laws.

“The DOJ has sent election monitors in support of this mission since the enactment of the Voting Rights Act in 1965 across all administrations,” it said in a statement.

“Today, the DOJ will further this mission by engaging in its largest monitoring effort in history — with approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers deployed, and, for the first time, in all 50 states.”

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon, who heads the Civil Rights Division, described election integrity as a top priority for the administration.

“Election integrity has been one of the top priorities for this Administration and this Division,” Dhillon said. “I am very proud we are deploying the largest monitoring effort in DOJ history, and pursuing transparency for elections in an assertive and nondiscriminatory manner.”

The monitors will check compliance with federal laws protecting voting rights, including the Voting Rights Act. Their responsibilities will also include overseeing protections for voters with disabilities and enforcing laws prohibiting voter intimidation and suppression based on race, colour, national origin or religion.

The department said its personnel would remain in contact with state and local election officials throughout Election Day.

It also urged voters who encounter violence, threats or intimidation at polling places to contact local police immediately by calling 911. Suspected violations of federal voting rights laws can also be reported to the Civil Rights Division.

The unprecedented deployment comes amid a broader national debate over election security, the limits of federal authority and public confidence in the American electoral process.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.
